entries.name: Anion gap
entries.purpose: Metabolic acidosis workup
entries.formula_human: AG = Na - (Cl + HCO3); albumin-corrected AG = AG + 2.5*(4 - albumin)

entries.name: Corrected QT
entries.purpose: (see cardiovascular)

entries.name: Corrected calcium
entries.purpose: Hyper/hypocalcemia assessment
entries.formula_human: CorrCa = measured Ca + 0.8*(4 - albumin)

entries.name: Delta ratio
entries.purpose: High-AG acidosis with additional disorder
entries.formula_human: Delta ratio = (AG - 12)/(24 - HCO3); <0.4 normal AG acidosis added, 0.4-0.8 mixed, >2 concomitant metabolic alkalosis

entries.name: MAP
entries.purpose: Perfusion pressure
entries.formula_human: MAP = DBP + (SBP - DBP)/3

entries.name: Osmolal gap
entries.purpose: Toxic alcohol ingestion
entries.formula_human: OG = measured Osm - calculated (2*Na + glucose/18 + BUN/2.8 [+ EtOH/4.6]); >10-15 abnormal

entries.name: Winter's formula
entries.purpose: Expected compensation in metabolic acidosis
entries.formula_human: Expected PaCO2 = 1.5*HCO3 + 8 +/- 2

entries.name: Lund-Browder chart
entries.purpose: TBSA estimation (children)
entries.formula_human: Age-specific body-region percentages

entries.name: Parkland formula
entries.purpose: Estimates crystalloid fluid requirements in the first 24 hours after major burn injury. Guides initial fluid management to prevent burn shock.
entries.formula_human:
Total fluid in first 24 hours = 4 mL × body weight (kg) × %TBSA burned

Timing:
- First 8 hours (from time of injury, not from presentation): give 50% of total
- Next 16 hours: give remaining 50%

Fluid type: Lactated Ringer's (preferred) or normal saline

Example: 70 kg, 40% TBSA → 4 × 70 × 40 = 11,200 mL total → 5,600 mL in first 8 hrs, 5,600 mL in next 16 hrs

Note: This is an ESTIMATE — must be titrated to urine output (target 0.5–1 mL/kg/hr in adults, 1–2 mL/kg/hr in children)

inputs.label: Body weight
inputs.description: Patient's weight in kilograms (pre-burn weight if possible)

inputs.label: %TBSA burned
inputs.description: Percentage total body surface area of 2nd and 3rd degree burns (Rule of 9s or Lund-Browder)

bands.meaning: Total 24-hour fluid requirement — 50% in first 8 hours, 50% in next 16 hours (from time of injury)
Adults: 0.5–1.0 mL/kg/hr. Children: 1.0–2.0 mL/kg/hr. Adjust fluid rate to maintain UOP.
UOP <0.5 mL/kg/hr despite calculated fluids — increase rate. Consider escharotomy if circumferential burns.
UOP >1.0 mL/kg/hr — may need to slow fluids. Complications of over-resuscitation: compartment syndrome, ARDS, abdominal compartment syndrome.

citations.text: Baxter CR, Shires T. Physiological response to crystalloid resuscitation of severe burns. Ann N Y Acad Sci. 1968;150(3):874-894. PMID: 5246049

entries.limitations: Overestimates fluid requirements in many patients (up to 50% of patients develop fluid overload). Formula is a starting point — must be titrated to urine output. Doesn't account for inhalation injury (increases fluid requirements 30-50%). Doesn't account for delay in resuscitation, electrical burns (greater internal injury), or patient comorbidities (CHF, CKD). Lactated Ringer's preferred — NS may cause hyperchloremic acidosis. Colloid controversial in first 24 hours (some guidelines add albumin after 12-18 hours). Modified Brooke formula (2 mL × kg × %TBSA) is alternative with similar outcomes. Burn depth estimation affects %TBSA calculation accuracy. Children require different UOP targets and maintenance fluids in addition to resuscitation fluids.

entries.name: Rule of nines
entries.purpose: TBSA estimation adults
entries.formula_human: Head 9, each arm 9, chest 18, back 18, each leg 18, perineum 1 (adult)

entries.name: TBSA by palmar surface
entries.purpose: Rapid TBSA estimate
entries.formula_human: Patient palm (with fingers) = 1% TBSA

entries.name: ASCVD Pooled Cohort Equations
entries.purpose: 10-yr atherosclerotic CVD risk (US guideline)
entries.formula_human: 1-S0^exp(sum(beta_i*X_i - sum_mean)); age, sex, race, TC, HDL, SBP (+/- Rx), DM, smoking; coefficients in Goff et al 2013

entries.name: CCS class
entries.purpose: Angina severity
entries.formula_human: I-IV by exertional threshold

entries.name: CHA2DS2-VASc
entries.purpose: Estimates annual stroke risk in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation to guide anticoagulation decisions.
entries.formula_human: CHA₂DS₂-VASc = CHF(1) + Hypertension(1) + Age_≥75(2) + Diabetes(1) + Stroke/TIA/VTE(2) + Vascular_disease(1) + Age_65-74(1) + Female_sex(1)

inputs.label: Congestive heart failure (or LVEF ≤40%)
inputs.description: Clinical HF or reduced ejection fraction

inputs.label: Hypertension
inputs.description: History of hypertension or BP >140/90 on treatment

inputs.label: Diabetes mellitus
inputs.description: History of DM or fasting glucose >126 mg/dL or HbA1c ≥6.5%

inputs.label: Stroke/TIA/thromboembolism
inputs.description: Prior history of ischemic stroke, TIA, or systemic thromboembolism

inputs.label: Vascular disease
inputs.description: Prior MI, PAD, or aortic plaque

bands.meaning: Low risk. Anticoagulation generally not recommended. Annual stroke risk ~0% (male) / ~0.6% (female).
Low-moderate risk. Consider anticoagulation based on individual factors. Annual stroke risk ~1.3%.

Moderate-high risk. Oral anticoagulation recommended (DOAC preferred over warfarin). Annual stroke risk escalates: 2.2% (score 2), 3.2% (3), 4.0% (4), 6.7% (5), 9.8% (6), 9.6% (7), 12.5% (8), 15.2% (9).

citations.text: Lip GYH, Nieuwlaat R, Pisters R, et al. Refining clinical risk stratification for predicting stroke and thromboembolism in atrial fibrillation using a novel risk factor-based approach: the Euro Heart Survey on Atrial Fibrillation. Chest. 2010;137(2):263-272. PMID: 19762550

entries.limitations: Low c-statistic (~0.6) for predicting stroke — discriminative ability is modest. Score of 1 in males vs. 1 solely from female sex have very different risk profiles. Does not account for AF burden (paroxysmal vs persistent). Most beneficial for identifying truly low-risk patients who can safely avoid anticoagulation.

entries.name: EuroSCORE II
entries.purpose: Predicts in-hospital mortality after cardiac surgery (CABG, valve, or combined procedures).
entries.formula_human: Logistic model: Predicted mortality = e^(β₀ + Σβᵢxᵢ) / (1 + e^(β₀ + Σβᵢxᵢ)). β₀ = −5.324537. All individual β coefficients for 18 variables are published in Nashef SAM, et al. 2012, supplementary tables. Use the online EuroSCORE II calculator for precise computation (euroscore.org).

inputs.label: Procedure type
inputs.options_text: isolated CABG / isolated non-CABG / 2 procedures / 3+ procedures

inputs.label: Renal dysfunction (Cr or dialysis)
inputs.description: Creatinine clearance category or on dialysis

bands.meaning: Low operative risk
Moderate risk
High risk
Very high risk

citations.text: Nashef SAM, Roques F, Sharples LD, et al. EuroSCORE II. Eur J Cardiothorac Surg. 2012;41(4):734-744. PMID: 22378855

entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app — calculator at euroscore.org
entries.limitations: Multiple variables require nuanced clinical judgment (e.g., 'poor mobility'). May overestimate risk in some contemporary cohorts with improved outcomes. Does not capture frailty, porcelain aorta, or liver disease. Designed for in-hospital mortality, not long-term outcomes. Less validated for TAVR or minimally invasive procedures.

entries.name: Framingham Risk Score
entries.purpose: 10-yr CHD/CVD risk
entries.formula_human: Cox equation: S0(t)^exp(sum(beta_i*X_i - mean_i)); sex-specific coefficients for age, TC, HDL, SBP(+/-Rx), smoking, DM

entries.name: GRACE
entries.purpose: Estimates in-hospital and 6-month mortality in patients presenting with the full spectrum of ACS (UA, NSTEMI, and STEMI).
entries.formula_human: GRACE = Age_points + HR_points + SBP_points + Creatinine_points + Killip_points + Cardiac_arrest(39 if yes) + ST_deviation(28 if yes) + Elevated_biomarkers(14 if yes). Non-linear point assignments for continuous variables are derived from the published nomogram/lookup tables; the GRACE 2.0 web calculator uses polynomial regression: Risk = 1/(1 + e^(-(β₀ + β₁×age + β₂×HR + β₃×SBP + β₄×Cr + β₅×Killip + β₆×arrest + β₇×STdev + β₈×troponin))) with published coefficients. Verify exact polynomial coefficients from the GRACE 2.0 publication.

inputs.label: Age
inputs.description: Age in years, with non-linear point assignment from nomogram

inputs.label: Heart rate
inputs.description: Heart rate at presentation (bpm), non-linear point assignment

inputs.label: Systolic blood pressure
inputs.description: SBP at presentation (mmHg), non-linear point assignment

inputs.label: Serum creatinine
inputs.description: Creatinine at presentation (mg/dL), non-linear point assignment

inputs.label: Killip class
inputs.description: Clinical heart failure classification at presentation
inputs.options_text: I = no HF; II = rales/JVD/ S3; III = pulmonary edema; IV = cardiogenic shock

bands.meaning: Low risk: in-hospital mortality <1%; 6-month mortality <3%
Intermediate risk: in-hospital mortality 1–3%; 6-month mortality 3–8%
High risk: in-hospital mortality >3%; 6-month mortality >8%

citations.text: Granger CB, Goldberg RJ, Dabbous O, et al. Predictors of hospital mortality in the Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events. Arch Intern Med. 2003;163(19):2345-2353. PMID: 14581255

entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app
entries.limitations: Non-linear point assignment requires lookup tables or web calculator (not easily computed at bedside). Requires serum creatinine. Less validated in specific subgroups (very elderly, CKD, racial/ethnic minorities in some studies). GRACE 2.0 preferred for use with calculator apps.

entries.name: HAS-BLED
entries.purpose: Estimates 1-year risk of major bleeding in patients with atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation, to balance against stroke risk.
entries.formula_human: HAS-BLED = Hypertension(1) + Abnormal_renal(1) + Abnormal_liver(1) + Stroke(1) + Bleeding(1) + Labile_INR(1) + Elderly(1) + Drugs(1) + Alcohol(1)

inputs.label: Abnormal renal function
inputs.description: Dialysis, transplant, or serum creatinine >200 µmol/L (>2.26 mg/dL)

inputs.label: Abnormal liver function
inputs.description: Cirrhosis or bilirubin >2× ULN or AST/ALT/ALP >3× ULN

inputs.label: Bleeding history or predisposition
inputs.description: Prior major bleeding or predisposition (e.g., anemia)

inputs.label: Labile INRs
inputs.description: Unstable/high INR or poor time in therapeutic range (<60%)

bands.meaning: Low bleeding risk (~1.0–1.9% annual major bleeding)
High bleeding risk (~3.7–12.5% annual major bleeding). High score should prompt review of modifiable risk factors, not necessarily contraindicate anticoagulation.

citations.text: Pisters R, Lane DA, Nieuwlaat R, et al. A novel user-friendly score (HAS-BLED) to assess 1-year risk of major bleeding in patients with atrial fibrillation: the Euro Heart Survey. Chest. 2010;138(5):1093-1100. PMID: 20299623

entries.limitations: Score ≥3 identifies high bleeding risk but should not be used alone to withhold anticoagulation (many high-CHA₂DS₂-VASc patients with HAS-BLED ≥3 still benefit from OAC). Labile INR not applicable to DOAC users. Modest discriminative ability (c-statistic ~0.6–0.7). Some criteria are subjective (bleeding predisposition).

entries.name: HEART
entries.purpose: Risk stratifies emergency department patients with acute chest pain for 6-week major adverse cardiac events (MACE).
entries.formula_human: HEART = History + ECG + Age + Risk_factors + Troponin

inputs.label: History
inputs.description: Clinical suspicion based on history characteristics
inputs.options_text: 0 = slightly suspicious; 1 = moderately suspicious; 2 = highly suspicious

inputs.label: ECG
inputs.options_text: 0 = normal; 1 = nonspecific repolarization disturbance; 2 = significant ST deviation

inputs.label: Risk factors
inputs.description: Number of cardiovascular risk factors (hypertension, hyperlipidemia, DM, current/recent smoking, family history of premature CAD, obesity, sedentary lifestyle)
inputs.options_text: 0 = no risk factors; 1 = 1–2 risk factors; 2 = ≥3 risk factors or history of atherosclerotic disease

inputs.label: Troponin
inputs.description: Initial or serial troponin relative to local upper limit of normal (ULN)

bands.meaning: Low risk (~0.9–1.7% MACE at 6 weeks). Consider early discharge with outpatient follow-up.
Moderate risk (~12–16.6% MACE). Consider admission or observation with serial troponins and provocative testing.
High risk (~50–65% MACE). Early invasive strategy recommended.

citations.text: Backus BE, et al. A prospective validation of the HEART score for chest pain patients at the emergency department. Int J Cardiol. 2013;168(3):2153-2158. PMID: 23465248 (concept originally from Six AJ, et al. 2008)

entries.limitations: Subjective components (History scoring varies by clinician). Validated primarily in ED populations; less studied in prehospital or primary care. Troponin assay-specific (high-sensitivity troponin may shift optimal cutoffs). Original validation used conventional troponin.

entries.name: Killip class
entries.purpose: AMI severity
entries.formula_human: I no HF=0, II rales/S3=1, III pulmonary edema=2, IV cardiogenic shock=3

entries.name: NYHA class
entries.purpose: HF functional class
entries.formula_human: I no limitation=1, II slight limitation=2, III marked limitation=3, IV symptoms at rest=4

entries.name: QRISK3
entries.purpose: 10-yr CVD risk (UK)
entries.formula_human: Cox model: age, ethnicity, smoking, BMI, BP, lipids, DM, CKD, AF, migraine, steroids, SLE, erectile dysfunction, severe mental illness, atypical antipsychotics, systemic corticosteroids, family history, Townsend score

entries.name: QTc (Bazett/Fridericia/Hodges/Framingham)
entries.purpose: ECG QT correction
entries.formula_human: QTc = QT/sqrt(RR); QT/RR^(1/3); QT+1.75(HR-60); QT+0.154(1-RR)

entries.name: Revised Cardiac Risk Index (Lee)
entries.purpose: Risk prediction model for major cardiac complications (MI, cardiac arrest, pulmonary edema, complete heart block, ventricular fibrillation) in patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery. Guides preoperative cardiac evaluation, monitoring intensity, and perioperative beta-blocker decisions. Most widely validated perioperative cardiac risk score.
entries.formula_human:
RCRI = Sum of present risk factors (0–6)
Each risk factor = 1 point

bands.meaning: ~3.9% risk of major cardiac complication. Low risk. Proceed with surgery without further cardiac testing in most cases.
~6.0% risk. Low-moderate risk. Proceed with surgery. Consider clinical risk factors and functional capacity.
~10.1% risk. Moderate risk. Consider non-invasive cardiac testing if it would change management.
~15%+ risk. High risk. Consider cardiology consultation, non-invasive testing, and careful perioperative planning.

citations.text: Lee TH, Marcantonio ER, Mangione CM, et al. Derivation and prospective validation of a simple index for prediction of cardiac risk of major noncardiac surgery. Circulation. 1999;100(10):1043-1049. PMID: 10477528

entries.copyright: public domain — published academic scoring system
entries.limitations: Does not capture functional capacity (METs — important for decision-making). Does not include age, type of surgery (beyond 'high-risk'), urgency, or hemodynamic status. Insulin-dependent diabetes only — does not capture non-insulin diabetes. Creatinine threshold (>2.0 mg/dL) may miss significant renal impairment (eGFR may be more informative). Does not predict 30-day mortality specifically — focuses on cardiac events. Not validated for cardiac surgery (CABG, valve) — use separate scores (EuroSCORE, STS). Underestimates risk in some vascular surgery patients. Doesn't capture current medications (beta-blockers, statins, anticoagulants). The ACS NSQIP calculator may be more accurate for individual risk but is more complex. Should be used with clinical judgment, not in isolation. 2014 ESC/ESA guidelines recommend combined use with functional capacity assessment. Does not include NT-proBNP or other biomarkers (emerging data supports preoperative biomarker testing).

entries.name: STS risk score
entries.purpose: Mortality/morbidity after cardiac surgery (US)
entries.formula_human: Bayesian logistic model of 40+ variables; STS calculator

entries.name: Shock Index
entries.purpose: Hemorrhage/shock screening
entries.formula_human: SI = HR/SBP; MSI = HR/MAP; SI>0.9 abnormal, >1.3 high risk

entries.name: TIMI (UA/NSTEMI)
entries.purpose: Predicts 14-day risk of all-cause mortality, new or recurrent MI, or urgent revascularization in patients with unstable angina or NSTEMI.
entries.formula_human: TIMI = Sum of all 7 binary criteria (each 0 or 1)

inputs.label: ≥3 CAD risk factors
inputs.description: Hypertension, hypercholesterolemia/dyslipidemia, diabetes, family history of premature CAD, current smoking

inputs.label: Known CAD (stenosis ≥50%)
inputs.description: Previously documented coronary artery disease with ≥50% stenosis

inputs.label: Aspirin use in prior 7 days
inputs.description: ASA taken within 7 days before presentation

inputs.label: ≥2 anginal episodes in 24 hours
inputs.description: Two or more episodes of anginal pain within the 24 hours preceding presentation

inputs.label: ST-segment deviation ≥0.5 mm
inputs.description: ST deviation (elevation or depression) of at least 0.5 mm on ECG

inputs.label: Elevated cardiac biomarkers
inputs.description: Elevated troponin or CK-MB above local assay threshold

bands.meaning: Low risk (~4.7% composite endpoint at 14 days)
Intermediate risk (~8.3–13.2%)

citations.text: Antman EM, Cohen M, Bernink PJLM, et al. The TIMI risk score for unstable angina/non-ST elevation MI: A method for prognostication and therapeutic decision making. JAMA. 2000;284(7):835-842. PMID: 10938172

entries.limitations: Originally derived from clinical trial populations (may underperform in real-world heterogeneous ED cohorts). Does not incorporate high-sensitivity troponin. Does not account for renal function or BNP. Subjective interpretation of 'risk factors' component.

entries.name: ISTH DIC score
entries.purpose: Diagnoses overt disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) using readily available coagulation parameters.
entries.formula_human: ISTH DIC Score = Platelet(0–2) + Fibrin_marker(0–3) + PT_prolongation(0–2) + Fibrinogen(0–1). Total = 0–8.

bands.meaning: Not consistent with overt DIC; repeat if clinically indicated
Compatible with overt DIC; initiate treatment

citations.text: Taylor FB Jr, Toh CH, Hoots WK, et al. Towards definition, clinical and laboratory criteria, and a scoring system for disseminated intravascular coagulation. Thromb Haemost. 2001;86(5):1327-1330. PMID: 11816725

entries.limitations: Fibrinogen is an acute phase reactant and may be elevated despite DIC. D-dimer/FDP cutoffs vary by assay. Score designed for overt DIC — may miss early/chronic DIC. Does not capture clinical context. Multiple DIC scoring systems exist (ISTH, JMHW, JAAM).

entries.name: APACHE II
entries.purpose: Predicts hospital mortality in ICU patients using acute physiology derangements, age, and chronic health status within the first 24 hours of ICU admission.
entries.formula_human:
APACHE II = APS (0–60) + Age_points (0–6) + Chronic_health_points (0 or 2 or 5). Total = 0–71.

Predicted mortality = e^(β₀ + β₁×APACHE_II_score + constant) / (1 + e^(β₀ + β₁×APACHE_II_score + constant)), where β₀ and β₁ are disease-specific coefficients published in Knaus et al. 1985. For general use: ln(R/(1−R)) = −3.517 + (APACHE_II × 0.146) + 0.603 (only if emergency surgery) + diagnostic category coefficient.

inputs.label: Acute Physiology Score (APS)
inputs.description: Score from 12 physiologic variables: temperature (core), MAP, HR, RR, oxygenation (A-aDO₂ or PaO₂), arterial pH, serum sodium, potassium, creatinine, hematocrit, WBC, GCS
inputs.options_text: Each variable scored 0–4 (derangement from normal), maximum APS = 60
inputs.points_text: 0–4 points per variable based on degree of abnormality

inputs.label: Chronic Health Points
inputs.description: Severe organ system insufficiency or immunocompromised status before ICU admission (liver, cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, immunocompromised)
inputs.options_text: 0 = no organ insufficiency or immunocompromised; 5 = if emergency postoperative or non-operative admission with chronic insufficiency; 2 = elective postoperative admission with chronic insufficiency

bands.meaning: Low severity; predicted mortality ~4%
Predicted mortality ~8%
Predicted mortality ~15%
Predicted mortality ~25%
Predicted mortality ~40%
Predicted mortality ~55%
Predicted mortality ~73%
Predicted mortality ~85%

citations.text: Knaus WA, Draper EA, Wagner DP, Zimmerman JE. APACHE II: a severity of disease classification system. Crit Care Med. 1985;13(10):818-829. PMID: 3928249

entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app
entries.limitations: Requires full 24 hours of data (not available at admission for rapid triage). Worst physiologic values in first 24h needed. Not calibrated for contemporary practice (developed 1985). GCS is subjective. Does not account for ICU treatment effectiveness. Superseded by APACHE IV for quality benchmarking.

entries.name: CAM-ICU
entries.purpose: Validated bedside tool to diagnose delirium in critically ill, intubated and non-intubated ICU patients.
entries.formula_human:
CAM-ICU positive (delirium present) if ALL of:
1. Feature 1 (acute onset/fluctuation) is present
AND
2. Feature 2 (inattention) is present
AND
3. Either Feature 3 (altered LOC) OR Feature 4 (disorganized thinking) is present

If RASS = −4 or −5, CAM-ICU cannot be assessed (patient is unarousable).

inputs.label: Feature 1: Acute onset or fluctuating course
Feature 2: Inattention
inputs.description: ASES letter recognition test: patient squeezes hand on letter 'A' when letters read. Inattention = <8 correct out of 10.

inputs.label: Feature 3: Altered level of consciousness
inputs.description: RASS ≠ 0 (anything other than alert and calm)

inputs.label: Feature 4: Disorganized thinking
inputs.description: Yes/no questions and command test (e.g., 'hold up this many fingers' + 'do the same thing with the other hand'). Score 0–4, positive if <4 correct.

bands.meaning: Delirium present. Associated with increased mortality, prolonged ICU stay, and long-term cognitive impairment.
Delirium not detected. May not be assessable if RASS ≤ −4.

citations.text: Ely EW, Inouye SK, Bernard GR, et al. Delirium in mechanically ventilated patients: validity and reliability of the confusion assessment method for the intensive care unit (CAM-ICU). JAMA. 2001;286(21):2703-2710. PMID: 11730446

entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app — training materials at icudelirium.org
entries.limitations: Cannot be assessed in deeply sedated patients (RASS ≤ −4). ASES letter test requires hearing/vision. May be difficult in patients with pre-existing dementia. False negatives possible with fluctuating delirium. Requires training for consistent administration.

entries.name: NEWS2
entries.purpose: Standardized track-and-trigger early warning score for detecting clinical deterioration in acutely ill patients. Used for bedside monitoring, triage, and escalation decisions in hospitals and prehospital settings. Adopted by the Royal College of Physicians (UK) and endorsed by NHS England.
entries.formula_human:
NEWS2 = sum of all parameter scores
Range: 0–20

Single parameter score of 3 in any category = automatic trigger (aggregate score = 3)

Note: Uses SpO₂ Scale 1 by default. Use Scale 2 for documented hypercapnic respiratory failure (COPD with chronic type 2 respiratory failure, on long-term oxygen therapy or NIV).

inputs.label: SpO₂ Scale 2 (for patients with hypercapnic respiratory failure)
inputs.options_text: ≤83 (3), 84–85 (2), 86–87 (1), 88–92 (0 for target), ≥93 (0 if on O₂, or 0 if no supplemental O₂)

inputs.label: Consciousness (ACVPU)
inputs.options_text: Alert (0 points), Confusion (3), Voice (3), Pain (3), Unresponsive (3)

bands.meaning: Continue routine monitoring. Minimum 12-hourly assessment.
Minimum every 4–6 hours. Consider if frequency of monitoring should increase.
Urgent review by ward nurse. Consider escalation. Minimum every hour monitoring.
Urgent review by clinician with competencies for acute illness. Consider transfer to higher dependency environment.
Emergency assessment by clinical team, including critical care. Transfer to higher level of care. Continuous monitoring.

citations.text: Royal College of Physicians. National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2: Standardising the assessment of acute-illness severity in the NHS. Updated report. London: RCP; 2017

entries.copyright: Royal College of Physicians — free for NHS and clinical use with attribution
entries.limitations: Designed for adult patients in hospital. Not validated for children (use PEWS). Not validated for pregnancy (use MEOWS/MODS). Different performance in different clinical areas (ED vs. ward vs. post-surgical). Relies on accurate vital sign measurement — nursing practice variability. NEWS2 ≥7 has high sensitivity but moderate specificity (high false-positive rate). Single parameter = 3 may cause over-triggering. Does not incorporate laboratory results, diagnosis, or trajectory. Cultural adoption varies (NEWS used in UK, Australia; modified versions elsewhere). Does not capture mental status changes in detail (only ACVPU). Does not incorporate pain assessment. Respiratory rate is often the most inaccurate vital sign (under-recorded). Oxygen administration assessment depends on documentation accuracy. Not validated in children </think>�<16 years. Chronic vital sign abnormalities may trigger falsely in some patients.

entries.name: RASS
entries.purpose: Validated level of alertness and agitation scale used to titrate sedation in mechanically ventilated ICU patients.
entries.formula_human:
RASS scale:
+4 = Combative (overtly combative, violent, immediate danger to staff)
+3 = Very agitated (pulls/removes tubes/catheters, aggressive)
+2 = Agitated (frequent non-purposeful movement, fights ventilator)
+1 = Restless (anxious, apprehensive, movements not aggressive)
0 = Alert and calm
−1 = Drowsy (not fully alert but has sustained awakening to voice, eye contact ≥10 sec)
−2 = Light sedation (briefly awakens to voice, eye contact <10 sec)
−3 = Moderate sedation (movement or eye opening to voice, no eye contact)
−4 = Deep sedation (no response to voice, movement or eye opening to physical stimulation)
−5 = Unarousable (no response to voice or physical stimulation)

inputs.label: Level of consciousness
inputs.description: Patient's level of alertness and response to voice and physical stimulation

bands.meaning: Agitated; may need sedating medication
Target sedation level for most ICU patients (PADIS guidelines)
Light sedation; appropriate for many mechanically ventilated patients
Moderate to deep sedation; reassess need (associated with worse outcomes)

citations.text: Sessler CN, Gosnell MS, Grap MJ, et al. The Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale: validity and reliability in adult intensive care unit patients. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2002;166(10):1338-1344. PMID: 12421743

entries.limitations: Cannot be used in patients receiving paralytic agents. Sedation assessment may be confounded by neurological injury. Requires patient interaction. Deeply sedated patients (−4, −5) are scored identically.

entries.name: SAPS II
entries.purpose: Predicts hospital mortality in ICU patients using 17 variables from the first 24 hours of ICU admission.
entries.formula_human:
SAPS II = Sum of all variable points. Max = 163.

Hospital mortality: logit = −7.7631 + 0.0737 × SAPS_II + 0.9971 × ln(SAPS_II + 1). Mortality = e^logit / (1 + e^logit).

bands.meaning: Low severity; predicted mortality <5%
Moderate severity; predicted mortality ~5–20%
High severity; predicted mortality ~20–50%
Very high severity; predicted mortality ~50–80%
Extremely high severity; predicted mortality >80%

citations.text: Le Gall JR, Lemeshow S, Saulnier F. A new Simplified Acute Physiology Score (SAPS II) based on a European/North American multicenter study. JAMA. 1993;270(24):2957-2963. PMID: 8254858

entries.limitations: 24-hour data collection window. Calibration drift over time (overestimates mortality in modern ICUs). GCS is subjective. Does not account for treatment received. Superseded by SAPS 3 for contemporary use.

entries.name: SIRS
entries.purpose: Identifies systemic inflammatory response; historically used to define sepsis (pre-Sepsis-3 definition).
entries.formula_human: SIRS = Temperature(1) + Heart_rate(1) + Respiratory_rate(1) + WBC(1). SIRS positive if ≥2 criteria met.

bands.meaning: SIRS negative
SIRS positive — historically defined sepsis when combined with suspected infection

citations.text: Bone RC, Balk RA, Cerra FB, et al. Definitions for sepsis and organ failure and guidelines for the use of innovative therapies in sepsis. Chest. 1992;101(6):1644-1655. PMID: 1303622

entries.limitations: Very sensitive but not specific (positive in many non-infectious conditions). Superseded by Sepsis-3 (qSOFA/SOFA-based definitions). Still used for sepsis screening in some protocols. High false-positive rate in postoperative, trauma, and critically ill patients.

entries.name: SOFA
entries.purpose: Assesses the degree of organ failure across six organ systems in critically ill patients; used to track organ dysfunction over time and define sepsis.
entries.formula_human: SOFA = Respiratory(0–4) + Coagulation(0–4) + Liver(0–4) + Cardiovascular(0–4) + CNS(0–4) + Renal(0–4). Total = 0–24.

inputs.label: Respiratory: PaO₂/FiO₂
inputs.description: Ratio of arterial oxygen to inspired oxygen fraction

inputs.label: Cardiovascular: MAP and vasopressors
inputs.description: Mean arterial pressure and dose of vasopressors (µg/kg/min)

bands.meaning: No organ failure
Mild organ dysfunction
Moderate organ failure
Severe organ failure; mortality ~50%
Critical organ failure; mortality >80%
Acute worsening; SOFA increase ≥2 defines sepsis-related organ dysfunction

citations.text: Vincent JL, Moreno R, Takala J, et al. The SOFA (Sepsis-related Organ Failure Assessment) score to describe organ dysfunction/failure. Intensive Care Med. 1996;22(7):707-710. PMID: 8844239

entries.limitations: Requires laboratory values (not instant). Cardiovascular subscore has changed definitions over time (vasopressor types/doses). GCS is subjective. Originally designed for sepsis but applied broadly. Sequential assessment more informative than single value.

entries.name: qSOFA
entries.purpose: Bedside screening tool to identify patients with suspected infection who are at risk for poor outcomes (prolonged ICU stay or in-hospital mortality). Part of Sepsis-3 definition.

bands.meaning: Low risk of poor outcome from infection
High risk. Consider further assessment for sepsis, including full SOFA score and clinical judgment.

citations.text: Singer M, Deutschman CS, Seymour CW, et al. The Third International Consensus Definitions for Sepsis and Septic Shock (Sepsis-3). JAMA. 2016;315(8):801-810. PMID: 26903338

entries.limitations: Not intended for use as a diagnostic criterion for sepsis — it is a screening/prognostic tool. Low sensitivity for sepsis (misses many septic patients). Not intended for use in the ICU. Better at identifying patients at risk of poor outcome than identifying sepsis per se. Does not perform as well as SIRS in some settings.

entries.name: Alvarado score
entries.purpose: Clinical scoring system to estimate probability of acute appendicitis and guide decision for imaging or surgery.
entries.formula_human: Alvarado = Migration(1) + Anorexia(1) + Nausea(1) + RLQ_tenderness(2) + Rebound(1) + Temperature(1) + Leukocytosis(2) + Left_shift(1). Acronym: MANTRELS

inputs.label: Migration of pain to RLQ
inputs.description: Pain migrating to the right lower quadrant

inputs.label: Left shift (neutrophilia)
inputs.description: WBC differential with >70% neutrophils (bands ≥1 = shift to left)

bands.meaning: Low probability of appendicitis (~1–5%). Consider discharge with follow-up.
Moderate probability (~15–30%). Observe, imaging (CT/US), or surgical consult.
High probability (~70–95%). Strongly consider surgical consultation or appendectomy.

citations.text: Alvarado A. A practical score for the early diagnosis of acute appendicitis. Ann Emerg Med. 1986;15(5):557-564. PMID: 3963537

entries.limitations: Less accurate in women of reproductive age, children, and elderly. CT scan has largely replaced clinical scoring in many settings. Does not account for imaging findings. Inter-rater variability on rebound tenderness. Performance varies by population and prevalence.

entries.name: Centor / McIsaac
entries.purpose: Strep pharyngitis
entries.formula_human: Fever 1, no cough 1, tender anterior nodes 1, exudate 1, age 3-14 +1 / >=45 -1; total -1 to 5

entries.name: Sgarbossa (see surgery)
entries.purpose: Identifies acute myocardial infarction in patients with left bundle branch block (LBBB) on ECG.
entries.formula_human: Sgarbossa = Concordant_ST_elevation(5 if yes) + Concordant_ST_depression_V1-V3(3 if yes) + Discordant_ST_elevation_≥5mm(2 if yes)

inputs.label: Concordant ST elevation ≥1 mm
inputs.description: ST-segment elevation ≥1 mm in any lead with a positive QRS complex (concordant with QRS)

inputs.label: Concordant ST depression ≥1 mm in V1–V3
inputs.description: ST depression ≥1 mm in V1, V2, or V3 (concordant with the negative QRS in these leads)

inputs.label: Discordant ST elevation ≥5 mm
inputs.description: ST elevation ≥5 mm in any lead with a negative QRS (discordant)

bands.meaning: High specificity (>90%) for acute MI. Recommended to activate cath lab.
Insufficient specificity to diagnose AMI in LBBB. Consider modified Sgarbossa.

citations.text: Sgarbossa EB, Pinski SL, Barbagelata A, et al. Electrocardiographic diagnosis of evolving acute myocardial infarction in the presence of left bundle-branch block. N Engl J Med. 1996;334(8):481-487. PMID: 8559200

entries.limitations: High specificity but low sensitivity (~20–36%) for AMI. Discordant ST elevation criterion (≥5 mm) was the most weighted but least specific. Modified Sgarbossa (using ST/S ratio ≤-0.25 in discordant leads) improves sensitivity.

entries.name: BISAP
entries.purpose: Simpler alternative to Ranson/APACHE II for predicting severe acute pancreatitis and in-hospital mortality within first 24 hours.
entries.formula_human: BISAP = BUN>25(1) + Impaired_mental_status(1) + SIRS(1) + Age>60(1) + Pleural_effusion(1)

inputs.label: BUN >25 mg/dL
inputs.description: Blood urea nitrogen >25 mg/dL at admission

inputs.label: Pleural effusion
inputs.description: Pleural effusion on imaging (CXR or CT)

bands.meaning: Low risk of severe pancreatitis and in-hospital mortality (<2%).
High risk. Mortality increases significantly (≥5–20% for score 3, up to 40%+ for score 5). ICU-level care recommended.

citations.text: Wu BU, Johannes RS, Sun X, et al. The early prediction of mortality in acute pancreatitis: a large population-based study. Gut. 2008;57(12):1698-1703. PMID: 18519429

entries.limitations: Single cutoff (≥3) may miss some at-risk patients. SIRS criteria require all 4 parameters (temp, HR, RR, WBC). Impaired mental status is subjective. Does not include imaging severity (CT severity index). Does not capture organ failure dynamics. Superseded by revised Atlanta classification for defining severity.

entries.name: CT Severity Index (CTSI)
entries.purpose: Pancreatitis severity on CT
entries.formula_human: Pancreatic inflammation grade 0-4 + necrosis extent 0-6 (none 0, <30% 2, 30-50% 4, >50% 6); total 0-10

entries.name: Child-Pugh
entries.purpose: Cirrhosis severity / transplant listing, surgical risk
entries.formula_human: Bilirubin <2/2-3/>3 =1/2/3; Albumin >3.5/2.8-3.5/<2.8 =1/2/3; INR <1.7/1.7-2.3/>2.3 =1/2/3; Ascites none/mild/mod-severe =1/2/3; Encephalopathy none/I-II/III-IV =1/2/3; total 5-15 (A 5-6, B 7-9, C 10-15)

entries.name: FIB-4
entries.purpose: Non-invasive serum biomarker index to estimate liver fibrosis stage in patients with chronic liver disease (especially HCV and NAFLD).
entries.formula_human:
FIB-4 = (Age × AST) / (Platelet_count × √ALT)

Units: Age in years, AST in U/L, Platelet in ×10⁹/L, ALT in U/L

bands.meaning: F0–F1 fibrosis unlikely. Low probability of advanced fibrosis. Negative predictive value ~90%.
Indeterminate zone. Further evaluation needed.
High probability of advanced fibrosis (≥F3). Specificity ~97%. Refer to hepatologist.

citations.text: Sterling RK, Lissen E, Clumeck N, et al. Development of a simple noninvasive index to predict significant fibrosis in patients with HIV/HCV coinfection. Hepatology. 2006;43(6):1317-1325. PMID: 16729309

entries.limitations: Less accurate in the indeterminate zone (1.3–2.67). Affected by acute hepatitis flare (AST/ALT fluctuate). Not reliable in HCV-HIV coinfection with very low CD4 counts. Cutoffs differ by age group and liver disease etiology. Does not replace liver biopsy for definitive staging. Less validated in non-White populations.

entries.name: Forrest classification
entries.purpose: UGIB endoscopic stigmata
entries.formula_human: Ia spurting, Ib oozing, IIa visible vessel, IIb clot, IIc flat spot, III clean base

entries.name: Glasgow-Blatchford Score
entries.purpose: Upper GI bleed risk stratification / safe discharge

entries.name: MELD
entries.purpose: Predicts 3-month mortality in patients with chronic liver disease. Used for prioritizing liver transplant allocation.
entries.formula_human:
MELD = 3.78 × ln(bilirubin mg/dL) + 11.20 × ln(INR) + 9.57 × ln(creatinine mg/dL) + 6.43

Minimum value for each variable = 1.0
Maximum creatinine = 4.0 mg/dL (or set to 4.0 if on dialysis)
All values set to minimum of 1.0 if below 1.0
Result rounded to nearest integer
Add +1 point if within 30 days of prior calculation (to ensure lab re-checks)
Add 10 points if hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exception applies (T2 HCC in original system, now variable by region)

bands.meaning: ~2% 3-month mortality
~6% 3-month mortality
~20% 3-month mortality
~53% 3-month mortality
~71% 3-month mortality. Highest priority for transplant.

citations.text: Kamath PS, Wiesner RH, Malinchoc M, et al. A model to predict survival in patients with end-stage liver disease. Hepatology. 2001;33(2):464-470. PMID: 11172350

entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app — used by UNOS/OPTN
entries.limitations: Does not capture hyponatremia (addressed by MELD-Na). Creatinine may be affected by muscle mass, AKI, or hepatorenal syndrome. Bilirubin and INR affected by cholestasis and warfarin, respectively. Does not include portal hypertension severity or encephalopathy. MELD exceptions (HCC, hepatopulmonary syndrome) introduce subjectivity. Not validated in acute liver failure (different pathophysiology). Dialysis creatinine rule is crude.

entries.name: MELD-Na
entries.purpose: Refined MELD score incorporating serum sodium to improve mortality prediction in cirrhosis. Current standard for liver transplant allocation in the US.
entries.formula_human:
MELD-Na = MELD + 1.32 × (137 − Na) − 0.033 × MELD × (137 − Na)

Where:
- MELD is calculated as above (minimum MELD = 1, maximum MELD used in calculation capped at 40 in the non-linear version)
- Na is constrained between 125 and 137 mEq/L
- If Na <125, use 125; if Na >137, use 137
- MELD score minimum = 1; maximum for Na interaction = 11 in the UNOS version

UNOS implementation (post-2016): MELD-Na replaces MELD with a floor of MELD = 1 and ceiling adjustments. Verify current UNOS policy for latest coefficients.

bands.range: Same MELD thresholds, but scores are generally 1–3 points higher with Na correction
bands.meaning: Higher scores with hyponatremia → higher transplant priority
Significantly worse prognosis. Sodium <125 adds substantial mortality risk.

citations.text: Kim WR, Biggins SW, Kremers WK, et al. Hyponatremia and mortality among patients on the liver-transplant waiting list. N Engl J Med. 2008;359(10):1018-1026. PMID: 18768945; MELD-Na: Leise MD, et al. Hepatology. 2014;60:284-292

entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app — used by UNOS/OPTN
entries.limitations: Sodium may be affected by diuretic use, fluid status, and measurement technique. Diuretic-adjusted MELD-Na has been proposed but not universally adopted. MELD-Na may disadvantage patients on aggressive diuretic therapy (iatrogenic hyponatremia). Changes to UNOS policy (MELD 3.0) may further refine scoring. Not validated for acute liver failure.

entries.name: SAAG
entries.purpose: Ascites cause
entries.formula_human: SAAG = serum albumin - ascitic albumin; >=1.1 g/dL = portal hypertension

entries.name: DXA T-score
entries.purpose: Osteoporosis diagnosis
entries.formula_human: T-score = (BMD - young adult mean)/SD; <= -2.5 osteoporosis, -1 to -2.5 osteopenia

entries.name: FRAX
entries.purpose: 10-yr fracture probability
entries.formula_human: WHO algorithm: age, sex, BMI, prior fracture, parent hip fracture, smoking, glucocorticoids, RA, alcohol, secondary osteoporosis, BMD (femoral neck)

entries.name: HbA1c / eAG
entries.purpose: Glycemic control

entries.name: ASPECTS
entries.purpose: CT ischemia extent (thrombectomy selection)
entries.formula_human: 10 regions, -1 each for early ischemic change; 10 normal

entries.name: Fisher grade
entries.purpose: SAH clot burden on CT
entries.formula_human: 1 none, 2 thin <1mm, 3 thick >=1mm, 4 IVH +/- parenchyma

entries.name: Hunt & Hess
entries.purpose: SAH clinical grade
entries.formula_human: I asymptomatic - V coma/decerebrate

entries.name: ICH score
entries.purpose: Predicts 30-day mortality after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage.
entries.formula_human: ICH Score = GCS(0–2) + Volume≥30mL(1) + IVH(1) + Infratentorial(1) + Age≥80(1)

inputs.label: ICH volume
inputs.description: Hemorrhage volume on initial CT (ABC/2 method)

bands.meaning: 30-day mortality ~0%. Excellent prognosis.
~13% mortality
~26% mortality
~72% mortality
~97% mortality
~100% mortality. Consider goals-of-care discussion.

citations.text: Hemphill JC 3rd, Bonovich DC, Besmertis L, et al. The ICH score: a simple, reliable grading scale for intracerebral hemorrhage. Stroke. 2001;32(4):891-897. PMID: 11283388

entries.limitations: Does not capture etiology (amyloid vs hypertensive), anticoagulation status, or hematoma expansion. Volume measurement by ABC/2 has inherent imprecision. GCS assessment may be confounded by sedation/intubation. Death prediction better than functional outcome prediction. Does not include ICH location per se (lobar vs deep) — infratentorial yes/no is crude. Not designed for treatment decisions — should complement clinical judgment.

entries.name: Modified Rankin Scale
entries.purpose: Measures degree of disability and dependence in daily activities after stroke. Primary outcome measure in most acute stroke trials.
entries.formula_human:
Single ordinal grade:
0 = No symptoms at all
1 = No significant disability despite symptoms; able to carry out all usual duties and activities
2 = Slight disability; unable to carry out all previous activities but able to look after own affairs without assistance
3 = Moderate disability; requiring some help but able to walk without assistance
4 = Moderately severe disability; unable to walk without assistance and unable to attend to bodily needs without assistance
5 = Severe disability; bedridden, incontinent, requiring constant nursing care and attention
6 = Dead

inputs.label: Overall disability
inputs.description: Global assessment of functional independence post-stroke

bands.meaning: No symptoms
No significant disability
Slight disability
Moderate disability
Moderately severe disability
Severe disability
Dead
Favorable outcome (commonly used as primary endpoint in stroke trials)

citations.text: Rankin J. Cerebral vascular accidents in patients over the age of 60. Scott Med J. 1957;2(5):200-215 (original); van Swieten JC, et al. Stroke. 1988;19:604-607 (modified version)

entries.limitations: Subjective, especially between adjacent grades (2 vs 3, 3 vs 4). Inter-rater variability significant without structured interview. Shift analysis preferred over dichotomization in clinical trials (mRS 0–2 vs 3–6 loses information). Does not capture cognitive, emotional, or quality of life domains. Self-reported or proxy-reported — subject to recall and perception biases. Minimum clinically important difference varies by baseline severity.

entries.name: NIHSS
entries.purpose: Quantifies neurological deficit severity in acute stroke for standardized assessment, treatment decisions (tPA eligibility), and prognosis.
entries.formula_human:
NIHSS = sum of all 15 items (1a + 1b + 1c + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5a + 5b + 6a + 6b + 7 + 8 + 9 + 10 + 11)

Total range 0–42

inputs.label: 1b. LOC questions
inputs.options_text: 0 = both correct; 1 = one correct; 2 = neither correct

inputs.label: 1c. LOC commands
inputs.options_text: 0 = both correct; 1 = one correct; 2 = neither correct

inputs.label: 2. Best gaze
inputs.options_text: 0 = normal; 1 = partial gaze palsy; 2 = forced deviation

inputs.label: 3. Visual fields
inputs.options_text: 0 = no loss; 1 = partial hemianopia; 2 = complete hemianopia; 3 = bilateral hemianopia

inputs.label: 5a/5b. Motor arm (L/R)
inputs.description: Arm drift (10 seconds if arms outstretched, 5 seconds if legs)
inputs.options_text: 0 = no drift; 1 = drift before 5s; 2 = some effort against gravity; 3 = no effort against gravity; 4 = no movement; UN = amputation/joint fusion

inputs.label: 6a/6b. Motor leg (L/R)
inputs.options_text: 0 = no drift; 1 = drift before 5s; 2 = some effort against gravity; 3 = no effort against gravity; 4 = no movement; UN = amputation/joint fusion

inputs.label: 7. Limb ataxia
inputs.options_text: 0 = absent; 1 = present in one limb; 2 = present in two limbs

inputs.label: 9. Best language
inputs.description: Describes picture, names items, reads sentences
inputs.options_text: 0 = no aphasia; 1 = mild-moderate; 2 = severe; 3 = mute/global aphasia

inputs.label: 10. Dysarthria
inputs.options_text: 0 = normal; 1 = mild-moderate; 2 = severe/anarthric; UN = intubated/physical barrier

inputs.label: 11. Extinction/inattention
inputs.options_text: 0 = no abnormality; 1 = partial (one modality); 2 = complete (two modalities)

bands.meaning: No neurological deficit (normal neurological exam)
Minor stroke
Moderate stroke. tPA eligible if within time window.
Moderate-severe stroke
Severe stroke. High mortality risk. Consider mechanical thrombectomy if large vessel occlusion.

citations.text: Brott T, Adams HP Jr, Olinger CP, et al. Measurements of acute cerebral infarction: a clinical examination scale. Stroke. 1989;20(7):864-870. PMID: 2749846

entries.limitations: Requires trained assessor (standardized training and certification recommended). Inter-rater variability exists, especially for items 5 (motor) and 8 (sensory). Score of 0 does not exclude significant stroke (posterior circulation stroke may have NIHSS 0). Does not capture posterior circulation deficits well (no cerebellar/brainstem specific items). Not a diagnostic tool — diagnosis requires imaging. Ceiling effect at higher scores.

entries.name: WFNS
entries.purpose: Grading system for subarachnoid hemorrhage based on GCS and focal neurological deficit, to predict outcome.
entries.formula_human:
Grade I: GCS 15, no motor deficit
Grade II: GCS 13–14, no motor deficit
Grade III: GCS 13–14, with motor deficit
Grade IV: GCS 7–12, with or without motor deficit
Grade V: GCS 3–6, with or without motor deficit

bands.meaning: Best prognosis. ~80% good outcome.
~70% good outcome.
~50% good outcome.
~30% good outcome.
~15% good outcome. Worst prognosis.

citations.text: Report of World Federation of Neurological Surgeons Committee on a Universal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage Grading Scale. J Neurosurg. 1988;68(6):985-986. PMID: 3373284

entries.limitations: Motor deficit assessment is subjective in obtunded patients. Does not capture aneurysm size, location, or vasospasm risk. Better inter-rater reliability than Hunt-Hess but still imperfect. Sedation and intubation confound GCS assessment. Not directly comparable to Hunt-Hess without conversion tables.

entries.name: Braden Scale
entries.purpose: Pressure ulcer risk
entries.formula_human: Sensory perception, moisture, activity, mobility, nutrition, friction/shear: 1-4 (1-3 friction); total 6-23; <=18 at risk

entries.name: Clinical Frailty Scale
entries.purpose: Rapid clinician-assessed 9-point visual scale for frailty assessment. Incorporates fitness, activity, and dependency into a single score. Used in geriatric, surgical, and critical care settings for prognosis and treatment planning.
entries.formula_human:
1 = Very Fit: Robust, active, energetic, motivated, fit. Regularly exercise. Fittest for age.
2 = Well: No active disease symptoms, less fit than category 1. Occasional vigorous activity.
3 = Managing Well: Medical problems well-controlled, not regularly active beyond walking.
4 = Vulnerable: Not dependent on others for daily help but symptoms limit activities. 'Slowed up'.
5 = Mildly Frail: Need help with high-order IADLs (finances, transportation, heavy housework, medications).
6 = Moderately Frail: Need help with all outside activities and housekeeping. May need assistance with dressing/bathing.
7 = Severely Frail: Completely dependent for personal care, stable condition unlikely to deteriorate rapidly.
8 = Very Severely Frail: Completely dependent, approaching end of life. Could recover from acute illness.
9 = Terminally Ill: Approaching end of life, not expected to recover from current illness (life expectancy <6 months).

inputs.label: Frailty assessment
inputs.description: Clinician judgment based on patient's baseline functional status 2 weeks before admission, incorporating fitness, comorbidity, and ability to perform activities of daily living

bands.meaning: Non-frail. Low perioperative risk. Standard surgical/anesthesia approach.
Vulnerable/pre-frail. Increased risk. Consider prehabilitation.
Mild-moderate frailty. Higher perioperative morbidity/mortality. Goals-of-care discussion recommended. Consider less invasive approaches.
Severe-very severe frailty. High perioperative mortality. Consider conservative management. Goals-of-care discussion essential.
Terminal illness. Comfort care. Not expected to recover from acute event.
CFS ≥5 associated with significantly higher mortality in COVID-19 patients (used in triage guidelines internationally)

citations.text: Rockwood K, Song X, MacKnight C, et al. A global clinical measure of fitness and frailty in elderly people. CMAJ. 2005;173(5):489-495. PMID: 16129869

entries.copyright: Canadian Geriatrics Society — free for clinical use with proper attribution
entries.limitations: Single-item clinician assessment — subject to inter-rater variability (moderate agreement, kappa ~0.6). Assessment based on patient/caregiver report of baseline function — may be inaccurate. Doesn't capture specific comorbidities, nutritional status, or cognitive impairment directly. Thresholds for treatment decisions not universally agreed upon. CFS 8 ('approaching end of life, could recover') distinction from CFS 7 ('stable, unlikely to deteriorate rapidly') can be subjective. Training materials available but not universally used. Doesn't replace comprehensive geriatric assessment. Validated primarily in older adults — not applicable to younger populations. 2-week baseline assessment may be difficult to determine in acute admissions.

entries.name: MUST
entries.purpose: 5-step screening tool for malnutrition risk in adults across all healthcare settings (hospital, community, care homes). Developed by BAPEN (British Association for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition). Simple and widely applicable.
entries.formula_human:
MUST = BMI score (0–2) + Weight loss score (0–2) + Acute disease effect (0 or 2)
Maximum = 6

If BMI and weight loss cannot be obtained: use alternative criteria (mid-upper arm circumference <23.5 cm = high risk)

Step 4: Overall risk category
Step 5: Management guidelines

inputs.label: Unplanned weight loss score
inputs.description: Unintentional weight loss in past 3-6 months

bands.meaning: Low risk — routine clinical care, repeat screening (weekly in hospital, monthly in care home, annually in community)
Medium risk — observe. Document dietary intake for 3 days. If adequate, routine care with monitoring.
High risk — treat. Refer to dietitian, nutritional support team. Set goals, improve nutritional intake with supplements, ONS, enteral or parenteral nutrition.

citations.text: Stratton RJ, King CL, Stroud MA, et al. 'Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool' predicts mortality and length of hospital stay in acutely ill elderly. Br J Nutr. 2006;95(2):325-330. PMID: 16466562; Elia M (ed). The 'MUST' Report. BAPEN, 2003

entries.copyright: BAPEN — free for clinical use with proper attribution
entries.limitations: Screening tool only — doesn't diagnose type of malnutrition or its etiology. BMI may be inaccurate in fluid overload, ascites, edema, or amputation. Weight loss over 3-6 months subject to recall bias. Acute disease effect (score 2) may overestimate risk in acutely ill but well-nourished patients. Mid-upper arm circumference alternative may not be practical in all settings. Doesn't capture micronutrient deficiencies or specific nutritional needs. Primarily validated in European populations. Simple design may miss nuanced nutritional problems. Management guidance is generic — requires dietitian input for complex cases.

entries.name: Morse Fall Scale
entries.purpose: Standardized nursing tool for assessing fall risk in hospitalized adult patients. Identifies patients who need fall prevention interventions. Most widely used fall risk assessment tool in hospitals internationally.
entries.formula_human:
MFS = History of falling + Secondary diagnosis + Ambulatory aid + IV/heparin lock + Gait + Mental status
Range: 0–125

inputs.label: History of falling (within 3 months or present illness)
Mental status
inputs.description: Patient's awareness of own ability and limitations
inputs.options_text: Oriented to own ability (0 points), Overestimates ability or forgets limitations (15 points)

bands.meaning: Standard fall prevention interventions (orientation, call light within reach, non-slip footwear, environment clear of hazards).
Standard interventions + targeted interventions (fall risk sign, toileting schedule, medications review, physical therapy consult).

Comprehensive fall prevention program. All low and moderate interventions + bed/chair alarm, 1:1 supervision if needed, low bed, room near nurses' station, consideration of movement restriction alternatives.

citations.text: Morse JM, Morse RM, Tylko SJ. Development of a scale to identify the fall-prone patient. Can J Aging. 1989;8(4):366-377; Morse JM. Enhancing the safety of hospitalized older adults. J Gerontol Nurs. 2006;32:6-10

entries.copyright: Dr. Janice Morse — free for clinical use with attribution
entries.limitations: Patient-reported history of falls may be inaccurate. 'Mental status' assessment is subjective. Secondary diagnosis is ubiquitous (most hospitalized patients score ≥15). Not validated for pediatric patients. Not validated for psychiatric patients. High specificity but variable sensitivity (moderate false-positive rate). Falls are multifactorial — no tool captures all risk factors. 'Ambulatory aid' category may not capture patients who refuse to use aids. Single-time assessment — should be reassessed regularly (minimum every shift in high-risk patients). Different cutoff values used by different institutions (25 vs. 45 for 'high risk'). Fall prevention interventions may not reduce fall rates in all settings. Not validated in all clinical environments (ED, OR, ICU may need different tools). Does not capture toileting urgency, environmental factors, or footwear. Cognitive impairment assessment is limited.

entries.name: NRS-2002
entries.purpose: Simple bedside screening tool for nutritional risk in hospitalized patients. Recommended by ESPEN (European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism) as first-line screening for all hospital admissions. Identifies patients who benefit from nutritional support.
entries.formula_human:
NRS-2002 = Nutritional score (BMI + Weight loss + Dietary intake, highest component 0–3) + Disease severity score (0–3) + Age adjustment (0–1)

Maximum = 7
Nutritional score = highest of BMI/weight loss/dietary intake categories
Disease severity = based on diagnosis and metabolic stress

inputs.label: BMI
inputs.options_text: ≥20.5=0, 18.5-20.5=1, <18.5=2, or BMI not available → use low BMI screening questions

inputs.label: Weight loss
inputs.description: Unintentional weight loss in past 3 months

inputs.label: Reduced dietary intake
inputs.description: Reduction in food intake in past week
inputs.options_text: No reduction=0, 25-50% reduction=1, 50-75% reduction=2, >75% reduction or starvation=3

inputs.label: Severity of disease
inputs.description: Disease severity as proxy for metabolic stress
inputs.options_text: Normal nutritional requirements=0, Hip fracture, acute complications of chronic disease=1, Major abdominal surgery, stroke, pneumonia, hematologic malignancy=2, Head injury, bone marrow transplant, ICU with APACHE ≥10=3

bands.meaning: No nutritional risk — re-screen weekly in hospital
Nutritional risk present — initiate nutritional support plan (dietary counseling, oral supplements, enteral or parenteral nutrition as indicated)
Severe nutritional risk — urgent nutritional intervention required

citations.text: Kondrup J, Rasmussen HH, Hamberg O, et al. Nutritional Risk Screening (NRS 2002): a new method based on an analysis of controlled clinical trials. Clin Nutr. 2003;22(3):321-336. PMID: 12765673

entries.copyright: free for clinical use — ESPEN published guidelines
entries.limitations: Screening tool, not diagnostic — doesn't assess type of malnutrition (protein-energy, micronutrient). Requires accurate height, weight, and dietary history — may be difficult in critically ill patients. BMI may be unreliable in edema, ascites, amputation, or fluid overload. Disease severity categories are coarse — some conditions span multiple categories. Weight loss over 3 months may be difficult to determine (recall bias). Not validated for outpatient use. Not suitable for pediatric patients. Doesn't capture specific nutrient deficiencies. Re-screening needed to capture evolving risk during hospitalization.

entries.name: Bishop score
entries.purpose: Clinician-assessed scoring of cervical favorability to predict likelihood of successful labor induction. Determines whether cervical ripening agents are needed before induction.
entries.formula_human:
Bishop Score = Dilation (0–3) + Effacement (0–3) + Station (0–3) + Consistency (0–2) + Position (0–2)
Maximum = 13

inputs.label: Station
inputs.description: Fetal head position relative to ischial spines

bands.meaning: Unfavorable cervix — cervical ripening needed (prostaglandins, mechanical methods) before induction
Intermediate — may benefit from ripening or proceed with induction
Favorable cervix — induction likely successful without ripening agents
Very favorable — spontaneous labor likely within 24 hours

citations.text: Bishop EH. Pelvic scoring for elective induction. Obstet Gynecol. 1964;24:266-268. PMID: 14199536

entries.limitations: Subjective — interobserver variability is significant, particularly for effacement, station, and consistency. Doesn't account for parity, gestational age, or fetal weight. Original described in low-risk nulliparous women — validation in modern populations limited. Modified Bishop (assigning 0–3 to each category equally) is most commonly used but not the original. Digital examination may be unreliable in obese patients. Doesn't predict cesarean delivery rate directly. Station assessment may vary depending on engagement vs. head position.

entries.name: Hadlock formula
entries.purpose: Estimated fetal weight on US
entries.formula_human: log10 EFW = 1.3596 - 0.00386*AC*FL + 0.0064*HC + 0.00061*BPD*AC + 0.0424*AC + 0.174*FL (Hadlock-4; variants Hadlock-1/2/3)

entries.name: MEOWS (Modified Early Obstetric Warning Score)
entries.purpose: Maternal deterioration on ward
entries.formula_human: RR, HR, temp, SBP, DBP, SpO2, neuro response, urine output; aggregate 0-? triggers

entries.name: Naegele's rule
entries.purpose: Estimated due date
entries.formula_human: EDD = LMP + 1 year - 3 months + 7 days (280 days)

entries.name: BCLC
entries.purpose: Staging and treatment allocation system for hepatocellular carcinoma incorporating tumor burden, liver function (CTP), and performance status.
entries.formula_human:
Staging algorithm:

Stage 0 (Very early): Single ≤2cm, CTP A, PS 0 → Resection or ablation
Stage A (Early): Single or ≤3 nodules each ≤3cm, CTP A-B, PS 0 → Resection, transplant, or ablation
Stage B (Intermediate): Multinodular, no vascular invasion/extrahepatic, CTP A-B, PS 0 → TACE
Stage C (Advanced): Vascular invasion or extrahepatic spread, CTP A-B, PS 1–2 → Systemic therapy
Stage D (Terminal): Any tumor, CTP C, PS 3–4 → Best supportive care

inputs.label: Tumor characteristics
inputs.description: Number of nodules, size, vascular invasion, extrahepatic spread
inputs.options_text: Single vs multinodular; ≤5cm vs >5cm; macrovascular invasion; metastases

bands.meaning: 5-year survival ~50–70% with treatment
5-year survival ~50% (transplant) or ~30% (resection/ablation)
Median survival ~20 months with TACE
Median survival ~11 months with systemic therapy (sorafenib, lenvatinib, atezolizumab+bevacizumab)
Median survival ~3 months. Best supportive care.

citations.text: Llovet JM, Brú C, Bruix J. Prognosis of hepatocellular carcinoma: the BCLC staging classification. Semin Liver Dis. 1999;19(3):329-338. PMID: 10518312; updated: Forner A, Reig ME, de Lope CR, Bruix J. Hepatology. 2018;67:1694-1705

entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published academic guideline
entries.limitations: Not all patients fit neatly into BCLC stages (e.g., large single tumor CTP A — BCLC A vs B). Treatment recommendations may not reflect local expertise or resources. Does not capture tumor biology (AFP, differentiation, molecular profile). Portal hypertension criterion is imprecise (HVPG ≥10 mmHg difficult to measure routinely). Staging and treatment allocation are combined — some prefer separation.

entries.name: Deauville 5-point scale
entries.purpose: Lymphoma PET response
entries.formula_human: 1 no uptake, 2 <=mediastinum, 3 >mediastinum <=liver, 4 >liver at 1 site, 5 >> liver/multiple; 1-3 complete metabolic response

entries.name: ECOG/WHO Performance Status
entries.purpose: Functional status in cancer trials
entries.formula_human: 0 fully active - 5 dead

entries.name: ELN 2022 AML risk
entries.purpose: AML transplant/intensity decision
entries.formula_human: Favorable: t(8;21), inv(16), NPM1-mut w/o FLT3-ITD, bZIP CEBPA; Intermediate: NPM1+FLT3, etc.; Adverse: TP53, complex karyotype, -5/5q-, etc.

entries.name: FIGO
entries.purpose: Gynecologic cancer staging
entries.formula_human: Stage I-IV by disease (cervix, endometrium, ovary...)

entries.name: Gleason score / ISUP grade
entries.purpose: Prostate cancer grade
entries.formula_human: Primary + secondary Gleason pattern (1-5 each, sum 6-10); ISUP GG1=6, GG2=3+4, GG3=4+3, GG4=8, GG5=9-10

entries.name: IPSS-R
entries.purpose: Prognostic classification system for MDS patients at diagnosis, predicting overall survival and risk of AML transformation.
entries.formula_human:
IPSS-R = Cytogenetics(0–4) + BM_blasts(0–4) + Hemoglobin(0–1.5) + Platelets(0–1) + ANC(0–0.5)

Total = 0–9 points (maximum theoretically 4+4+1.5+1+0.5=11 but in practice ≤9)

inputs.label: Cytogenetic risk category
inputs.options_text: Very good (del(11q), -Y), Good (normal, del(20q), del(5q), +8), Intermediate, Poor (complex 3 abnormalities, chromosome 7 abnormalities), Very poor (complex ≥3 abnormalities)

inputs.label: Bone marrow blast percentage
inputs.description: Percentage of blasts in bone marrow aspirate

bands.meaning: Median survival ~8.8 years. AML transformation risk low (~4% at 5 years).
Median survival ~5.3 years. AML transformation risk ~10% at 5 years.
Median survival ~3.0 years. AML risk ~25% at 5 years.
Median survival ~1.6 years. AML risk ~55% at 5 years.
Median survival ~0.8 years. AML risk ~85% at 5 years. Transplant evaluation recommended.

citations.text: Greenberg PL, Tuechler H, Schanz J, et al. Revised international prognostic scoring system for myelodysplastic syndromes. Blood. 2012;120(12):2454-2465. PMID: 22740453

entries.limitations: Cytogenetics require skilled cytogeneticist and may take 1–2 weeks. Some patients have insufficient metaphases. Does not incorporate somatic mutations (IPSS-M adds molecular data). At diagnosis only — does not capture disease evolution over time. Thresholds for treatment decisions (e.g., transplant at high/very high) are expert consensus, not empirically derived.

entries.name: International Prognostic Index (IPI)
entries.purpose: Predicts overall survival in aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma (primarily DLBCL) based on clinical factors.
entries.formula_human: IPI = Age>60(1) + LDH>normal(1) + PS≥2(1) + Stage_III/IV(1) + Extranodal>1(1)

inputs.label: Serum LDH >normal
inputs.description: Lactate dehydrogenase above upper limit of normal

inputs.label: Extranodal sites >1
inputs.description: More than one extranodal site of disease

bands.meaning: Low risk. 5-year OS ~70–80% (in rituximab era — R-IPI)
Low-intermediate risk. 5-year OS ~50–60%.
High-intermediate risk. 5-year OS ~40–50%.
High risk. 5-year OS ~25–35%.

citations.text: A predictive model for aggressive non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. The International Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma Prognostic Factors Project. N Engl J Med. 1993;329(14):987-994. PMID: 8141877

entries.limitations: Developed in pre-rituximab era. R-IPI and NCCN-IPI are better calibrated for contemporary patients receiving R-CHOP. Age cutoff of 60 is crude. LDH elevation is non-specific. Does not capture molecular subtypes (GCB vs ABC DLBCL) or MYC/BCL2 double-hit status. Extranodal site definition varies (some count bone marrow, others don't).

entries.name: Karnofsky Performance Status
entries.purpose: Clinician-assessed measure of functional status and ability to perform activities of daily living. Used in oncology to assess prognosis, guide treatment decisions (e.g., chemotherapy eligibility), and assess palliative care needs.
entries.formula_human:
100: Normal, no complaints, no evidence of disease
90: Able to carry on normal activity, minor signs/symptoms
80: Normal activity with effort, some signs/symptoms
70: Cares for self, unable to carry on normal activity
60: Requires occasional assistance, cares for most needs
50: Requires considerable assistance and frequent medical care
40: Disabled, requires special care and assistance
30: Severely disabled, hospitalization indicated
20: Very sick, hospitalization necessary, active supportive treatment
10: Moribund, fatal processes progressing rapidly
0: Dead

inputs.label: Functional capacity
inputs.description: Clinician assessment of patient's ability to carry on normal activity and perform self-care

bands.meaning: Able to carry on normal activity. Usually eligible for clinical trials and active treatment.
Unable to work, can live at home, cares for most personal needs. May still be eligible for some treatments.
Requires considerable assistance. Palliative care referral recommended. Active treatment benefit-risk must be carefully weighed.
Hospitalization indicated, severely disabled. Focus on comfort and symptom management.
Moribund. Comfort care and end-of-life planning.
KPS <50-60 generally associated with <6-month median survival in advanced cancer (varies by tumor type)

citations.text: Karnofsky DA, Burchenal JH. The clinical evaluation of chemotherapeutic agents in cancer. In: MacLeod CM (ed). Evaluation of Chemotherapeutic Agents. New York: Columbia University Press, 1949:191-205

entries.limitations: Clinician-assessed — subject to observer bias and variability (ICC ~0.6–0.7). 10-point intervals may not capture subtle changes. Ceiling effect (most patients cluster at 60-80). Different assessors may classify the same patient differently. Patient self-assessment often differs from clinician assessment. Not validated for all conditions equally (strongest in oncology). Doesn't capture cognitive function or psychological well-being. Functional status alone may not predict treatment tolerance or toxicity. Superseded in some settings by ECOG (simpler, 6 categories) or Palliative Performance Scale (PPS). Doesn't account for disease-specific symptoms.

entries.name: Lugano classification
entries.purpose: Lymphoma response assessment
entries.formula_human: PET-based or CT-based CR/PR/SD/PD per disease

entries.name: Milan criteria
entries.purpose: Liver transplant for HCC
entries.formula_human: Single <=5cm, or <=3 nodules each <=3cm, no extrahepatic/vascular spread

entries.name: Nottingham (Scarff-Bloom-Richardson)
entries.purpose: Breast cancer grade
entries.formula_human: Tubule formation + nuclear pleomorphism + mitotic count, each 1-3; sum 3-9; G1 3-5, G2 6-7, G3 8-9

entries.name: TNM (AJCC/UICC)
entries.purpose: Universal anatomical staging system for solid tumors, classifying by primary tumor extent (T), regional lymph node involvement (N), and distant metastasis (M).
entries.formula_human: Site-specific algorithms map T, N, M (and sometimes grade, biomarkers) to overall Stage 0, I, II, III, IV (with substages). Each cancer type has its own TNM definitions and stage groupings published in the AJCC Cancer Staging Manual, 8th edition (2017). This is a classification system, not a numerical formula.

inputs.label: T (Primary Tumor)
inputs.description: Size and extent of the primary tumor

inputs.label: N (Regional Lymph Nodes)
inputs.description: Extent of regional lymph node involvement

bands.meaning: Carcinoma in situ. Excellent prognosis.
Localized, small tumor. Good prognosis.
Locally advanced or larger tumor. Intermediate prognosis.
Regional lymph node involvement or locally advanced. Variable prognosis.
Distant metastases. Generally incurable (exceptions exist, e.g., oligometastatic disease).

citations.text: American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC). AJCC Cancer Staging Manual, 8th edition. New York: Springer; 2017. No single PMID — book/manual publication.

entries.copyright: licensed — verify before use (AJCC/UICC hold copyright; medical coding requires licensed access)
entries.limitations: Site-specific definitions are complex (>100 pages per cancer type in the full manual). Anatomical staging does not capture molecular markers (some cancers now have prognostic staging incorporating grade, PSA, biomarkers). Staging evolves (8th edition differs significantly from 7th). Some staging discrepancies between AJCC and UICC. Clinical staging (cTNM) vs pathological staging (pTNM) may differ. Imaging-dependent clinical staging can be inaccurate.

entries.name: Apgar score
entries.purpose: Rapid standardized assessment of newborn status at 1 and 5 minutes after birth. Guides need for resuscitation and predicts neonatal outcomes. APGAR is also a backronym: Appearance, Pulse, Grimace, Activity, Respiration.
entries.formula_human:
APGAR = Appearance (0–2) + Pulse (0–2) + Grimace (0–2) + Activity (0–2) + Respiration (0–2)
Scored at 1 minute and 5 minutes after birth
If 5-minute score <7, repeat every 5 minutes up to 20 minutes

inputs.label: Appearance (skin color)
inputs.options_text: Blue/pale all over=0, Body pink/extremities blue=1, Completely pink=2

inputs.label: Grimace (reflex irritability)
inputs.description: Response to stimulation (nasal catheter, foot slap)

inputs.label: Respiration
inputs.options_text: Absent=0, Irregular/weak cry=1, Strong cry/regular breathing=2

bands.meaning: Normal newborn transition — no intervention needed
Moderately depressed — may need stimulation, suctioning, oxygen, or positive-pressure ventilation
Severely depressed — immediate resuscitation (intubation, medications, chest compressions)
Good recovery — common and generally favorable prognosis
Associated with increased risk of neurological morbidity and neonatal mortality

citations.text: Apgar V. A proposal for a new method of evaluation of the newborn infant. Curr Res Anesth Analg. 1953;32(4):260-267. PMID: 13083014

entries.copyright: public domain — named after Virginia Apgar, Anesthesiologist
entries.limitations: Subjective — interobserver variability. APGAR affected by gestational age (preterm infants score lower), maternal medications (sedatives, anesthetics), and resuscitation interventions performed before scoring. Not designed to predict long-term neurological outcomes. A low score at 1 minute is common and not necessarily pathological. 5-minute score has better prognostic value. Doesn't guide specific resuscitation steps (NRP algorithm more useful). Not a substitute for blood gas analysis or clinical assessment of neonatal well-being. Score 7 doesn't distinguish between well-perfused and mildly compromised infants.

entries.name: FLACC
entries.purpose: Pediatric pain (non-verbal)
entries.formula_human: Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability each 0-2; total 0-10

entries.name: PEWS
entries.purpose: Identifies hospitalized children at risk of clinical deterioration requiring ICU transfer or escalation of care.
entries.formula_human: PEWS = Behavior(0–3) + Cardiovascular(0–3) + Respiratory(0–3). Different versions exist (Birmingham, Bristol, Canadian, etc.) with variable definitions.

inputs.label: Behavior
inputs.description: Playing/appropriate, sleeping, irritable/consolable, irritable/inconsolable, lethargic/confused/reduced response to pain

inputs.label: Cardiovascular
inputs.description: Color, heart rate, capillary refill time, blood pressure

inputs.label: Respiratory
inputs.description: Work of breathing, respiratory rate, oxygen requirement

bands.meaning: Low risk
Moderate risk; increase monitoring frequency, senior clinician review
High risk; urgent assessment; consider ICU transfer

citations.text: Duncan H, Hutchison J, Parshuram CS. The Pediatric Early Warning System score: a severity of illness score to predict urgent medical or ICU admission in hospitalized children. J Crit Care. 2006;21(3):271-278. PMID: 16952818

entries.limitations: Multiple versions exist with variable components and cutoffs (non-standardized). Requires nursing training. Inter-rater variability. Different performance in different pediatric populations. May not perform well in specialty populations (cardiac, oncology).

entries.name: Pediatric GCS
entries.purpose: Consciousness in children
entries.formula_human: Eye 1-4, Verbal modified <2y (5 coos/babbles... 2 inconsolable crying), Motor 1-6; total 3-15

entries.name: AUDIT
entries.purpose: 10-item WHO-developed screening tool for hazardous and harmful alcohol consumption, alcohol dependence, and alcohol-related problems. Validated worldwide for identifying the full spectrum of alcohol misuse.
entries.formula_human:
AUDIT = Sum of Q1 through Q10 (each 0–4)
Maximum = 40

Sub-scores:
Consumption (Q1–Q3): Hazardous drinking pattern
Dependence (Q4–Q6): Alcohol dependence markers
Harmful use (Q7–Q10): Alcohol-related problems

inputs.label: Q1: Frequency of drinking
inputs.description: How often do you have a drink containing alcohol?

inputs.label: Q2: Quantity per occasion
inputs.description: Standard drinks on a typical drinking day?

inputs.label: Q3: Frequency of heavy drinking
inputs.description: How often do you have 6+ drinks on one occasion?

inputs.label: Q4: Inability to stop drinking
inputs.description: How often found unable to stop drinking once started?

inputs.label: Q5: Failure to fulfill obligations
inputs.description: How often failed to meet expectations because of drinking?

inputs.label: Q6: Morning drinking
inputs.description: How often needed a first drink in the morning?

inputs.label: Q7: Guilt after drinking
inputs.description: How often felt guilt or remorse after drinking?

inputs.label: Q8: Blackouts
inputs.description: How often unable to remember what happened while drinking?

inputs.label: Q9: Injury from drinking
inputs.description: Have you or someone else been injured because of your drinking?
inputs.options_text: 0=No, 2=Yes but not in last year, 4=Yes during last year

inputs.label: Q10: Concerned by others
inputs.description: Has a relative/friend/doctor been concerned about your drinking?
inputs.options_text: 0=No, 2=Yes but not in last year, 4=Yes during last year

bands.meaning: Low risk (Zone I) — brief advice if indicated
Hazardous drinking (Zone II) — simple advice and monitoring
Harmful drinking (Zone III) — brief counseling and continued monitoring
Possible alcohol dependence (Zone IV) — referral for evaluation and treatment, possible medically managed withdrawal

citations.text: Babor TF, Higgins-Biddle JC, Saunders JB, Monteiro MG. AUDIT: The Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test: Guidelines for Use in Primary Care. 2nd ed. Geneva: WHO, 2001; Saunders JB, et al. Addiction. 1993;88:791-804

entries.copyright: free for clinical use — WHO copyright, released for open use
entries.limitations: Self-reported — underreporting is common, particularly in settings where alcohol use carries stigma. Standard drink definitions vary by country. Cultural variation in alcohol use norms and disclosure. Gender differences in risk thresholds (some use ≥6 for women vs ≥8 for men). AUDIT-C (consumption questions only, Q1–Q3) is faster but misses dependence and harm domains. May perform less well in elderly, pregnant, or medically ill populations. Doesn't quantify actual grams of ethanol consumed.

entries.name: BDI-II
entries.purpose: Depression severity (research)
entries.formula_human: 21 items x 0-3; total 0-63

entries.name: C-SSRS
entries.purpose: Structured clinician-administered interview for systematic assessment of suicidal ideation and behavior. Distinguishes between types of suicidal ideation (from passive to active with plan) and suicidal behaviors (actual attempt, interrupted attempt, aborted attempt, preparatory acts, self-injurious behavior without suicidal intent).
entries.formula_human:
No numerical total score — categorical assessment:
1. Identify highest type of suicidal ideation (1–5)
2. Assess intensity of ideation (frequency, duration, controllability, deterrents, reasons)
3. Assess lifetime and recent suicidal behavior (attempts, interrupted, aborted, preparatory)
4. Rate lethality of actual attempts (0=No physical damage to 5=Death)

inputs.label: Suicidal Ideation (Intensity)
inputs.description: 5 types of ideation: 1=Wish to be dead, 2=Nonspecific active thoughts, 3=Active ideation with any methods (not plan), 4=Active ideation with some intent, 5=Active ideation with specific plan and intent
inputs.options_text: Types 1–5 (cumulative: endorsement of 5 implies endorsement of 1–4)

inputs.label: Suicidal Ideation (Intensity subscale)
inputs.description: Frequency, duration, controllability, deterrents, reasons for ideation

inputs.label: Suicidal Behavior
inputs.note: Yes/No per behavior type; lethality of actual attempts rated 0–5

bands.meaning: Passive ideation (wish to be dead) — low-moderate risk, assess protective factors
Active ideation without intent/plan — moderate risk, safety planning, close follow-up
