Active ideation with intent or specific plan — high risk, immediate safety intervention, consider hospitalization
High risk regardless of current ideation type
Near-lethal attempt — high medical risk, intensive psychiatric intervention

citations.text: Posner K, Brown GK, Stanley B, et al. The Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale: initial validity and internal consistency findings from three multisite studies with adolescents and adults. Am J Psychiatry. 2011;168(12):1266-1277. PMID: 22193671

entries.copyright: Columbia University — free for clinical and research use with registration
entries.limitations: Clinician-administered — requires trained assessor. Not a risk prediction tool — assesses current and recent suicidal ideation/behavior but doesn't predict future attempts. Categorical, not numerical — doesn't generate a risk score. Distinction between types may be difficult in practice. Patient may not disclose ideation (minimization, fear of consequences). Doesn't capture psychosocial risk/protective factors, diagnosis, or treatment history. Abbreviated versions (screener, baseline/follow-up) may not capture full assessment detail. Cultural factors influence reporting of suicidality. Structured format may feel intrusive to some patients.

entries.name: CAGE
entries.purpose: Ultra-brief 4-item screening questionnaire for alcohol use disorder. Originally developed for detecting alcoholism. Simple to administer in any clinical setting.
entries.formula_human: CAGE = Number of 'Yes' answers (0–4)

bands.meaning: Low likelihood of alcohol dependence (but 1 may warrant further inquiry)
Positive screen for alcohol use disorder. Sensitivity 43–94%, specificity 70–96% at this threshold.
More sensitive than past-year questions
Strongly suggestive of alcohol dependence

citations.text: Ewing JA. Detecting alcoholism: the CAGE questionnaire. JAMA. 1984;252(14):1905-1907. PMID: 6471323

entries.limitations: Screening tool only — doesn't assess severity, quantity, or frequency. Binary yes/no doesn't capture nuance. Lower sensitivity for hazardous drinking (not just dependence). Questions are 'ever' — may detect past problems rather than current drinking. Doesn't distinguish between current and historical alcohol problems. Cultural sensitivity varies. Lower sensitivity in women, elderly, and non-white populations. Being 'annoyed by criticism' (A) may be less specific — could relate to other issues. Superseded by AUDIT and AUDIT-C for most screening purposes. Gender-neutral questions may miss gender-specific patterns of alcohol misuse.

entries.name: CIWA-Ar
entries.purpose: Validated 10-item scale for assessing severity of alcohol withdrawal and guiding benzodiazepine dosing.
entries.formula_human: CIWA-Ar = Sum of 10 items (maximum 67). Item 10 (orientation) max 4; all others max 7.

inputs.label: Tactile disturbances
inputs.description: Itching, pins/needles, burning, numbness, or bugs crawling on skin

inputs.label: Auditory disturbances
inputs.description: Sounds seem louder/softer, hearing things not there

inputs.label: Visual disturbances
inputs.description: Light sensitivity, blurred vision, seeing things not there

bands.meaning: Minimal withdrawal. May not need benzodiazepine.
Mild-moderate withdrawal. Symptom-triggered benzodiazepine dosing.
Moderate-severe withdrawal. More aggressive benzodiazepine management.
Severe withdrawal. High risk for seizures and DTs. Aggressive treatment and ICU monitoring.

citations.text: Sullivan JT, Sykora K, Schneiderman J, et al. Assessment of alcohol withdrawal: the revised clinical institute withdrawal assessment for alcohol scale (CIWA-Ar). Br J Addict. 1989;84(11):1353-1357. PMID: 2597811

entries.limitations: Requires patient cooperation (not valid if intubated, sedated, or uncooperative). Some items are subjective. Intermittent assessment (every 1–4 hours) — may miss rapid deterioration. Not validated in all populations (withdrawal severity varies by individual). Requires trained staff.

entries.name: EPDS
entries.purpose: 10-item self-report questionnaire specifically designed to screen for postnatal depression in the first year after delivery. Avoids somatic symptoms that overlap with normal postpartum experiences.
entries.formula_human:
EPDS = Sum of 10 items (each 0–3)
Maximum = 30
Some items are reverse-scored
Item 10 (self-harm thoughts) scored: 0=Never, 1=Hardly ever, 2=Sometimes, 3=Yes, quite often

inputs.label: 10 items about feelings in the past 7 days
inputs.description: Each item scored 0–3 based on frequency. Items: able to laugh, enjoyment, self-blame, anxiety/worry, fear/panic, things getting on top, difficulty sleeping (sadness), feeling sad/miserable, crying, self-harm thoughts
inputs.options_text: 0=No, not at all to 3=Yes, most of the time (for most items; some items reversed)

bands.meaning: Depression unlikely — standard postnatal care
Possible depression — repeat in 2 weeks, clinical assessment if persistent
Probable depression — clinical interview recommended, consider treatment referral
Any endorsement of self-harm thoughts requires immediate further assessment regardless of total score

citations.text: Cox JL, Holden JM, Sagovsky R. Detection of postnatal depression: development of the 10-item Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale. Br J Psychiatry. 1987;150:782-786. PMID: 3651732

entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published academic tool by Cox JL
entries.limitations: Screening tool, not diagnostic — positive screen requires clinical interview. Self-reported — may underreport symptoms due to stigma, fear of judgment, or normalization of symptoms. May miss atypical presentations of postpartum depression (anger, irritability, bonding difficulties). Somatic items excluded by design — but may miss depression primarily presenting with somatic symptoms. Threshold score debated (10, 11, 12, or 13 used in different studies). Doesn't distinguish postpartum depression from postpartum psychosis or anxiety disorders. Cultural variation in symptom expression. Not validated in antenatal populations (though used antenatally in practice). Doesn't assess social support, history of mental illness, or psychosocial risk factors.

entries.name: GAD-7
entries.purpose: Self-administered 7-item questionnaire for screening and severity measurement of generalized anxiety disorder. Also sensitive to panic disorder, social anxiety, and PTSD.
entries.formula_human:
GAD-7 = Sum of Q1 through Q7 (each 0–3)
Maximum = 21
GAD-2 (ultra-brief screening): Q1 + Q2 only (threshold ≥3)

inputs.label: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by:
inputs.options_text: 0=Not at all, 1=Several days, 2=More than half the days, 3=Nearly every day

inputs.label: Q1: Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge
Q2: Not being able to stop or control worrying
Q3: Worrying too much about different things
Q5: Being so restless that it's hard to sit still
Q6: Becoming easily annoyed or irritable
Q7: Feeling afraid as if something awful might happen

bands.meaning: Minimal anxiety
Mild anxiety
Moderate anxiety — consider treatment
Severe anxiety — active treatment recommended
Positive screen — proceed to full GAD-7

citations.text: Spitzer RL, Kroenke K, Williams JBW, Löwe B. A brief measure for assessing generalized anxiety disorder: the GAD-7. Arch Intern Med. 2006;166(10):1092-1097. PMID: 16717171

entries.copyright: free for clinical use — Pfizer developed, released for open use
entries.limitations: Screening tool, not diagnostic. Self-reported. Doesn't differentiate between specific anxiety disorders (GAD, panic, social anxiety, PTSD all score elevated). Somatic symptoms (restlessness, irritability) overlap with other psychiatric and medical conditions. Cultural variation in reporting anxiety symptoms. May underperform in severe mental illness (psychosis, bipolar mania). Doesn't capture avoidance behaviors or functional impairment. Recommended to use alongside structured clinical interview for diagnosis.

entries.name: HAM-D (17)
entries.purpose: Depression severity (research)
entries.formula_human: 17 items weighted; total 0-52; >=20 moderate-severe

entries.name: MADRS
entries.purpose: Clinician-rated 10-item depression severity scale designed to be more sensitive to treatment effects than HAM-D. Preferred in modern psychopharmacology trials for detecting change with antidepressants.
entries.formula_human:
MADRS = Sum of all 10 items (each 0–6)
Maximum = 60
Each item rated 0, 2, 4, or 6 (anchors defined) with 1, 3, 5 for intermediate severity

inputs.label: 8. Inability to feel
inputs.description: Emotional blunting, inability to feel pleasure

bands.meaning: Normal / Remission
Mild depression
Moderate depression
Severe depression
≥50% reduction from baseline
MADRS ≤10 (commonly used threshold)

citations.text: Montgomery SA, Asberg M. A new depression scale designed to be sensitive to change. Br J Psychiatry. 1979;134:382-389. PMID: 444788

entries.limitations: Clinician-rated — requires trained assessor (~10 minutes). Fewer somatic items than HAM-D (advantage in medically ill but may miss somatic depression). Subjective anchor points require calibration between raters. Not as extensively validated in community or primary care settings as HAM-D. Self-rated version (MADRS-S) exists but may not correspond exactly to clinician version. Limited content coverage — doesn't assess anxiety, agitation, or guilt as directly as HAM-D. Cut-off scores for severity categories vary across studies.

entries.name: MMSE
entries.purpose: Brief 30-point clinician-administered cognitive screening test for dementia. Assesses orientation, memory, attention, calculation, language, and visuospatial function. Most widely used cognitive screening tool globally.
entries.formula_human: MMSE = Sum of all items (0–30)

inputs.label: Orientation — Time
inputs.description: What is the (year, season, date, day, month)? (5 points)

inputs.label: Orientation — Place
inputs.description: Where are we (state, county, town, hospital, floor)? (5 points)

inputs.label: Registration
inputs.description: Name 3 objects, ask patient to repeat (3 points)

inputs.label: Attention and Calculation
inputs.description: Serial 7s (100-93-86-79-72) or spell WORLD backwards (5 points)

inputs.label: Recall
inputs.description: Recall the 3 objects from registration (3 points)

inputs.label: Language — Naming
inputs.description: Name a pencil and a watch (2 points)

inputs.label: Language — Repetition
inputs.description: Repeat 'No ifs, ands, or buts' (1 point)

inputs.label: Language — Three-stage command
inputs.description: Take paper in right hand, fold in half, place on floor (3 points)

inputs.label: Reading
inputs.description: Read and obey 'CLOSE YOUR EYES' (1 point)

bands.meaning: No cognitive impairment (normal range)
Mild cognitive impairment
Severe cognitive impairment
≤23 suggests impairment (general), but ≤20 for those with high school education, ≤25 for college-educated. Low education may give false positives, high education may give false negatives.

citations.text: Folstein MF, Folstein SE, McHugh PR. 'Mini-mental state'. A practical method for grading the cognitive state of patients for the clinician. J Psychiatr Res. 1975;12(3):189-198. PMID: 1202204

entries.copyright: PAR Inc (Psychological Assessment Resources) — requires paid license for most clinical/research uses since 2001
entries.limitations: Affected by education, age, culture, and language — different thresholds needed. Ceiling effect — not sensitive to mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Doesn't assess executive function well (limited frontal assessment). Motor component (pentagon copy) affected by visual/hearing impairment. Copyright held by PAR (Psychological Assessment Resources) — fee for clinical/research use since 2001. Serial 7s affected by math anxiety, education, and cultural factors. Doesn't capture rate of cognitive change (single time-point only). Superseded by MoCA for MCI screening in many guidelines. Depression may cause low scores (pseudodementia). Doesn't assess functional impact of cognitive impairment.

entries.name: MoCA
entries.purpose: Brief 30-point clinician-administered cognitive screening test designed to detect mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and early dementia. More sensitive than MMSE for MCI, with better executive function and attention assessment.
entries.formula_human:
MoCA = Visuospatial(5) + Naming(3) + Attention(6) + Language(3) + Abstraction(2) + Recall(5) + Orientation(6) = 30
+1 point added for ≤12 years of education (maximum score remains 30)

inputs.label: Visuospatial/Executive (5 points)
inputs.description: Trail-making test (alternating numbers and letters), cube copy, clock drawing

inputs.label: Naming (3 points)
inputs.description: Name lion, rhinoceros, camel from pictures

inputs.label: Memory (0 points, but tested for recall)
inputs.description: 5-word immediate and delayed recall (2 trials + delayed recall). Scored on recall section below.

inputs.label: Attention (6 points)
inputs.description: Forward/backward digit span, tapping on letter A (list read aloud), serial 7 subtraction

inputs.label: Language (3 points)
inputs.description: Repeat 2 sentences, fluency (name ≥11 words beginning with F in 1 minute)

inputs.label: Abstraction (2 points)
inputs.description: Similarities (e.g., train-bicycle = transportation; watch-ruler = measuring instrument)

inputs.label: Delayed Recall (5 points)
inputs.description: Recall the 5 words from earlier (free recall scored, with multiple-choice cue if needed)

inputs.label: Orientation (6 points)
inputs.description: Date, month, year, day, place, city

bands.meaning: Normal cognitive function
Mild cognitive impairment
Moderate cognitive impairment
Severe cognitive impairment
+1 point for ≤12 years of education (to reduce false positives in low-education populations)

citations.text: Nasreddine ZS, Phillips NA, Bédirian V, et al. The Montreal Cognitive Assessment, MoCA: a brief screening tool for mild cognitive impairment. J Am Geriatr Soc. 2005;53(4):695-699. PMID: 15817019

entries.copyright: Ziad Nasreddine — free for clinical and research use with registration at mocatest.org
entries.limitations: Takes ~10 minutes to administer — longer than MMSE. Education bias (partially addressed by +1 adjustment). Not suitable for telephone administration (requires visual/spatial components). Trail-making test and cube copy affected by motor impairment. Cultural and language adaptation needed for different populations. Copyright restrictions (www.mocatest.org — free for clinical use but registration required). May have floor effect in severe dementia. Serial 7s affected by math anxiety. May not be sensitive to very early or preclinical Alzheimer's. Higher false-positive rate in some populations (elderly without cognitive complaints).

entries.name: PANSS
entries.purpose: Schizophrenia symptoms
entries.formula_human: Positive 7 (7-49) + Negative 7 (7-49) + General 16 (16-112); total 30-210

entries.name: PHQ-9
entries.purpose: Self-administered 9-item questionnaire for screening, diagnosing, monitoring, and measuring severity of depression. Based on DSM-5 criteria. Most widely used depression screening tool in primary care and clinical practice.
entries.formula_human:
PHQ-9 = Sum of Q1 through Q9 (each 0–3)
Maximum = 27
PHQ-2 (ultra-brief screening): Q1 + Q2 only (threshold ≥3)

inputs.label: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by:
inputs.description: 9 items derived from DSM-5 major depressive disorder criteria
inputs.options_text: 0=Not at all, 1=Several days, 2=More than half the days, 3=Nearly every day

inputs.label: Q1: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
Q2: Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless
Q3: Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
Q4: Feeling tired or having little energy
Q6: Feeling bad about yourself or that you are a failure
Q8: Moving or speaking slowly/being fidgety/restless
Q9: Thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself

bands.meaning: Minimal or no depression
Mild depression — watchful waiting, repeat PHQ-9
Moderate depression — treatment plan (counseling, follow-up, pharmacotherapy)
Moderately severe depression — active treatment with pharmacotherapy and/or psychotherapy
Severe depression — immediate initiation of pharmacotherapy, referral for specialist care
Positive screen — proceed to full PHQ-9
Any positive response to suicidal ideation question requires further safety assessment regardless of total score

citations.text: Kroenke K, Spitzer RL, Williams JB. The PHQ-9: validity of a brief depression severity measure. J Gen Intern Med. 2001;16(9):606-613. PMID: 11556941

entries.copyright: free for clinical use — Pfizer developed, released for open use
entries.limitations: Screening tool, not diagnostic — positive screen requires clinical interview to confirm MDD. Self-reported — subject to response bias. May miss atypical depression presentations (hypersomnia, increased appetite). Somatic symptoms (sleep, appetite, energy) may be caused by medical conditions, not depression. Cultural variation in symptom expression and disclosure. Q9 (suicidality) positive response requires immediate clinical assessment — score alone doesn't guide safety management. Sensitivity ~88%, specificity ~88% at threshold ≥10 (varies by population). Does not assess bipolar disorder, psychotic depression, or anxiety disorders.

entries.name: YMRS
entries.purpose: Mania severity
entries.formula_human: 11 items; 7 x 0-4 + 4 x 0-8 (irritability, speech, thought content, disruptive behavior x2 weight); total 0-60

entries.name: CKD-EPI 2021 (race-free)
entries.purpose: Estimates glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) from serum creatinine without a race variable (replacing the 2009 version that included race).
entries.formula_human:
eGFR = 142 × min(Scr/κ, 1)^α × max(Scr/κ, 1)^(−1.200) × 0.9938^Age × (1.012 if female)

Where:
κ = 0.9 (male), 0.7 (female)
α = −0.302 (male), −0.241 (female)
min = minimum of Scr/κ or 1
max = maximum of Scr/κ or 1

eGFR in mL/min/1.73 m²

bands.meaning: Normal or high eGFR (G1)
Mildly decreased (G2). Kidney damage markers should be assessed.
Mildly to moderately decreased (G3a)
Moderately to severely decreased (G3b)
Severely decreased (G4)
Kidney failure (G5). Dialysis or transplant evaluation.

citations.text: Inker LA, Eneanya ND, Coresh J, et al. New creatinine- and cystatin C-based equations to estimate GFR without race. N Engl J Med. 2021;385(19):1737-1749. PMID: 34554658

entries.limitations: Less accurate at extremes of muscle mass (bodybuilders, amputees, malnourished). Not valid for patients on dialysis. Does not perform well in acute kidney injury (non-steady-state creatinine). Race variable was removed due to health equity concerns but may affect accuracy in some populations. All GFR estimating equations have ~90% accuracy within ±30% of measured GFR. Cystatin C-based or combined equations may be more accurate for some patients.

entries.name: Cockcroft-Gault
entries.purpose: CrCl for drug dosing
entries.formula_human: CrCl = (140-age)*weight(kg)*(0.85 if female)/(72*Scr mg/dL)

entries.name: FENa
entries.purpose: Prerenal vs intrinsic AKI
entries.formula_human: FENa = (UrineNa * SerumCr)/(SerumNa * UrineCr)*100; <1% prerenal/HRS, >2% ATN

entries.name: KDIGO AKI staging
entries.purpose: AKI diagnosis/staging
entries.formula_human: Stage1: Cr 1.5-1.9x baseline or +>=0.3 mg/dL; UOP<0.5 x6-12h. Stage2: Cr 2-2.9x; UOP<0.5 x>=12h. Stage3: Cr 3x, or >=4, or dialysis; UOP<0.3 x24h or anuria x12h

entries.name: 4Ts
entries.purpose: Pre-test clinical scoring system estimating the probability of HIT to guide diagnostic testing and management decisions.
entries.formula_human: 4Ts = Thrombocytopenia(0–2) + Timing(0–2) + Thrombosis(0–2) + Other_causes(0–2)

inputs.label: Thrombocytopenia
inputs.description: Degree of platelet count fall from baseline
inputs.options_text: 2 = >50% fall AND nadir ≥20K; 1 = 30–50% fall or nadir 10–19K; 0 = <30% fall or nadir <10K

inputs.label: Timing of platelet fall
inputs.description: Timing of platelet fall relative to heparin exposure
inputs.options_text: 2 = Days 5–10 onset (or ≤1 day if recent heparin in past 30 days); 1 = Day 5–10 (unclear) or >10 days; 0 = ≤4 days without recent exposure

inputs.label: Thrombosis or other sequelae
inputs.description: New thrombosis, skin necrosis, or acute systemic reaction after IV heparin bolus
inputs.options_text: 2 = new confirmed thrombosis or skin necrosis or acute systemic reaction; 1 = progressive/recurrent thrombosis or suspected thrombosis; 0 = none

inputs.label: Other causes of thrombocytopenia
inputs.description: Presence of other explanations for platelet fall
inputs.options_text: 2 = no other cause evident; 1 = possible other cause; 0 = definite other cause present

bands.meaning: Low probability of HIT (~5% positive HIT antibodies). HIT testing may not be needed.
Intermediate probability (~14%). Send HIT antibodies (PF4/heparin ELISA). If positive, confirm with functional assay.
High probability (~64%). Stop all heparin immediately. Start non-heparin anticoagulant (argatroban, bivalirudin). Send HIT antibodies urgently.

citations.text: Lo GK, Juhl D, Warkentin TE, et al. Evaluation of pretest clinical score (4 T's) for the diagnosis of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia in two clinical settings. J Thromb Haemost. 2006;4(4):759-765. PMID: 16634744

entries.limitations: Scoring requires careful clinical assessment (timing, alternative causes). Intermediate score (4–5) requires lab testing. Low scores do not completely exclude HIT (5% false negative). Not applicable to patients on heparin flushes only. Inter-rater variability possible. HIT antibody testing has high sensitivity but low specificity.

entries.name: A-a gradient
entries.purpose: Oxygenation defect
entries.formula_human: A-a = (713*FiO2) - PaCO2/0.8 - PaO2 (at sea level, on room air ~713*0.21)

entries.name: CAT
entries.purpose: Patient-reported questionnaire to quantify COPD symptom burden (8 items scored 0–5 each).
entries.formula_human: CAT = sum of all 8 items (each 0–5)

inputs.label: Phlegm
inputs.description: How much phlegm do you have in your chest?

inputs.label: Chest tightness
inputs.description: How tight does your chest feel?

inputs.label: Breathlessness walking up hills/one flight
inputs.description: Do you get breathless walking up a hill or one flight of stairs?

inputs.label: Activity limitation
inputs.description: Are you limited in activities at home?

inputs.label: Confidence leaving home
inputs.description: How confident are you leaving home despite lung condition?

bands.meaning: Low symptom burden (GOLD Group A: low risk, low symptoms)
Medium symptom burden (GOLD Group B or E)
High symptom burden (GOLD Group E if exacerbation history). Consider escalation of bronchodilator therapy.

citations.text: Jones PW, Harding G, Berry P, et al. Development and first validation of the COPD Assessment Test. Eur Respir J. 2009;34(3):648-654. PMID: 19720809

entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app (copyright by GlaxoSmithKline)
entries.limitations: Patient-reported (subjective, subject to mood and recall bias). CAT is affected by comorbidities (e.g., heart failure, anxiety). Does not capture lung function or exacerbation history. Minimum clinically important difference (MCID) = 2 points. Not a diagnostic tool. Designed for stable COPD, not acute exacerbations.

entries.name: CURB-65
entries.purpose: Predicts 30-day mortality in community-acquired pneumonia to guide site-of-care decision (outpatient vs inpatient vs ICU).
entries.formula_human: CURB-65 = Confusion(1) + Urea>7(1) + RR≥30(1) + BP_low(1) + Age≥65(1)

inputs.label: Confusion
inputs.description: New-onset confusion (abbreviated mental test score ≤8 or equivalent)

inputs.label: Urea >7 mmol/L (>20 mg/dL)
inputs.description: Blood urea nitrogen >20 mg/dL or urea >7 mmol/L

inputs.label: Respiratory rate ≥30/min
inputs.description: Respiratory rate 30 breaths per minute or higher

inputs.label:
Blood pressure (SBP

<90 or DBP ≤60)
inputs.description: Systolic BP <90 mmHg or diastolic BP ≤60 mmHg

bands.meaning: Low risk (mortality ~0.6–2.7%). Consider outpatient management.
Moderate risk (~6.8–9.2%). Consider short inpatient stay or supervised outpatient treatment.
High risk (~14–40%+). Inpatient admission; consider ICU for score 4–5.

citations.text: Lim WS, van der Eerden MM, Laing R, et al. Defining community acquired pneumonia severity on presentation to hospital: an international derivation and validation study. Thorax. 2003;58(5):377-382. PMID: 12728155

entries.limitations: Does not include oxygenation status, bilateral infiltrates, or pleural effusion. May underestimate severity in younger patients without other risk factors. No direct inclusion of comorbidities. CRB-65 (without urea) is a bedside alternative. Single threshold for BP may miss patients with relative hypotension.

entries.name: Epworth Sleepiness Scale
entries.purpose: Daytime sleepiness
entries.formula_human: 8 situations x 0-3; total 0-24; >=11 abnormal

entries.name: GOLD ABE assessment
entries.purpose: COPD management groups
entries.formula_human: A: 0-1 exacerbation, mMRC 0-1/CAT<10; B: 0-1 exacerbation, mMRC>=2/CAT>=10; E: >=2 moderate or >=1 severe exacerbation

entries.name: Light's criteria
entries.purpose: Transudate vs exudate
entries.formula_human: Exudate if >=1: pleural/serum protein >0.5, pleural/serum LDH >0.6, pleural LDH > 2/3 upper limit normal serum LDH

entries.name: Oxygenation Index
entries.purpose: Pediatric/ventilator oxygenation
entries.formula_human: OI = mean airway pressure * FiO2 / PaO2 * 100

entries.name: P/F ratio
entries.purpose: Oxygenation (Berlin ARDS)
entries.formula_human: PaO2/FiO2: mild 200-300, moderate 100-200, severe <=100

entries.name: PERC
entries.purpose: Identifies low-risk ED patients in whom PE can be safely excluded without D-dimer testing.
entries.formula_human:
PERC: All 8 criteria must be negative (and patient must be low risk by gestalt). Any single criterion positive = PERC fails. PERC negative = PE ruled out without D-dimer.
PERC fail rate = number of positive criteria / 8

inputs.label: No surgery/trauma within 4 weeks
inputs.description: No recent surgery or trauma requiring hospitalization

bands.meaning: PE effectively excluded (<2% missed PE). No further testing needed.
PERC fails. Proceed to D-dimer and/or imaging based on clinical probability.

citations.text: Kline JA, Mitchell AM, Kabrhel C, et al. Clinical criteria to prevent unnecessary diagnostic testing in emergency department patients with suspected pulmonary embolism. J Thromb Haemost. 2004;2(8):1247-1255. PMID: 15304025

entries.limitations: Only applicable to low-risk patients (must first determine low clinical suspicion). Not valid in high-prevalence settings. D-dimer testing is inexpensive and readily available — some clinicians prefer testing over PERC. Missed PE rate ~1-2% (not zero). Should not override strong clinical suspicion.

entries.name: Pneumonia Severity Index (PORT)
entries.purpose: CAP mortality (discriminative)
entries.formula_human: 2-step: age+comorbid + 20-item points table -> risk class I-V

entries.name: Revised Geneva (simplified)
entries.purpose: Pre-test probability PE (rule-based)
entries.formula_human: Age>65=1, prior DVT/PE=1, surgery/fracture=1, cancer=1, unilateral leg pain=1, hemoptysis=1, HR 75-94=1, >=95=2, unilateral edema+pain=1; 0-12; >=11 high? (commonly 0-3 low, 4-10 intermediate, 11-12 high)

entries.name: STOP-Bang
entries.purpose: Screens for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) risk in surgical and general populations.
entries.formula_human: STOP-BANG = Snoring(1) + Tired(1) + Observed_apnea(1) + Pressure_HTN(1) + BMI>35(1) + Age>50(1) + Neck>40cm(1) + Male(1)

inputs.label: Snoring
inputs.description: Do you snore loudly (louder than talking or heard through closed doors)?

inputs.label: Tiredness
inputs.description: Do you often feel tired, fatigued, or sleepy during the daytime?

inputs.label: Observed apnea
inputs.description: Has anyone observed you stop breathing during sleep?

inputs.label: Pressure (hypertension)
inputs.description: Are you being treated for high blood pressure?

bands.meaning: Low risk of OSA (AHI <5: sensitivity 34–70%)
Intermediate risk (AHI ≥5: sensitivity 70–88%)
High risk of OSA (AHI ≥30: sensitivity 75–90%). Polysomnography recommended.

citations.text: Chung F, Yegneswaran B, Liao P, et al. STOP questionnaire: a tool to screen patients for obstructive sleep apnea. Anesthesiology. 2008;108(5):812-821. PMID: 18431116; Chung F, et al. Anesthesiology. 2012;116:895-904 (STOP-BANG)

entries.limitations: Sensitivity varies by AHI threshold — good for ruling out severe OSA but may miss moderate OSA. Specificity is modest (many false positives in surgical populations). Age >50 and male sex are non-modifiable risk factors that increase score in many surgical patients. Does not replace polysomnography for diagnosis. BMI cutoff >35 may be too high for Asian populations (>25–30 may be more appropriate).

entries.name: Wells PE
entries.purpose: Clinical prediction rule estimating pretest probability of pulmonary embolism to guide diagnostic workup.
entries.formula_human: Wells PE = DVT_signs(3) + PE_most_likely(3) + HR>100(1.5) + Immobilization_surgery(1.5) + Prior_VTE(1.5) + Hemoptysis(1) + Malignancy(1)

inputs.label: Clinical signs/symptoms of DVT
inputs.description: Leg swelling, pain with palpation of deep veins

inputs.label: PE is #1 diagnosis or equally likely
inputs.description: PE is the most likely diagnosis based on clinical judgment

inputs.label: Immobilization ≥3 days or surgery within 4 weeks
Active malignancy
inputs.description: Cancer treated within 6 months or palliative

bands.meaning: PE unlikely (prevalence ~3–8%). Consider D-dimer; if negative, PE effectively excluded.
PE likely (prevalence ~20–40%). Proceed to CT pulmonary angiography or V/Q scan.

citations.text: Wells PS, Anderson DR, Rodger M, et al. Derivation of a simple clinical model to categorize patients probability of pulmonary embolism: increasing the models utility with the SimpliRED D-dimer. Thromb Haemost. 2000;83(3):416-420. PMID: 10744147

entries.limitations: Subjective component ('PE most likely diagnosis'). D-dimer needed to safely rule out PE in low-risk patients. Less accurate in elderly, pregnant, and cancer patients. Requires imaging for high-risk patients. Various modifications exist (original 3-level vs simplified 2-level).

entries.name: YEARS algorithm
entries.purpose: Stepwise diagnostic algorithm for PE combining Wells-like items with D-dimer thresholds to reduce unnecessary imaging.
entries.formula_human:
YEARS items = DVT signs + Hemoptysis + PE most likely.

Step 1: Count YEARS items (0, 1, 2, or 3 positive).
Step 2: If 0 YEARS items → PE excluded if D-dimer <1000 ng/L.
If 1–3 YEARS items → PE excluded if D-dimer <500 ng/L.
If D-dimer above threshold → proceed to CTPA.

bands.meaning: PE ruled out. No imaging needed.
PE ruled out. No imaging needed.
Proceed to CTPA.

citations.text: van der Hulle T, Cheung WY, Kooij S, et al. Simplified diagnostic management of suspected pulmonary embolism (the YEARS study): a prospective, multicentre, cohort study. Lancet. 2017;390(10091):289-297. PMID: 28629698

entries.limitations: Higher D-dimer threshold (1000 ng/L) may cause concern for missing PE — absolute miss rate ~0.5%. Validated primarily in the Netherlands — external validation needed. Subjective 'PE most likely' item. Not applicable to pregnant patients. CTPA rate reduction ~14% vs conventional approaches.

entries.name: mMRC
entries.purpose: Grades breathlessness severity in COPD for symptom assessment and GOLD classification.
entries.formula_human: Single categorical grade 0–4 based on patient-reported dyspnea

inputs.label: Dyspnea grade
inputs.description: Breathlessness level based on activities that provoke dyspnea
inputs.options_text: 0 = breathless only with strenuous exercise; 1 = short of breath hurrying on level ground or walking up a slight hill; 2 = walks slower than people of same age due to breathlessness or stops for breath when walking at own pace; 3 = stops for breath after walking 100 yards or after a few minutes on level ground; 4 = too breathless to leave house or breathless when dressing/undressing

bands.meaning: Less breathless (GOLD Group A or B low symptom threshold). COPD Assessment Test <10 correlates with mMRC <2.
More breathless. Used in GOLD classification as threshold for symptom assessment (mMRC ≥2 = more symptomatic, GOLD Group B or E).

citations.text: Bestall JC, Paul EA, Garrod R, et al. Usefulness of the Medical Research Council (MRC) dyspnoea scale as a measure of disability in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Thorax. 1999;54(7):581-586. PMID: 10343635

entries.limitations: Very simple single-item scale — may miss nuanced symptom differences. Threshold of ≥2 for 'more symptomatic' is arbitrary and doesn't capture all clinically significant breathlessness. CAT ≥10 is more sensitive. Patient-reported and subjective. Doesn't capture daily variability in symptoms.

entries.name: ACR/EULAR Boolean remission
entries.purpose: RA remission (treat-to-target)
entries.formula_human: TJC<=1 AND SJC<=1 AND CRP<=1 AND PtGA<=1

entries.name: ASDAS-CRP
entries.purpose: AxSpA activity (preferred)
entries.formula_human: ASDAS = 0.12*BASDAI-Q5(back pain) + 0.06*PtGlobal + 0.11*peripheral pain/swelling + 0.07*morning stiffness + 0.11*ln(CRP+1); ASDAS-ESR: 0.08*BP + 0.07*MD + 0.11*PP + 0.09*MS + 0.29*sqrt(ESR)

entries.name: BASDAI
entries.purpose: Patient-reported disease activity measure for ankylosing spondylitis and axial spondyloarthritis. Assesses fatigue, spinal pain, peripheral joint pain, enthesitis, and morning stiffness.
entries.formula_human:
BASDAI = (Q1 + Q2 + Q3 + Q4 + (Q5+Q6)/2) / 5
Mean of 5 components (Q5 and Q6 averaged before inclusion since both measure morning stiffness)

inputs.label: Q1: Fatigue/tiredness
inputs.description: How much fatigue/tiredness have you had?

inputs.label: Q2: Neck/back/hip pain
inputs.description: How much pain/stiffness in neck, back, or hips?

inputs.label: Q3: Peripheral joint pain/swelling
inputs.description: How much pain/swelling in joints other than neck/back/hips?

inputs.label: Q4: Enthesitis
inputs.description: How much tenderness/pain at insertion of tendons/ligaments (excluding hips)?

inputs.label: Q5: Severity of morning stiffness
inputs.description: How severe is your morning stiffness from awakening?

inputs.label: Q6: Duration of morning stiffness
inputs.description: How long does your morning stiffness last from awakening?

bands.meaning: Low disease activity / inactive disease
Active disease — commonly used threshold for biologic initiation in AS
Minimum clinically important improvement

citations.text: Garrett S, Jenkinson T, Kennedy LG, et al. A new approach to defining disease status in ankylosing spondylitis: the Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI). J Rheumatol. 1994;21(12):2286-2291. PMID: 7699630

entries.copyright: free for clinical use — University of Bath
entries.limitations: Patient-reported — subjective and may not correlate with imaging (MRI inflammation, radiographic damage). Fatigue and morning stiffness components less specific for axSpA. BASDAI ≥4 threshold for biologic therapy criticized as arbitrary (BASDAI can be elevated in fibromyalgia, depression, mechanical back pain). Not sensitive to change in mild disease. ASDAS (incorporating CRP/ESR) preferred for objective assessment. Peripheral spondyloarthritis may not be well captured.

entries.name: CDAI
entries.purpose: Simplified disease activity index for RA that does not require acute phase reactants (ESR/CRP). Purely clinical assessment allowing rapid point-of-care evaluation.
entries.formula_human: CDAI = TJC28 + SJC28 + Patient Global (0–10) + Physician Global (0–10)

inputs.label: Tender Joint Count (TJC28)
inputs.description: Number of tender joints out of 28

inputs.label: Swollen Joint Count (SJC28)
inputs.description: Number of swollen joints out of 28

bands.meaning: Remission
Low disease activity
Moderate disease activity
High disease activity

citations.text: Aletaha D, Nell VP, Stamm T, et al. Acute phase reactants add little to composite disease activity indices for rheumatoid arthritis: validation of a clinical activity score. Arthritis Res Ther. 2005;7(4):R796-R806. PMID: 15987482

entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published academic tool
entries.limitations: Relies on physician and patient global assessments which are subjective. Joint counts require training to perform reliably. Less sensitive to change than DAS28 in some studies. CDAI remission (≤2.8) corresponds closely to Boolean remission but may not capture residual subclinical synovitis.

entries.name: DAS28-ESR
entries.purpose: RA disease activity
entries.formula_human: DAS28 = 0.56*sqrt(TJC28) + 0.28*sqrt(SJC28) + 0.70*ln(ESR) + 0.014*PtGlobal(mm); <2.6 remission, <3.2 low, 3.2-5.1 moderate, >5.1 high

entries.name: EASI
entries.purpose: Atopic eczema severity
entries.formula_human: Region score (erythema+edema+excoriation+lichenification 0-3 each) x area (0-6) x multiplier (0.1 head, 0.2 upper, 0.3 trunk, 0.4 lower); total 0-72

entries.name: PASI
entries.purpose: Gold-standard clinician-assessed composite measure of psoriasis severity incorporating area involvement and lesion characteristics. Used as primary endpoint in clinical trials for biologic and systemic psoriasis therapies.
entries.formula_human:
For each region: (Erythema + Induration + Desquamation) × Area × BSA weight
PASI = 0.1 × (Head sum) + 0.2 × (Upper extremity sum) + 0.3 × (Trunk sum) + 0.4 × (Lower extremity sum)

Each region sum = (E+I+D) × Area score
Maximum = 72

inputs.label: Body regions
inputs.description: 4 body regions: Head (10% BSA), Upper extremities (20% BSA), Trunk (30% BSA), Lower extremities (40% BSA)

bands.meaning: No psoriasis
Mild psoriasis
Moderate psoriasis
Moderate-to-severe psoriasis
Severe psoriasis
75% improvement from baseline — standard primary endpoint in clinical trials
90% improvement — emerging preferred endpoint (near-complete clearance)
100% improvement — complete clearance

citations.text: Fredriksson T, Pettersson U. Severe psoriasis — oral therapy with a new retinoid. Dermatologica. 1978;157(4):238-244. PMID: 357213

entries.limitations: Clinician-assessed — requires training, time (10–15 minutes), and has interobserver variability (kappa ~0.5–0.7 for PASI 75 response). Difficult to assess intertriginous areas, scalp, and palms/soles accurately. Low sensitivity to change at mild end (PASI <5) — ceiling effect for mild disease. Weighted toward lower extremities (40% weight) — may not reflect patient's most bothersome areas. Doesn't capture pruritus, nail involvement, or quality of life impact. Body surface area estimation by clinician is subjective. PASI 50 and PASI 75 are dichotomous endpoints — patients with 74% improvement score as failures.

entries.name: SDAI
entries.purpose: Composite RA disease activity index similar to CDAI but includes CRP. Slightly more robust than CDAI due to inclusion of acute phase reactant.
entries.formula_human: SDAI = TJC28 + SJC28 + Patient Global (0–10) + Physician Global (0–10) + CRP (mg/dL)

inputs.label: Tender Joint Count (TJC28)
inputs.description: Number of tender joints out of 28

inputs.label: Swollen Joint Count (SJC28)
inputs.description: Number of swollen joints out of 28

bands.meaning: Remission
Low disease activity
Moderate disease activity
High disease activity

citations.text: Smolen JS, Breedveld FC, Schiff MH, et al. A simplified disease activity index for rheumatoid arthritis for use in clinical practice. Rheumatology (Oxford). 2003;42(2):244-257. PMID: 12595618

entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published academic tool
entries.limitations: Requires CRP measurement — though simple, adds one more lab test compared to CDAI. CRP units must be in mg/dL for formula (conversion needed if reported in mg/L). Subjective global assessments. Remission threshold (≤3.3) validated against Boolean remission and structural outcomes.

entries.name: ASA Physical Status
entries.purpose: Pre-anesthesia comorbidity class
entries.formula_human: I healthy, II mild systemic, III severe systemic, IV life-threatening, V moribund, VI brain-dead donor

entries.name: NSQIP risk calculators
entries.purpose: Surgical complication risk (US)
entries.formula_human: ACS NSQIP logistic models (30-day mortality/morbidity)

entries.name: Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS)
entries.purpose: Standardized tool for assessing and documenting level of consciousness. Originally developed for traumatic brain injury assessment but now used universally in emergency medicine, critical care, neurology, and prehospital care. Provides reproducible measurement of consciousness level for triage, prognostication, and clinical decision-making.
entries.formula_human:
GCS = E + V + M
Range: 3–15

Best response should be recorded for each component. If asymmetric, record best response.

Intubated patients: Record E and M. Verbal component recorded as '1T' (intubated). Do not estimate verbal score in intubated patients.

bands.meaning: Fully alert and oriented.
Mild brain injury (in TBI context). Alert with minor confusion or only minor verbal deficit.
Moderate brain injury. Requires close monitoring. CT imaging indicated.
Severe brain injury. Coma. Intubation usually indicated (GCS ≤8 = 'intubate'). Airway management critical.
Deep coma/unresponsive. Most severe possible. Poor prognosis.

citations.text: Teasdale G, Jennett B. Assessment of coma and impaired consciousness. A practical scale. Lancet. 1974;2(7872):81-84. PMID: 4136544; Teasdale G, Jennett B. Acta Neurochir Suppl (Wien). 1979;28:13-16

entries.limitations: Subjective assessment for some responses (verbal and motor scoring can vary). Inter-rater variability (especially V and M components). Does not assess pupil reactivity, brainstem reflexes, or focal neurological deficits. Not validated in children </think>�<2 years (use Pediatric GCS or AVPU). Confounded by sedation, paralysis, intoxication, intubation. Does not capture specific injury patterns (focal vs. diffuse). The FOUR Score is preferred in ICU for intubated patients (separates eye and motor responses from verbal). GCS 3 (minimum) is a category, not a single value (heterogeneous). Should be supplemented with pupil reactivity for prognostication. Not suitable for chronic consciousness assessment (use JFK Coma Recovery Scale). 15-point scale may have gaps (GCS 14 patients are heterogeneous). Motor component is most prognostically important — consider using M alone for rapid triage.

entries.name: Injury Severity Score (ISS)
entries.purpose: Quantifies overall injury severity in trauma patients using the Abbreviated Injury Scale across six body regions.
entries.formula_human: ISS = sum of squares of the three highest AIS scores from three different body regions (choose the 3 most severe among 6 regions). ISS = AIS₁² + AIS₂² + AIS₃². Each AIS is coded 1–6.

inputs.label: Head/Neck AIS
inputs.description: Abbreviated Injury Scale score for head and neck region

inputs.label: Abdomen/Pelvis AIS
inputs.description: AIS for abdomen and pelvic contents

inputs.label: Extremities/Pelvis AIS
inputs.description: AIS for extremities and pelvic girdle

bands.meaning: Minor injury
Moderate injury
Severe injury
Serious injury
Major polytrauma; significantly increased mortality
Maximum score (any AIS 6 automatically = 75)

citations.text: Baker SP, O'Neill B, Haddon W Jr, Long WB. The injury severity score: a method for describing patients with multiple injuries and evaluating emergency care. J Trauma. 1974;14(3):187-196. PMID: 4814394

entries.copyright: licensed — verify before use (AIS is copyrighted by the Association for the Advancement of Automotive Medicine)
entries.limitations: Only uses three of six body regions — may miss injury in excluded regions. Does not account for age or comorbidities. AIS coding requires trained specialists. Cannot distinguish between single-region and multi-region injuries with same score. Age-adjusted ISS and New ISS (NISS) address some limitations.

entries.name: Caprini score
entries.purpose: Surgical VTE risk
entries.formula_human: 40+ factors weighted 1-5 (age 41-60=1, 61-74=2, >=75=3; prior VTE 3; thrombophilia 3; major open surgery 2...); 0 low, 1-2 mod, 3-4 high, >=5 highest

entries.name: Padua score
entries.purpose: Medical inpatient VTE risk
entries.formula_human: Active cancer 3, prior VTE 3, reduced mobility 3, known thrombophilia 3, recent surgery/trauma 2, age>=70 1, HF/resp failure 1, MI/ischemic stroke 1, acute infection/rheum disease 1, obesity 1, hormonal Rx 1; total 0-20? (max 21); >=4 high

entries.name: Wells DVT
entries.purpose: Clinical prediction rule estimating pretest probability of DVT to guide diagnostic imaging (compression ultrasonography).
entries.formula_human: Wells DVT = Cancer(1) + Paralysis(1) + Bedridden_surgery(1) + Tenderness(1) + Entire_leg_swollen(1) + Calf_swelling≥3cm(1) + Pitting_edema(1) + Collateral_veins(1) + Prior_DVT(1) + Alternative_dx(−2)

inputs.label: Bedridden >3 days or major surgery within 12 weeks
Localized tenderness along deep venous system
Calf swelling ≥3 cm compared to asymptomatic side
Alternative diagnosis at least as likely as DVT

bands.meaning: Low probability (~5% DVT prevalence). D-dimer can rule out if negative.
Moderate probability (~17%). D-dimer or ultrasound.
High probability (~53%). Proceed directly to compression ultrasonography.

citations.text: Wells PS, Hirsh J, Anderson DR, et al. Accuracy of clinical assessment of deep-vein thrombosis. Lancet. 1995;345(8961):1326-1330. PMID: 7752753

entries.limitations: Subjective component ('alternative diagnosis'). D-dimer has lower specificity in elderly, post-surgical, and hospitalized patients. Calf swelling measurement requires comparison with contralateral leg. Not validated in inpatients.

entries.name: Base excess
entries.purpose: Acid-base status
entries.formula_human: BE = (HCO3 - 24) + [0.14*(40 - PaCO2)? ] standard formula by blood gas analyzer

entries.name: Renal failure index / UOP
entries.purpose: (see renal)

entries.name: Serum osmolality
entries.purpose: Calculated osmolality
entries.formula_human: 2*Na + glucose/18 + BUN/2.8

entries.name: ABI / Rutherford / Fontaine / WIfI
entries.purpose: Non-invasive measurement of lower extremity arterial perfusion relative to upper extremity blood pressure. Used for diagnosis and severity assessment of peripheral arterial disease (PAD). ABI = systolic BP at ankle / systolic BP at arm (higher of two arms).
entries.formula_human:
Right ABI = Higher ankle BP (right) / Higher arm BP
Left ABI = Higher ankle BP (left) / Higher arm BP

ABI = max(DP systolic, PT systolic) / max(Right brachial, Left brachial)

Note: If ABI >1.40, consider calcification (non-compressible arteries) — perform toe-brachial index (TBI).

inputs.label: Right ankle systolic BP
inputs.description: Higher of dorsalis pedis or posterior tibial artery systolic BP measured by Doppler

inputs.label: Left ankle systolic BP
inputs.description: Higher of dorsalis pedis or posterior tibial artery systolic BP measured by Doppler

inputs.label: Right brachial systolic BP
inputs.description: Systolic BP in right brachial artery measured by Doppler

inputs.label: Left brachial systolic BP
inputs.description: Systolic BP in left brachial artery measured by Doppler

bands.meaning: Non-compressible arteries (calcification). Consider TBI. Associated with diabetes, CKD, elderly.
Normal. No PAD.
Borderline. Possible PAD — further evaluation with exercise ABI if symptomatic.
Mild-to-moderate PAD. Claudication expected.
Severe PAD. Critical limb ischemia (CLI) likely. Rest pain, tissue loss.
Rutherford category 5–6 / Fontaine stage IV. Limb-threatening ischemia.

citations.text: Aboyans V, et al. 2017 ESC Guidelines on the Diagnosis and Treatment of Peripheral Arterial Diseases. Eur Heart J. 2018;39(9):763-816; AHA/ACC Guidelines on Management of PAD (2016)

entries.copyright: ESC/AHA Guidelines — free for clinical use
entries.limitations: Falsely elevated ABI (>1.40) in diabetes, CKD, and elderly due to medial calcinosis (non-compressible tibial arteries). Measurement technique-dependent (Doppler probe angle, cuff width). ABI </think>�<0.90 has high specificity but moderate sensitivity for angiographically significant stenosis. Does not localize level of disease. Exercise ABI more sensitive for mild disease. Toe-brachial index (TBI) better for patients with calcified arteries. Does not distinguish claudication from other causes of leg pain. Bilateral PAD may affect brachial BP (subclavian stenosis). Reproducibility affected by operator experience. Not validated as screening in asymptomatic low-risk populations. ABI has independent prognostic value for cardiovascular events (MI, stroke, CV death). ABI ≤0.90 associated with 2–3x increased cardiovascular mortality. Not applicable to acute limb ischemia (different assessment needed).

entries.name: ATRIA stroke
entries.purpose: AF stroke risk
entries.formula_human: CHF=1, HTN=1, DM=1, Vascular disease=1, Age>=75=2? (weighting: age 65-74=2? published: age>75=2? ) components with published weights; total 0-13

entries.name: CHA2DS2-VA
entries.purpose: ESC variant (sex removed)
entries.formula_human: CHA2DS2-VASc minus female sex; 0-8

entries.name: CHADS2
entries.purpose: Predecessor to CHA₂DS₂-VASc; estimates stroke risk in atrial fibrillation patients to guide anticoagulation.
entries.formula_human: CHADS₂ = CHF(1) + Hypertension(1) + Age_≥75(1) + Diabetes(1) + Stroke/TIA(2)

bands.meaning: Low risk. Annual stroke rate ~1.9%. Consider aspirin or no therapy.
Low-intermediate risk. Annual stroke rate ~2.8%. Consider anticoagulation.
Moderate-high risk. Annual stroke rate 4.0–18.2%. Anticoagulation recommended.

citations.text: Gage BF, Waterman AD, Shannon W, et al. Validation of clinical classification schemes for predicting stroke: results from the National Registry of Atrial Fibrillation. JAMA. 2001;285(22):2864-2870. PMID: 11401607

entries.limitations: Largely superseded by CHA₂DS₂-VASc. Score of 0 has limited discriminative ability — CHA₂DS₂-VASc better identifies truly low-risk patients. Does not include vascular disease, age 65–74, or sex. C-statistic ~0.6–0.7.

entries.name: Duke Treadmill Score
entries.purpose: Risk stratifies patients undergoing exercise stress testing for coronary artery disease severity and prognosis.
entries.formula_human: DTS = Exercise_time − (5 × ST_deviation) − (4 × Angina_index)

inputs.label: Exercise time
inputs.description: Duration of exercise on standard Bruce protocol

inputs.label: Maximum ST-segment deviation
inputs.description: Maximum ST elevation or depression during exercise or recovery

inputs.label: Angina index
inputs.options_text: 0 = no angina; 1 = non-limiting angina; 2 = exercise-limiting angina

bands.meaning: Low risk: 4-year survival ~99%; annual mortality <0.5%
Moderate risk: 4-year survival ~95%; annual mortality ~1%
High risk: 4-year survival ~79%; annual mortality ~5%

citations.text: Mark DB, Shaw L, Harrell FE Jr, et al. Prognostic value of a treadmill exercise score in outpatients with suspected coronary artery disease. N Engl J Med. 1991;325(12):849-853. PMID: 1875969

entries.limitations: Requires formal exercise testing (not applicable to patients who cannot exercise). Based on standard Bruce protocol; other protocols require conversion. Not validated with stress imaging modalities. Pre-dates routine use of coronary CTA.

entries.name: GARFIELD-AF
entries.purpose: AF stroke/mortality risk
entries.formula_human: Registry-derived weighted model; includes age, BMI, BP, smoking, bleeding, alcohol, prior events

entries.name: ORBIT bleeding
entries.purpose: AF bleeding risk
entries.formula_human: Age>=75=1, Reduced Hb/Hct=2, Bleeding history=2, Renal impairment=1, Antiplatelet use=1; total 0-7

entries.name: SAMe-TT2R2
entries.purpose: Predicts which patients with AF on warfarin will have poor anticoagulation control (time in therapeutic range <65%), helping decide between warfarin and DOAC.
entries.formula_human: SAMe-TT₂R₂ = Sex_female(1) + Age<60(1) + Medical_history>2(1) + Treatment_interacting(1) + Tobacco(2) + Race_nonWhite(2)

inputs.label: Medical history (>2 comorbidities)
inputs.description: More than 2 comorbidities (hypertension, DM, CAD, PAD, CHF, stroke, hepatic/renal disease, etc.)

inputs.label: Treatment (interacting medications)
inputs.description: Use of interacting drugs (amiodarone, anticonvulsants, rifampin, etc.)

bands.meaning: Good TTR likely; warfarin is a reasonable option.
Poor TTR predicted; consider DOAC instead of warfarin.

citations.text: Lip GYH, Hagerty T, Haynes B, et al. Thromb Haemost. 2015;114(6):1242-1248. PMID: 26354844 (concept from Apostolakis S, et al. J Thromb Haemost. 2013;11:365-372)

entries.limitations: Race/ethnicity category is a crude variable with significant heterogeneity. Developed in warfarin-era; with increasing DOAC use, the tool's clinical utility may be decreasing. Score of 2 for non-White race may be seen as ethically problematic.

entries.name: SYNTAX / SYNTAX II
entries.purpose: Quantifies coronary artery disease complexity to guide revascularization strategy (PCI vs CABG) in patients with left main and/or three-vessel disease.
entries.formula_human: Sum of all lesion-specific points from the coronary anatomy (12-item algorithm applied to each lesion, then summed). Full algorithm published by SYNTAX working group and available at syntaxscore.com. Each lesion adds 0–20+ points depending on characteristics. Total is sum across all lesions in the coronary tree.

inputs.label: Coronary lesion characteristics
inputs.description: Each coronary lesion scored for: dominance, lesion location, number of lesions, total occlusion, trifurcation, bifurcation, aorto-ostial, severe tortuosity, length >20mm, heavy calcification, thrombus, diffuse disease
inputs.options_text: Multiple scored items per lesion based on the 12-item SYNTAX algorithm
inputs.points_text: Points assigned per lesion characteristic (detailed in SYNTAX score working group)

bands.meaning: Low complexity. PCI and CABG have similar outcomes. PCI is reasonable.
Intermediate complexity. CABG preferred in most patients.
High complexity. CABG strongly recommended over PCI.

citations.text: Sianos G, Morel MA, Kappetein AP, et al. The SYNTAX Score: an angiographic tool grading the complexity of coronary artery disease. EuroIntervention. 2005;1(2):219-227. PMID: 19758907 (score algorithm); SYNTAX Trial: Serruys PW, et al. N Engl J Med. 2009;360:961-972. PMID: 19228615

entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app — syntaxscore.com
entries.limitations: Requires angiographic interpretation by experienced interventional cardiologist (significant inter-observer variability). Does not include clinical variables (SYNTAX Score II adds clinical factors). Only applicable to left main and/or 3-vessel disease. Does not account for ischemia (FFR).

entries.name: CRUSADE
entries.purpose: In-hospital bleeding post-ACS
entries.formula_human: Admission Hct, CrCl, HR, SBP, sex, DM, CHF, prior VTE -> 0-100 score; >50 high

entries.name: JAAM DIC
entries.purpose: DIC (Japanese criteria)
entries.formula_human: SIRS >=3 =1; platelets 80-120k or >30% drop=1, <80k or >50% drop=3; PT ratio >=1.2=1; FDP >=25 ug/mL=1, >=25 with strong=3; total >=4

entries.name: PRECISE-DAPT
entries.purpose: PCI bleeding risk (DAPT duration)
entries.formula_human: Hemoglobin, WBC, age, CrCl, prior bleeding; points 0-25 via nomogram; >=25 high bleeding risk -> short DAPT

entries.name: SIC (sepsis-induced coagulopathy)
entries.purpose: DIC in sepsis
entries.formula_human: Platelet 100-150=1, <100=2; PT-INR 1.2-1.4=1, >1.4=2; SOFA (resp/CNS) 1-2=1, 3-4=2? (liver/cardiovascular/renal) ; total 0-6; >=4 = SIC

entries.name: TIMI major/minor bleeding
entries.purpose: Bleeding definition in trials
entries.formula_human: Hgb drop >=5 g/dL (major), >=3 with source etc.; TIMI criteria tables

entries.name: 4AT
entries.purpose: Rapid delirium screen (geriatrics/ED)
entries.formula_human: Alertness 0-4 + AMT4 0-4 + attention 0-2 + acute change 0-2; total 0-12; >=4 probable delirium

entries.name: APACHE IV
entries.purpose: Updated ICU mortality prediction model with improved calibration for contemporary practice, incorporating 129 variables.
entries.formula_human: Logistic regression: ln(R/(1−R)) = β₀ + Σβᵢxᵢ with 129 candidate variables (reduced model uses fewer). Exact coefficients published in Zimmerman JE, et al. 2006. ICU mortality = e^LP / (1 + e^LP). Separate hospital mortality model available. Use APACHE IV calculator from Cerner/verifiable source.

inputs.label: Acute Physiology Score (APS)
inputs.description: Same 12 physiologic variables as APACHE II/III but with updated weights
inputs.points_text: updated weights from 0–4 to 0–60+ per variable

inputs.label: Admission source
inputs.description: Floor, OR/recovery, other hospital, direct admission

inputs.label: Length of stay prior to ICU
inputs.description: Days from hospital admission to ICU admission

inputs.label: Other variables
inputs.description: Serum glucose, BUN, albumin, bilirubin, WBC, temperature interactions, etc.

bands.meaning: Low ICU mortality risk
Moderate risk
High risk
Very high risk

citations.text: Zimmerman JE, Kramer AA, McNair DS, Malila FM. Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation (APACHE) IV: hospital mortality assessment for today's critically ill patients. Crit Care Med. 2006;34(5):1297-1310. PMID: 16540951

entries.limitations: Very complex (requires dedicated software). 116 diagnostic categories require coding expertise. US-specific calibration. Not freely available for bedside use. May not perform well outside US ICUs. Superseded by newer models in some settings.

entries.name: CPOT
entries.purpose: ICU pain (non-verbal)
entries.formula_human: Facial expression 0-2 + body movements 0-2 + muscle tension 0-2 + vocalization/intubated 0-2; total 0-8

entries.name: MEWS
entries.purpose: Identifies deteriorating ward patients who may require ICU admission or escalation of care, using bedside vital signs.
entries.formula_human: MEWS = SBP_points + HR_points + RR_points + Temperature_points + AVPU_points

bands.meaning: Low risk; routine monitoring
Consider increasing monitoring frequency; senior review recommended
High risk for clinical deterioration; urgent senior review and possible ICU/CCU transfer. ≥5 associated with significantly increased mortality.

citations.text: Subbe CP, Kruger M, Rutherford P, Gemmel L. Validation of a modified Early Warning Score in medical admissions. QJM. 2001;94(10):521-526. PMID: 11588210

entries.limitations: AVPU is less granular than GCS. Does not capture oxygen saturation or supplemental oxygen. Subjective components. Various versions exist with slightly different cutoffs (non-standardized). Sensitivity varies by patient population.

entries.name: OASIS
entries.purpose: ICU severity (claims/administrative use)
entries.formula_human: 7 variables (age, GCS, HR, MAP, RR, Cr, LOS) weighted 0-48

entries.name: Phoenix criteria
entries.purpose: Pediatric sepsis (2024 Surviving Sepsis)
entries.formula_human: Respiratory, cardiovascular, coagulation, neurologic dysfunction; 1 pt each component (age-adjusted); >=2 = Phoenix sepsis

entries.name: SOFA-based Sepsis-3
entries.purpose: Sepsis = infection + SOFA rise >=2

entries.name: Sedation-Agitation Scale
entries.purpose: ICU sedation
entries.formula_human: 1-7 scale (unarousable to dangerous agitation)

entries.name: AIR score
entries.purpose: More nuanced clinical and laboratory score for appendicitis risk stratification, incorporating CRP and segmented neutrophils.
entries.formula_human: AIR = Vomiting(1) + RLQ_tenderness(1) + Rebound(0-2) + Fever(1) + WBC(0-2) + CRP(0-2) + Segmented_neutrophils(0-2)

bands.meaning: Low risk (~0–5% appendicitis). Observation or discharge.
Intermediate risk (~20–65%). Imaging recommended.
High risk (~90–100%). Consider direct surgical consultation.

citations.text: Andersson M, Andersson RE. The Appendicitis Inflammatory Response Score: a tool for the diagnosis of acute appendicitis that outperforms the Alvarado score. World J Surg. 2008;32(8):1843-1849. PMID: 18427889

entries.limitations: Requires CRP (not always immediately available in all EDs). More complex than Alvarado. Needs external validation in diverse populations. Cutoff values for neutrophils may vary. Less studied in children and elderly.

entries.name: CIWA / COWS (see psychiatry)
entries.purpose: CIWA / COWS (see psychiatry)

entries.name: EGSYS
entries.purpose: Cardiac syncope prediction
entries.formula_human: Syncope during exertion 3, abnormal ECG 3? palpitations 4, dyspnea 2? ... ; >=3 predicts cardiac cause

entries.name: FeverPAIN
entries.purpose: Sore throat antibiotic guidance
entries.formula_human: Fever 1, purulence 1, attend <3d 1, inflamed tonsils 1, no cough/coryza 1; total 0-5; 3-4 consider abx, 5-6 prescribe

entries.name: PERC / YEARS (see respiratory)
entries.purpose: Identifies low-risk ED patients in whom PE can be safely excluded without D-dimer testing.
entries.formula_human:
PERC: All 8 criteria must be negative (and patient must be low risk by gestalt). Any single criterion positive = PERC fails. PERC negative = PE ruled out without D-dimer.
PERC fail rate = number of positive criteria / 8

inputs.label: No surgery/trauma within 4 weeks
inputs.description: No recent surgery or trauma requiring hospitalization

bands.meaning: PE effectively excluded (<2% missed PE). No further testing needed.
PERC fails. Proceed to D-dimer and/or imaging based on clinical probability.

citations.text: Kline JA, Mitchell AM, Kabrhel C, et al. Clinical criteria to prevent unnecessary diagnostic testing in emergency department patients with suspected pulmonary embolism. J Thromb Haemost. 2004;2(8):1247-1255. PMID: 15304025

entries.limitations: Only applicable to low-risk patients (must first determine low clinical suspicion). Not valid in high-prevalence settings. D-dimer testing is inexpensive and readily available — some clinicians prefer testing over PERC. Missed PE rate ~1-2% (not zero). Should not override strong clinical suspicion.

entries.name: RIPASA score
entries.purpose: Appendicitis (Asian populations)
entries.formula_human: 12-14 items weighted (symptoms, signs, labs, sex, age); 0-16

entries.name: San Francisco Syncope Rule
entries.purpose: Identifies syncope patients at risk for serious outcomes within 30 days who require admission or intensive evaluation.
entries.formula_human: SFSR = CHF(1) + Hct<30(1) + ECG_abnormal(1) + SOB(1) + SBP<90(1). Positive if any criterion present (CHESS mnemonic: CHF, Hct, ECG, SOB, SBP).

inputs.label: ECG abnormality
inputs.description: New changes, ischemia, arrhythmia, or non-sinus rhythm

inputs.label: Shortness of breath
inputs.description: Dyspnea as presenting or associated symptom

bands.meaning: Low risk (~2% serious outcome at 30 days). Safe for discharge with outpatient evaluation.
High risk (~7–19% serious outcome). Admit or observe for further evaluation.

citations.text: Quinn JV, Stiell IG, McDermott DA, et al. Derivation of the San Francisco Syncope Rule to predict patients with short-term serious outcomes. Ann Emerg Med. 2004;43(2):224-232. PMID: 14747812

entries.limitations: External validation shows mixed results — sensitivity may be lower than original study. ECG abnormality definition is broad and subjective. Hematocrit cutoff of 30% is unusual. Higher sensitivity but lower specificity may lead to over-admission. Other competing scores (EGSYS, Canadian) exist.

entries.name: ALBI grade
entries.purpose: HCC liver function / prognosis
entries.formula_human: ALBI = 0.66*log10(bilirubin umol/L) - 0.085*albumin(g/L); grade 1 <= -2.61, 2 > -2.61 to -1.39, 3 > -1.39

entries.name: APRI
entries.purpose: Simple non-invasive marker of liver fibrosis using AST and platelet count. Validated primarily in chronic hepatitis C.
entries.formula_human: APRI = [(AST / ULN_AST) / Platelet_count(×10⁹/L)] × 100

inputs.label: AST upper limit of normal
inputs.description: ULN for AST at local laboratory (typically 40 IU/L)

bands.meaning: Low probability of significant fibrosis (≥F2). NPV ~80–90%.
Indeterminate range.
High probability of significant fibrosis. PPV ~80%.
High probability of cirrhosis (F4). Specificity ~90%.

citations.text: Wai CT, Greenson JK, Fontana RJ, et al. A simple noninvasive index can predict both significant fibrosis and cirrhosis in patients with chronic hepatitis C. Hepatology. 2003;38(2):518-526. PMID: 12883497

entries.limitations: Moderate sensitivity and specificity for intermediate fibrosis stages. AST ULN varies between laboratories. Not recommended as sole test — should be used in combination with FIB-4 or elastography. Less validated in NAFLD than FIB-4. Affected by hemolysis, myopathy, and other non-hepatic causes of AST elevation.

entries.name: CDAI
entries.purpose: Simplified disease activity index for RA that does not require acute phase reactants (ESR/CRP). Purely clinical assessment allowing rapid point-of-care evaluation.
entries.formula_human: CDAI = TJC28 + SJC28 + Patient Global (0–10) + Physician Global (0–10)

inputs.label: Tender Joint Count (TJC28)
inputs.description: Number of tender joints out of 28

inputs.label: Swollen Joint Count (SJC28)
inputs.description: Number of swollen joints out of 28

bands.meaning: Remission
Low disease activity
Moderate disease activity
High disease activity

citations.text: Aletaha D, Nell VP, Stamm T, et al. Acute phase reactants add little to composite disease activity indices for rheumatoid arthritis: validation of a clinical activity score. Arthritis Res Ther. 2005;7(4):R796-R806. PMID: 15987482

entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published academic tool
entries.limitations: Relies on physician and patient global assessments which are subjective. Joint counts require training to perform reliably. Less sensitive to change than DAS28 in some studies. CDAI remission (≤2.8) corresponds closely to Boolean remission but may not capture residual subclinical synovitis.

entries.name: CLIF-C ACLF
entries.purpose: ACLF short-term mortality
entries.formula_human: CLIF-C ACLF = 10*(0.33*CLIF-OF + 0.04*age + 0.63*ln(WBC) - 2)

entries.name: ELF test
entries.purpose: Advanced fibrosis blood panel
entries.formula_human: ELF = -7.412 + 0.681*ln(HA) + 0.775*ln(PIIINP) + 0.494*ln(TIMP-1); >=9.8 advanced fibrosis? >=11.3 cirrhosis

entries.name: Glasgow Alcoholic Hepatitis Score
entries.purpose: Predicts 28-day mortality in alcoholic hepatitis; alternative to MDF for identifying patients who may benefit from steroid therapy.
entries.formula_human: GAHS = Age(1–2) + WBC(1–2) + Urea(1–2) + PT_ratio(1–2) + Bilirubin(1–2)

bands.meaning: Low 28-day mortality (~10–15%). Steroids not recommended.
High 28-day mortality (~40–75%). Consider steroid therapy.

citations.text: Forrest EH, Evans CD, Stewart S, et al. Analysis of factors predictive of mortality in alcoholic hepatitis and derivation and validation of the Glasgow alcoholic hepatitis score. Gut. 2005;54(8):1174-1179. PMID: 16009691

entries.limitations: Derived in predominantly White Scottish population. Cutoff values (urea 5 mmol/L) may need adjustment for different populations. Bilirubin cutoff in µmol/L may confuse US clinicians (125 µmol/L ≈ 7.3 mg/dL). Not as widely adopted as MDF in US guidelines.

entries.name: Harvey-Bradshaw Index
entries.purpose: Crohn activity (simpler)
entries.formula_human: General well-being 0-4 + abdominal pain 0-3 + diarrhea x2 + mass 0-3 + complications 1 each; 0-~20; <=4 remission

entries.name: Lille score
entries.purpose: Predicts 6-month survival in severe alcoholic hepatitis after 7 days of corticosteroid treatment to identify non-responders.
entries.formula_human:
Lille = exp(−R) / (1 + exp(−R))

Where R = 3.19 − 0.101×age(years) + 0.147×albumin_day0(g/L) + 0.0165×evolution_bilirubin(d0−d7)(µmol/L) − 0.206×renal_insufficiency(0/1) − 0.0065×bilirubin_day0(µmol/L) − 0.0096×bilirubin_day7(µmol/L)

Note: The exact formula coefficients are from the 2007 publication. Verify exact formula and variable transformations (some publications use mg/dL, others µmol/L) from Louvet A, et al. 2007. Bilirubin and albumin in mg/dL conversions may differ from µmol/L formula.

inputs.label: Change in bilirubin (day 0 to day 7)
inputs.description: Evolution of bilirubin over first 7 days of steroids
inputs.options_text: continuous (can be negative if bilirubin drops)

inputs.label: Evolution of bilirubin (day 0 to 7)
inputs.description: Change in bilirubin value (day 7 − day 0, but incorporated as bilirubin_evolution)

bands.meaning: Complete response. 6-month survival ~85–95%. Continue corticosteroids.
Partial response. 6-month survival ~50–60%. Consider stopping steroids and palliative care discussion.
Non-response. 6-month survival ~10–25%. Corticosteroids should be stopped. Consider palliative care.

citations.text: Louvet A, Naveau S, Abdelnour M, et al. The Lille model: a new tool for therapeutic strategy in patients with severe alcoholic hepatitis treated with steroids. Hepatology. 2007;45(6):1348-1354. PMID: 17518367

entries.limitations: Should only be calculated after 7 days of corticosteroid treatment. Requires serial bilirubin (day 0 and day 7). Cannot be applied to patients not receiving steroids. Formula uses µmol/L (not mg/dL) for bilirubin in the original — conversion needed for US laboratories (1 mg/dL = 17.1 µmol/L). Thresholds may need calibration for different populations. Does not include encephalopathy at day 7 (which independently worsens prognosis).

entries.name: MELD 3.0
entries.purpose: US transplant listing (2023+)

entries.name: Maddrey Discriminant Function
entries.purpose: Identifies patients with severe alcoholic hepatitis who may benefit from corticosteroid therapy.
entries.formula_human:
MDF = 4.6 × (PT_patient − PT_control) + Bilirubin(mg/dL)

Alternative using INR (when INR is available instead of PT control):
MDF = 4.6 × (INR − 1) + Bilirubin(mg/dL)

bands.meaning: Non-severe alcoholic hepatitis. Steroids not routinely recommended. 28-day mortality ~10%.
Severe alcoholic hepatitis. Consider corticosteroids (prednisolone 40 mg/day × 28 days). 28-day mortality ~30–50%.

citations.text: Maddrey WC, Boitnott JK, Bedine MS, et al. Corticosteroid therapy of alcoholic hepatitis. Gastroenterology. 1978;75(2):193-199. PMID: 352788

entries.limitations: PT/INR and bilirubin can be elevated from causes other than alcoholic hepatitis (sepsis, cholestasis). Cutoff of 32 is somewhat arbitrary. Does not capture renal function, infection status, or nutritional status. INR-based formula is approximate (not identical to original PT-based version). Steroid response should be assessed early (Lille score at day 7).

entries.name: Mayo Clinic Score
entries.purpose: Ulcerative colitis activity
entries.formula_human: Stool frequency 0-3 + rectal bleeding 0-3 + mucosal appearance 0-3 + physician rating 0-3; 0-12; <=2 remission

entries.name: NAFLD Fibrosis Score
entries.purpose: Estimates the probability of advanced fibrosis (F3–F4) in patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD).
entries.formula_human: NFS = −1.675 + 0.037 × Age(years) + 0.094 × BMI(kg/m²) + 1.13 × IFG/DM(0/1) + 0.66 × log(AST/ALT) − 0.013 × Platelet(×10⁹/L) − 0.66 × Albumin(g/dL)

bands.meaning: F0–F2 fibrosis likely. NPV ~88–93%. Advanced fibrosis excluded.
Indeterminate zone. Biopsy may be needed.
Advanced fibrosis (F3–F4) likely. PPV ~82–90%.

citations.text: Angulo P, Hui JM, Marchesini G, et al. The NAFLD fibrosis score: a noninvasive system that identifies liver fibrosis in patients with NAFLD. Hepatology. 2007;45(4):846-854. PMID: 17393509

entries.limitations: Less accurate in the indeterminate zone. Performed poorly in elderly (age coefficient may overestimate fibrosis). Requires BMI (affected by ethnicity-specific cutoffs). Does not perform well in non-NAFLD liver disease. External validation shows AUC ~0.7–0.8 (modest). Should not replace biopsy when definitive staging is needed.

entries.name: Ranson criteria
entries.purpose: Pancreatitis severity (legacy)
entries.formula_human: Admission: age>55, WBC>16k, glucose>200, LDH>350, AST>250 (each 1); 48h: Hct drop>10%, BUN rise>5, Ca<8, PaO2<60, base deficit>4, fluid sequestration>6L (each 1); total 0-11

entries.name: Rockall score
entries.purpose: UGIB mortality (post-endoscopy)
entries.formula_human: Clinical: age <60/60-79/>=80 =0/1/2; shock none/HR>100/SBP<100 =0/1/2; comorbidity none/some/renal-liver-cancer =0/2/3. Endoscopy: dx 0-2; stigmata 0-2. Total 0-11

entries.name: FINDRISC
entries.purpose: Estimates 10-year probability of developing type 2 diabetes using non-invasive clinical variables. Used for population-level screening.
entries.formula_human: FINDRISC = Age(0–5) + BMI(0–3) + Waist(0–4) + Physical_activity(0/2) + Fruit_veg(0/1) + HTN_meds(0/2) + High_glucose(0/5) + Family_hx(0/5)

bands.meaning: Low risk (~1% 10-year T2DM risk)
Slightly elevated risk (~4%)
Moderate risk (~17%)
High risk (~33%)
Very high risk (~50%+). Fasting glucose/HbA1c testing and lifestyle intervention strongly recommended.

citations.text: Lindström J, Tuomilehto J. The diabetes risk score: a practical tool to predict type 2 diabetes risk. Diabetes Care. 2003;26(3):725-731. PMID: 12610029

entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app
entries.limitations: Self-reported variables (diet, activity) are subject to recall bias. Waist circumference cutoffs may differ for Asian populations. Not validated as a diagnostic test (not a replacement for fasting glucose or OGTT). Performance varies by ethnicity. Does not include ethnicity-specific adjustments. No laboratory data included (by design for population screening).

entries.name: HOMA-IR
entries.purpose: Insulin resistance (research)
entries.formula_human: HOMA-IR = fasting glucose(mmol/L)*fasting insulin(uU/mL)/22.5 (or /405 with mg/dL)

entries.name: HOMA-beta
entries.purpose: Beta-cell function
entries.formula_human: HOMA-beta = 20*fasting insulin/(fasting glucose - 3.5)

entries.name: QDiabetes
entries.purpose: UK diabetes risk
entries.formula_human: Cox model ~30 factors

entries.name: TyG index
entries.purpose: Insulin resistance surrogate
entries.formula_human: TyG = ln[fasting TG(mg/dL)*fasting glucose(mg/dL)/2]

entries.name: ABCD2
entries.purpose: Predicts 2-day, 7-day, and 90-day risk of stroke after transient ischemic attack.
entries.formula_human: ABCD² = Age≥60(1) + BP≥140/90(1) + Clinical(0–2) + Duration(0–2) + Diabetes(1)

bands.meaning: Low risk of stroke at 2 days (~1%). Outpatient workup acceptable.
Moderate risk (~4% at 2 days). Consider urgent evaluation.
High risk (~8–12% at 2 days). Urgent inpatient evaluation and imaging recommended.

citations.text: Johnston SC, Rothwell PM, Nguyen-Huynh MN, et al. Validation and refinement of scores to predict very early stroke risk after transient ischaemic attack. Lancet. 2007;369(9558):283-292. PMID: 17258668

entries.limitations: May underestimate risk in patients with atrial fibrillation, carotid stenosis, or DWI-positive MRI lesions. Does not incorporate imaging findings (DWI, vessel occlusion). The original ABCD² may be superseded by ABCD²I (includes imaging). Clinical feature category requires accurate history (may be unreliable in amnestic TIA). Cut-off values are somewhat arbitrary.

entries.name: ESSEN Stroke Risk Score
entries.purpose: Secondary stroke prevention
entries.formula_human: CHF 1, HTN 1, age 65-75=1/>75=2, DM 1, prior stroke/TIA 2, MI 1, PAD 1, smoking 1; total 0-9

entries.name: FOUR score
entries.purpose: Alternative to GCS for assessing level of consciousness in critically ill, intubated patients. Eliminates the verbal component of GCS (which cannot be assessed in intubated patients) and replaces it with brainstem reflexes and respiratory pattern. Developed for ICU use.
entries.formula_human:
FOUR Score = E + M + B + R
Range: 0–16

inputs.label: Eye response (E)
inputs.options_text: 4 (eyelids open, tracking or blinking to command), 3 (eyelids open but not tracking), 2 (eyelids closed but open to loud voice), 1 (eyelids closed but open to pain), 0 (eyelids remain closed with pain)

inputs.label: Motor response (M)
inputs.options_text: 4 (thumbs-up, fist, or peace sign to command), 3 (localizing to pain), 2 (flexion response to pain), 1 (extension response to pain), 0 (no response to pain or generalized myoclonus)

inputs.label: Brainstem reflexes (B)
inputs.options_text: 4 (pupils and corneal reflexes present), 3 (one pupil wide and fixed), 2 (pupils OR corneal reflexes absent), 1 (pupils AND corneal reflexes absent), 0 (absent pupil, corneal, and cough reflex

inputs.label: Respiration (R)
inputs.description: Respiratory pattern (for intubated patients: breathing over ventilator rate, or triggering ventilator)
inputs.options_text: 4 (not intubated, regular breathing), 3 (not intubated, Cheyne-Stokes breathing), 2 (not intubated, breathing irregularly or ataxic), 1 (breathes at ventilator rate or above), 0 (breathes below ventilator rate or apnea)

bands.meaning: Fully alert, intact brainstem reflexes, normal respiration.
Mild impairment. May be confused or have mild tracking deficit.
Moderate impairment. Requires close monitoring.
Severe impairment. Coma likely. Brainstem reflexes may be partially intact.
Deep coma. Brainstem reflexes largely absent. Poor prognosis.
Near-complete or complete brainstem failure. Critical prognosis.

citations.text: Wijdicks EF, Bamlet WR, Maramattom BV, et al. Validation of a new coma scale: The FOUR score. Ann Neurol. 2005;58(4):585-593. PMID: 16178024

entries.limitations: Developed for ICU patients — may be less practical in prehospital or ED settings (requires assessment of brainstem reflexes). Requires training for consistent brainstem reflex assessment. Respiratory component difficult to assess on ventilated patients with specific modes. Does not capture cognitive assessment (memory, orientation). Not as widely adopted as GCS. Limited data in non-TBI coma (toxic, metabolic, post-cardiac arrest). Not validated for pediatric populations. May have ceiling effect in patients with moderate impairment. Not validated for sedated/paralyzed patients. Requires examiner to know ventilator settings for respiratory assessment. Does not capture cranial nerve deficits other than those reflected in brainstem reflexes. Less familiar to non-ICU clinicians.

entries.name: Glasgow Outcome Scale
entries.purpose: TBI outcome
entries.formula_human: 1 death - 5 good recovery

entries.name: Rancho Los Amigos
entries.purpose: TBI cognitive recovery
entries.formula_human: Levels I-X

entries.name: Sarnat staging
entries.purpose: Neonatal HIE severity
entries.formula_human: Stage I mild, II moderate, III severe

entries.name: Edmonton Frail Scale
entries.purpose: Frailty (community)
entries.formula_human: 9 domains; 0-17; >=8 frail

entries.name: Fried Frailty Phenotype
entries.purpose: Frailty research
entries.formula_human: 5 criteria (shrinking, weakness, exhaustion, slowness, low activity); >=3 frail

entries.name: GNRI
entries.purpose: Geriatric nutritional risk
entries.formula_human: GNRI = 14.89*albumin + 41.7*(weight/ideal weight); <92 risk

entries.name: Hendrich II Fall Risk
entries.purpose: Fall risk (acute care)
