entries.formula_human: Confusion/disorientation 4, depression 2, altered voiding 1, diarrhea 1, nocturia 1, dizziness/vertigo 1, male 1, antiepileptics 2, benzodiazepines 1, GET-up-and-go test 4; total 0-16; >=5 high risk

entries.name: MNA-SF
entries.purpose: Elderly nutrition screen
entries.formula_human: 6 items -> 0-14; <=11 at risk

entries.name: Norton Scale
entries.purpose: Original pressure injury risk assessment scale, developed in 1962. Simpler and older than the Braden Scale. Still used in some settings, particularly in Europe and for rapid screening. Less comprehensive than Braden but quicker to administer.
entries.formula_human:
Norton Score = Physical condition + Mental condition + Activity + Mobility + Incontinence
Range: 5–20

inputs.label: Mobility
inputs.description: Ability to move and change position

inputs.label: Incontinence
inputs.options_text: 1 (double incontinent — urine and feces), 2 (usually incontinent), 3 (occasionally incontinent), 4 (continent)

bands.meaning: Low risk. Standard nursing care. Skin assessment.
Moderate risk. Implement preventive measures (turning, pressure-redistributing surface, nutrition).
High risk. Aggressive prevention program (specialized mattress, frequent turning, nutrition support, comprehensive skin care).

citations.text: Norton D, McLaren R, Exton-Smith AN. An investigation of geriatric nursing problems in hospital. Edinburgh: Churchill Livingstone; 1962

entries.limitations: Older and less comprehensive than Braden Scale (only 5 items vs. 6). 'Physical condition' and 'mental condition' are very broad categories. Less validated than Braden in current hospital populations. Subjective assessment. Does not include friction/shear (important risk factor). Does not capture nutrition independently (embedded in 'physical condition'). Lower sensitivity and specificity compared to Braden. Not validated for pediatric populations. Original cutoff scores (≤14 high risk) may not be optimal for current hospital populations. Used more in European than North American settings. 'Incontinence' assessment may be challenging in catheterized patients. Not suitable for medical device-related pressure injuries.

entries.name: SGA / GLIM criteria
entries.purpose: Clinician-performed comprehensive nutritional assessment tool combining history and physical examination findings to classify patients into nutritional categories. Gold standard for clinical nutritional assessment in hospitalized patients.
entries.formula_human:
SGA = Clinical judgment integrating all history and physical findings:

SGA A (Well-nourished): No weight loss or minimal, good intake, no functional impairment, no fat/muscle loss
SGA B (Moderately malnourished): 5-10% weight loss, reduced intake, mild functional impairment, mild fat/muscle loss
SGA C (Severely malnourished): >10% weight loss, significant intake reduction, significant functional impairment, obvious fat/muscle loss

inputs.label: Weight change
inputs.description: Weight loss/gain over past 6 months and 2 weeks
inputs.options_text: Assessed for amount, rate, and trajectory

inputs.label: Dietary intake
inputs.description: Current dietary intake relative to normal and changes in intake pattern

inputs.label: Functional capacity
inputs.description: Ability to perform activities of daily living
inputs.options_text: Full capacity, ambulatory but suboptimal, bedridden

inputs.label: Disease and its relation to nutritional requirements
Subcutaneous fat loss
inputs.description: Loss of subcutaneous fat in triceps, chest, and face

inputs.label: Muscle wasting
inputs.description: Loss of muscle in quadriceps, deltoids, temporalis

bands.meaning: Well-nourished — no specific nutritional intervention required
Moderately malnourished or suspected malnutrition — nutritional support (dietary counseling, ONS, dietary fortification)
Severely malnourished — aggressive nutritional support (enteral/parenteral nutrition), close monitoring

citations.text: Detsky AS, McLaughlin JR, Baker JP, et al. What is subjective global assessment of nutritional status? JPEN J Parenter Enteral Nutr. 1987;11(1):8-13. PMID: 3820522

entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published academic tool
entries.limitations: Subjective — requires trained assessor (dietitian or physician experienced in nutritional assessment). Inter-rater reliability moderate (kappa ~0.5–0.7). Non-quantitative — categorical classification may miss subtle changes. Physical exam findings affected by edema, ascites, and patient body habitus. Not suitable for screening (requires full assessment). Time-consuming (10–15 minutes per assessment). Subjective nature limits research comparability. Doesn't capture micronutrient status. Pediatric version (SGA-PG-SGA) is separate. No standardized training protocol — assessment may vary by institution.

entries.name: Waterlow Scale
entries.purpose: Pressure ulcer risk (UK)
entries.formula_human: Build/weight, skin type, sex/age, continence, mobility, appetite, meds, tissue malnutrition, neuro deficit, surgery/trauma; total 0-?

entries.name: Apgar / GCS (cross)
entries.purpose: Rapid standardized assessment of newborn status at 1 and 5 minutes after birth. Guides need for resuscitation and predicts neonatal outcomes. APGAR is also a backronym: Appearance, Pulse, Grimace, Activity, Respiration.
entries.formula_human:
APGAR = Appearance (0–2) + Pulse (0–2) + Grimace (0–2) + Activity (0–2) + Respiration (0–2)
Scored at 1 minute and 5 minutes after birth
If 5-minute score <7, repeat every 5 minutes up to 20 minutes

inputs.label: Appearance (skin color)
inputs.options_text: Blue/pale all over=0, Body pink/extremities blue=1, Completely pink=2

inputs.label: Grimace (reflex irritability)
inputs.description: Response to stimulation (nasal catheter, foot slap)

inputs.label: Respiration
inputs.options_text: Absent=0, Irregular/weak cry=1, Strong cry/regular breathing=2

bands.meaning: Normal newborn transition — no intervention needed
Moderately depressed — may need stimulation, suctioning, oxygen, or positive-pressure ventilation
Severely depressed — immediate resuscitation (intubation, medications, chest compressions)
Good recovery — common and generally favorable prognosis
Associated with increased risk of neurological morbidity and neonatal mortality

citations.text: Apgar V. A proposal for a new method of evaluation of the newborn infant. Curr Res Anesth Analg. 1953;32(4):260-267. PMID: 13083014

entries.copyright: public domain — named after Virginia Apgar, Anesthesiologist
entries.limitations: Subjective — interobserver variability. APGAR affected by gestational age (preterm infants score lower), maternal medications (sedatives, anesthetics), and resuscitation interventions performed before scoring. Not designed to predict long-term neurological outcomes. A low score at 1 minute is common and not necessarily pathological. 5-minute score has better prognostic value. Doesn't guide specific resuscitation steps (NRP algorithm more useful). Not a substitute for blood gas analysis or clinical assessment of neonatal well-being. Score 7 doesn't distinguish between well-perfused and mildly compromised infants.

entries.name: Maternal early warning criteria (MEWC)
entries.purpose: US trigger criteria
entries.formula_human: SBP<90 or >160, DBP>100, HR<50 or >120, RR<10 or >30, SpO2<95%, temp>38, O2 need, drop in urine, neuro concerns

entries.name: OGTT (IADPSG/WHO) thresholds
entries.purpose: GDM diagnosis
entries.formula_human: Fasting >=92, 1h >=180, 2h >=153 mg/dL (IADPSG; 1 abnormal = GDM)

entries.name: CAPRA
entries.purpose: Prostate cancer pre-treatment risk
entries.formula_human: PSA (0-6?), Gleason, T stage, %positive cores, age; total 0-10

entries.name: FLIPI / FLIPI2
entries.purpose: Predicts overall survival in follicular lymphoma based on clinical factors at diagnosis.
entries.formula_human: FLIPI = Age>60(1) + Stage_III-IV(1) + Hb<12(1) + LDH>ULN(1) + Nodal>4(1)

bands.meaning: Low risk. 10-year OS ~71%.
Intermediate risk. 10-year OS ~51%.
High risk. 10-year OS ~36%.

citations.text: Solal-Céligny P, Roy P, Colombat P, et al. Follicular lymphoma international prognostic index. Blood. 2004;104(5):1258-1265. PMID: 15126323

entries.limitations: Does not incorporate molecular markers (m7-FLIPI adds mutational status). Does not capture rituximab-era treatment differences. Advanced stage is nearly universal in FL (limiting discriminatory power). FLIPI2 uses different variables (beta-2 microglobulin, bone marrow involvement, longest diameter of largest node).

entries.name: HCC: Hong Kong Liver Cancer (HKLC)
entries.purpose: HCC prognosis (alternative to BCLC)
entries.formula_human: Stage I-V + ECOG + liver status

entries.name: MIPI
entries.purpose: Mantle cell lymphoma prognosis

entries.name: Masaoka-Koga
entries.purpose: Thymoma stage
entries.formula_human: I encapsulated - IVb dissemination

entries.name: NCCN-IPI
entries.purpose: DLBCL refined
entries.formula_human: Age (41-60=1? >60-75=2? >75=3? published points: age <=40 0, 40-60 1? (points: <=40=0, 41-60? ) LDH ratio (1-3x=1, >3x=2), extranodal sites (>1=1), stage IV=1; total 0-8

entries.name: Rai / Binet
entries.purpose: Pediatric tool combining AKI risk (baseline vulnerability) and AKI injury signals (creatinine/fluid overload) to predict severe AKI in critically ill children, analogous to 'angina' preceding 'infarction.'
entries.formula_human:
RAI = Risk_tier(1–3) × Injury_signal(1–2). Range: 1–6.
Renal Angina Fulfilled: RAI ≥8 at 12h or ≥6 at 24h (depending on version).

inputs.label: Risk tier (baseline vulnerability)
inputs.description: Patient's baseline risk: standard ICU, high-risk ICU, or bone marrow transplant/CPR

inputs.label: Injury signal (creatinine change or fluid overload)
inputs.description: Creatinine rise from baseline or fluid overload percentage

bands.meaning: Renal angina NOT fulfilled. Low probability of severe AKI (negative predictive value >95%).
Renal angina fulfilled. High risk of severe AKI. Consider biomarkers (NGAL, KIM-1) for further stratification.

citations.text: Basu RK, Zappitelli M, Brunner L, et al. Derivation and validation of the renal angina index to improve the prediction of acute kidney injury in critically ill children. Kidney Int. 2014;85(3):659-667. PMID: 23925279

entries.limitations: Developed for pediatric ICU populations only. Thresholds for RAI fulfillment debated. Requires accurate fluid balance tracking. Not validated in adults. Injury signal definitions may vary by study. Requires baseline creatinine or estimated value.

entries.name: Revised IPI (R-IPI)
entries.purpose: DLBCL (rituximab era)
entries.formula_human: Same 5 factors; 0=very good, 1-2=good, 3-5=poor

entries.name: WPSS
entries.purpose: MDS prognosis
entries.formula_human: IPSS cytogenetics + BM blasts + cytopenias + transfusion need; 0 very low - >=3 high

entries.name: Ballard score
entries.purpose: Neonatal gestational age assessment
entries.formula_human: Neuromuscular + physical maturity items -> GA weeks

entries.name: Bhutani nomogram / AAP hour-specific
entries.purpose: Neonatal jaundice treatment thresholds
entries.formula_human: Plot TSB vs hours of age; phototherapy/exchange thresholds by risk zone

entries.name: COMFORT-B
entries.purpose: PICU sedation/pain
entries.formula_human: 6 behavioral items x 1-5; total 6-30

entries.name: CRIB II
entries.purpose: NICU mortality
entries.formula_human: Birthweight, gestational age, temperature, base excess, FiO2 (0-27); <6 low risk

entries.name: Downe score
entries.purpose: Neonatal respiratory distress
entries.formula_human: 5 signs scored 0-2; total 0-10

entries.name: NPASS
entries.purpose: Neonatal pain
entries.formula_human: 6 items x -1 to +2 (gestational age + postnatal age adjustments); total -7 to +42

entries.name: PELD
entries.purpose: Pediatric liver transplant waitlist
entries.formula_human: PELD = 4.80*ln(bili) + 18.57*ln(INR) - 6.87*ln(albumin) + 4.36(<1yr) + 6.67(growth failure <-2SD); or Pedi MELD for >12y

entries.name: PIM2 / PIM3
entries.purpose: PICU mortality (admission)
entries.formula_human: Logistic: PIM2 = -5.50 + weighted terms (pupils, mechanical vent, base excess, FiO2, SBP, elective admission...); similar PIM3

entries.name: PRISM III
entries.purpose: PICU mortality
entries.formula_human: 17 physiologic variables, worst in first 12/24h; score -> mortality

entries.name: Pediatric Parkland / Galveston
entries.purpose: Pediatric burn fluids
entries.formula_human: Parkland 3-4 mL/kg/%TBSA; Galveston: 5000 mL/m2 BSA + 2000 mL/m2 TBSA

entries.name: SNAP-II / SNAPPE-II
entries.purpose: Neonatal illness severity
entries.formula_human: 6/7 physiologic items weighted; scores 0-?

entries.name: Silverman-Anderson index
entries.purpose: Neonatal respiratory distress
entries.formula_human: 5 signs x 0-2 (upper chest retraction, lower chest retraction, xiphoid retraction, nasal flaring, grunting/groaning); total 0-10

entries.name: 4AT (delirium)
entries.purpose: Rapid delirium screen
entries.formula_human: see critical care

entries.name: AIMS
entries.purpose: EPS (tardive dyskinesia)
entries.formula_human: 10 items x 0-4; total 0-40

entries.name: AUDIT-C
entries.purpose: Alcohol screen (brief)
entries.formula_human: 3 items x 0-4; total 0-12; >=4 men / >=3 women positive

entries.name: BPRS
entries.purpose: Psychosis symptoms (research)
entries.formula_human: 18-24 items 1-7; total 18-126

entries.name: COWS
entries.purpose: Opioid withdrawal
entries.formula_human: 11 items (resting pulse, GI, sweats, tremor, restlessness, yawning, pupils, anxiety, aches, gooseflesh, rhinorrhea) total 0-48

entries.name: GAF (legacy) / WHODAS 2.0
entries.purpose: Function/disability

entries.name: GDS-15
entries.purpose: Geriatric depression
entries.formula_human: 15 yes/no items; 0-15; >=5 depression

entries.name: HAM-A
entries.purpose: Anxiety severity (research)
entries.formula_human: 14 items 0-4; total 0-56

entries.name: MDQ
entries.purpose: Bipolar screen
entries.formula_human: 7+ yes on part 1 + co-occurring + moderate-severe impairment

entries.name: Mini-Cog
entries.purpose: Dementia screen (1 min)
entries.formula_human: 3-word recall (0-3) + clock drawing (0-2); <=2 positive

entries.name: 6-Minute Walk Test
entries.purpose: Functional capacity
entries.formula_human: Distance walked in 6 min; % predicted by age/sex/height/weight equations

entries.name: Barthel Index
entries.purpose: ADL independence
entries.formula_human: 10 ADLs weighted 0-15; total 0-100

entries.name: Berg Balance Scale
entries.purpose: Fall risk / balance
entries.formula_human: 14 items x 0-4; total 0-56; <45 fall risk

entries.name: FIM (Functional Independence Measure)
entries.purpose: Rehab outcomes
entries.formula_human: 18 items x 1-7 (motor 13 + cognitive 5); total 18-126

entries.name: TUG (Timed Up and Go)
entries.purpose: Mobility/fall risk
entries.formula_human: Time to stand, walk 3m, turn, sit; >13.5s = fall risk

entries.name: AKIN
entries.purpose: Refined AKI classification (modification of RIFLE) requiring serial creatinine measurements over 48 hours.
entries.formula_human:
AKIN staging (within 48h window):
Stage 1: SCr ↑≥0.3 mg/dL or 1.5–1.9× baseline; UO <0.5 mL/kg/h × 6h
Stage 2: SCr 2.0–2.9× baseline; UO <0.5 mL/kg/h × ≥12h
Stage 3: SCr ≥3× or ≥4.0 mg/dL (with acute rise ≥0.5) or RRT; UO <0.3 mL/kg/h × ≥24h or anuria ≥12h

inputs.label: Serum creatinine rise within 48 hours
inputs.description: SCr increase ≥0.3 mg/dL or 1.5–2× baseline within 48h
inputs.options_text: Stage 1: ≥0.3 mg/dL or 1.5–1.9×; Stage 2: 2.0–2.9×; Stage 3: ≥3× or ≥4.0 mg/dL or RRT

inputs.label: Urine output
inputs.description: Urine output per kg per hour
inputs.options_text: Stage 1: <0.5 mL/kg/h × 6h; Stage 2: <0.5 mL/kg/h × 12h; Stage 3: <0.3 mL/kg/h × 24h or anuria × 12h

bands.meaning: Mild AKI. Increase monitoring frequency.
Moderate AKI. Evaluate and correct contributing factors.
Severe AKI. Nephrology consult; RRT if indicated.

citations.text: Mehta RL, Kellum JA, Shah SV, et al. Acute Kidney Injury Network: report of an initiative to improve outcomes in acute kidney injury. Crit Care. 2007;11(2):R31. PMID: 17331245

entries.limitations: Largely superseded by KDIGO AKI (2012). AKIN's 48-hour window is more restrictive than KDIGO's 7-day window. Removed 'Loss' and 'End-stage' categories (outcome vs injury debate). The ≥0.3 mg/dL threshold improved early detection over original RIFLE.

entries.name: CKD staging (G/A)
entries.purpose: CKD classification

entries.name: FEUrea
entries.purpose: AKI on diuretics
entries.formula_human: FEurea = (Uurea*Scr)/(Surea*Cr)*100; <35% prerenal

entries.name: MDRD-4
entries.purpose: eGFR (legacy)
entries.formula_human: eGFR = 175*Scr^-1.154 * age^-0.203 * 0.742(if female) * 1.212(if Black)

entries.name: RIFLE
entries.purpose: Earlier classification system for AKI severity based on serum creatinine change and urine output (predecessor to KDIGO AKI staging).
entries.formula_human:
RIFLE classification:
R (Risk): SCr 1.5× baseline or ↑≥0.3 mg/dL or UO <0.5 mL/kg/h × 6h
I (Injury): SCr 2× baseline or UO <0.5 mL/kg/h × 12h
F (Failure): SCr 3× baseline or SCr ≥4 mg/dL + acute rise ≥0.5 mg/dL or UO <0.3 mL/kg/h × 24h or anuria × 12h
L (Loss): Complete loss of kidney function >4 weeks
E (End-stage): Complete loss of kidney function >3 months

inputs.label: Serum creatinine change
inputs.options_text: Risk: 1.5× baseline or ↑≥0.3 mg/dL; Injury: 2× baseline; Failure: 3× baseline or SCr ≥4 mg/dL with acute rise ≥0.5 mg/dL

inputs.label: Urine output
inputs.description: Urine output per kg per hour
inputs.options_text: Risk: <0.5 mL/kg/h × 6h; Injury: <0.5 mL/kg/h × 12h; Failure: <0.3 mL/kg/h × 24h or anuria × 12h

bands.meaning: AKI risk identified. Monitor.
Kidney injury. Intervene.
Kidney failure. Consider RRT.
Persistent loss >4 weeks
End-stage kidney disease >3 months

citations.text: Bellomo R, Ronco C, Kellum JA, et al. Acute renal failure — definition, outcome measures, animal models, fluid therapy and information technology needs: the Second International Consensus Conference of the Acute Dialysis Quality Initiative (ADQI) Group. Crit Care. 2004;8(4):R204-R212. PMID: 15312219

entries.limitations: Largely superseded by KDIGO AKI criteria (2012). SCr rise threshold of 1.5× may miss small absolute increases in patients with low baseline SCr. L and E categories describe outcomes, not acute severity. UO criteria require accurate timing. Multiple versions exist (originally used different creatinine cutoffs).

entries.name: BODE index
entries.purpose: Multidimensional prognostic index for COPD that predicts all-cause and respiratory mortality better than FEV₁ alone.

inputs.label: FEV₁ % predicted (post-bronchodilator)
inputs.description: Forced expiratory volume in 1 second as percent predicted

inputs.label: MMRC Dyspnea Scale
inputs.description: Modified Medical Research Council dyspnea grade
inputs.options_text: 0 = none; 1 = breathless on hurrying; 2 = walks slower than peers; 3 = stops for breath after 100 yards; 4 = too breathless to leave house or breathless dressing

bands.meaning: Low mortality risk (~10% 4-year mortality)
Moderate risk
High risk (~60% 4-year mortality)
Very high risk (~80% 4-year mortality). Consider palliative care discussion and advanced care planning.

citations.text: Celli BR, Cote CG, Marin JM, et al. The body-mass index, airflow obstruction, dyspnea, and exercise capacity index in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. N Engl J Med. 2004;350(10):1005-1012. PMID: 14999112

entries.limitations: Requires 6-minute walk test (needs space, trained staff, standardized protocol). MMRC has inter-observer variability. BMI cutoff ≤21 may not be appropriate for all ethnic groups. Does not capture exacerbation frequency. FEV₁ variability affects reproducibility. BODE has not been formally updated for GOLD 2023+ classification changes.

entries.name: CRB-65
entries.purpose: Simplified version of CURB-65 that does not require laboratory testing, for use in primary care or prehospital settings.
entries.formula_human: CRB-65 = Confusion(1) + RR≥30(1) + BP_low(1) + Age≥65(1)

inputs.label: Confusion
inputs.description: New confusion or altered mental status

bands.meaning: Low risk (<1% mortality). Consider home management.
Moderate risk (~8–12% mortality). Consider hospital assessment.
High risk (~17–35% mortality). Urgent hospital admission; consider ICU.

citations.text: Lim WS, et al. Thorax. 2003;58(5):377-382. PMID: 12728155 (same derivation as CURB-65, CRB-65 presented separately)

entries.limitations: Does not include BUN (may miss renal impairment). Same limitations as CURB-65 regarding oxygenation and imaging. Score of 0 does not always exclude need for admission (social factors, comorbidities). Primary care validation is less robust than ED validation.

entries.name: DLCO / FEV1-FVC
entries.purpose: PFT interpretation
entries.formula_human: FEV1/FVC <0.7 = obstruction; GOLD by FEV1%: >=80 mild, 50-79 moderate, 30-49 severe, <30 very severe

entries.name: Murray Lung Injury Score
entries.purpose: ARDS severity
entries.formula_human: Average of: CXR quadrants (0-4), PaO2/FiO2 (0-3), PEEP (0-3), compliance (0-4); total 0-4

entries.name: RSBI
entries.purpose: Predicts weaning success from mechanical ventilation by assessing respiratory pattern during a spontaneous breathing trial.
entries.formula_human: RSBI = Respiratory_rate (breaths/min) / Tidal_volume (L)

inputs.label: Respiratory rate
inputs.description: Breaths per minute during 1-minute trial on CPAP/T-piece

inputs.label: Tidal volume
inputs.description: Tidal volume in liters during 1-minute trial

bands.meaning: Predicts successful weaning (high negative predictive value)
Predicts weaning failure

citations.text: Yang KL, Tobin MJ. A prospective study of indexes predicting the outcome of trials of weaning from mechanical ventilation. N Engl J Med. 1991;324(21):1445-1450. PMID: 2023603

entries.limitations: Measured over only 1 minute (may not represent sustained breathing). Influenced by pain, anxiety, airway resistance. Cutoff of 105 has imperfect sensitivity (~65%) and specificity (~75%). Should not be used as sole predictor — must be combined with clinical assessment.

entries.name: SCAP score
entries.purpose: Severe CAP
entries.formula_human: Major: RR>=30, confusion, BUN>30, shock; minor: PaO2<54? multilobar, platelets<100k, alb<3, age>80; >=1 major or >=2 minor = severe

entries.name: SMART-COP
entries.purpose: Predicts need for intensive respiratory or vasopressor support (IRVS) within 24 hours of hospital admission for CAP.
entries.formula_human: SMART-COP = SBP<90(2) + Multilobar(1) + Albumin<3.5(1) + RR_ age-adjusted(1) + HR≥125(1) + Confusion(1) + Oxy_ age-adjusted(2) + pH<7.35(2). Points divided into: Low risk (≤2 young or ≤3 old), Moderate risk (3–4 young or 4–5 old), High risk (≥5 young or ≥6 old).

inputs.label: Multilobar/bilateral infiltrates
inputs.description: Chest radiograph showing involvement of ≥2 lobes

inputs.label: Oxygenation
inputs.description: PaO₂ <70 mmHg or SpO₂ <93% (or PaO₂/FiO₂ <333) — age ≤50; PaO₂ <60 mmHg or SpO₂ <90% (or PaO₂/FiO₂ <250) — age >50

bands.meaning: Low risk of needing IRVS (~5%). Ward-level care.
Moderate risk (~10–15%). Close monitoring, possible HDU/step-down.
High risk (~25–35%). High likelihood of requiring ICU/IRVS.

citations.text: Charles PG, Wolfe R, Whitby M, et al. SMART-COP: a tool for predicting the need for intensive respiratory or vasopressor support in community-acquired pneumonia. Clin Infect Dis. 2008;47(3):375-384. PMID: 18558884

entries.limitations: Requires ABG (not always available). Age-adjusted oxygenation criteria can be confusing. Not as widely known as CURB-65/PSI. Australian derivation cohort may differ from other populations. Albumin may not be checked routinely.

entries.name: sPESI / PESI
entries.purpose: PE mortality / outpatient eligibility
entries.formula_human: sPESI: age>80=1, cancer=1, cardiopulm disease=1, HR>=110=1, SBP<100=1, O2sat<90=1; 0-6? (0 = low risk). PESI 11-variable 0-5 class points

entries.name: ACR 2010/2016 Fibromyalgia criteria
entries.purpose: Fibromyalgia diagnosis
entries.formula_human: WPI (19 regions 0-19) + SSS (0-12): criteria: WPI>=7 & SSS>=5 OR WPI 3-6 & SSS>=9 + generalized pain + >=3 months

entries.name: BASFI / BASMI
entries.purpose: AxSpA function/spinal mobility
entries.formula_human: BASFI: 10 items 0-10; BASMI: cervical rotation, tragus-wall, lumbar flexion, Schober, intermalleolar distance each 0-10

entries.name: Physician Global / PtGA
entries.purpose: (components above)

entries.name: SCORAD
entries.purpose: Atopic eczema (combined)
entries.formula_human: SCORAD = A/5 + 7B/2 + C (A extent 0-100, B intensity sum 0-18, C symptoms 0-20); total 0-103

entries.name: ARISCAT
entries.purpose: Risk prediction model for postoperative pulmonary complications (PPC) in patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery. Identifies patients at risk for pneumonia, atelectasis, respiratory failure, and other pulmonary complications. Guides preoperative pulmonary optimization.
entries.formula_human:
ARISCAT = Age + SpO₂ + Respiratory infection + Anemia + Incision site + Duration + Emergency
Range: 0–123

inputs.label: Respiratory infection in the last month
Surgical incision site
inputs.options_text: Peripheral/abdominal (0 points), Upper abdominal (15 points), Intrathoracic (24 points)

inputs.label: Duration of surgery
inputs.options_text: </think>�<2 hours (0 points), 2–3 hours (14 points), >3 hours (23 points)

bands.meaning: Low risk of PPC (~1.6%). Standard perioperative care.
Moderate risk of PPC (~9.4%). Consider incentive spirometry, early mobilization, chest physiotherapy.

High risk of PPC (~21.8%). Aggressive pulmonary optimization: smoking cessation (≥4 weeks if possible), bronchodilators if COPD/asthma, inspiratory muscle training, epidural anesthesia if feasible, postoperative ICU monitoring, early mobilization, lung-protective ventilation intraoperatively.

citations.text: Canet J, Gallart L, Gomar C, et al. Prediction of postoperative pulmonary complications in a population-based surgical cohort. Anesthesiology. 2010;113(6):1338-1350. PMID: 20966661

entries.copyright: public domain — published academic scoring system
entries.limitations: Developed in non-cardiac surgery — not validated for cardiac surgery (use separate scores). Does not include smoking history, COPD severity, or BMI. Does not capture intraoperative factors (fluid balance, ventilation strategy). Emergency surgery factor is weighted moderately (8 points) — some centers consider it higher risk. Does not predict specific complication type (pneumonia vs. atelectasis vs. ARDS). Not validated in pediatric populations. SpO₂ measurement may be affected by preoperative supplemental oxygen. Duration of surgery is a post-hoc factor — not available preoperatively (use estimated duration). Limited external validation outside Europe. Does not replace clinical judgment or specific pulmonary function testing in high-risk patients. Anemia threshold (≤10 g/dL) may not capture patients with borderline values. Respiratory infection may be underreported by patients.

entries.name: Gupta calculators (postop resp failure / pneumonia)
entries.purpose: NSQIP-derived
entries.formula_human: Logistic models: functional status, ASA, sepsis, COPD, age, etc.

entries.name: Mannheim Peritonitis Index
entries.purpose: Peritonitis mortality
entries.formula_human: 8 items weighted (age>50, female, organ failure, malignancy, origin colon, duration, fecal/visceral contamination, diffuse peritonitis) total 0-47?

entries.name: P-POSSUM
entries.purpose: (mortality only, recalibrated)

entries.name: POSSUM
entries.purpose: Surgical morbidity/mortality
entries.formula_human: ln(R/1-R) = -9.065 + 0.16*PS + 0.19*OS; PS = 12 physiologic vars, OS = 6 operative severity vars

entries.name: SORT
entries.purpose: Perioperative mortality
entries.formula_human: Age + ASA + urgency + specialty + cancer + severity of surgery; points 0-? (SORT score 0-? )

entries.name: Surgical Apgar Score
entries.purpose: Perioperative risk (general surgery)

entries.name: ABC score
entries.purpose: Predicts massive transfusion need
entries.formula_human: Penetrating=1, SBP<=90=1, HR>=120=1, FAST+=1; total 0-4

entries.name: AIS
entries.purpose: International standard for neurological classification of spinal cord injury. Grades severity of injury, determines level of injury, and predicts functional outcomes. Published by the American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) and International Spinal Cord Society (ISCoS).
entries.formula_human:
Neurological Level of Injury (NLI): Most caudal level with normal motor AND sensory function bilaterally

AIS Grade:
A (Complete): No motor or sensory function in S4-S5 (no DAP, no VAC)
B (Sensory Incomplete): Sensory but not motor function below NLI including S4-S5 (DAP present, no VAC)
C (Motor Incomplete): Motor function preserved below NLI, >half key muscles below NLI have grade <3 (VAC may or may not be present)
D (Motor Incomplete): Motor function preserved below NLI, at least half key muscles below NLI grade ≥3
E (Normal): Normal motor and sensory examination (typically used for recovered patients)

Zone of Partial Preservation: Dermatomes/myotomes caudal to NLI that are partially innervated (AIS A only)

Motor Level: Most caudal key muscle with grade ≥3, provided all segments above have grade 5
Sensory Level: Most caudal dermatome with normal (2/2) light touch AND pin prick

inputs.label: Motor examination (key muscles)
inputs.description: 5 key upper extremity muscles (C5-T1) and 5 key lower extremity muscles (L2-S1) graded 0–5 bilaterally. C5: elbow flexors, C6: wrist extensors, C7: elbow extensors, C8: finger flexors (FDP to middle finger), T1: finger abductors (ADM). L2: hip flexors, L3: knee extensors, L4: ankle dorsiflexors, L5: long toe extensors, S1: ankle plantar flexors

inputs.label: Sensory examination
inputs.description: Light touch and pin prick at 28 dermatomes (C2-S4-5) bilaterally. Each scored 0 (absent), 1 (impaired), 2 (normal). S4-5 deep anal pressure assessed as present/absent.

bands.meaning: Complete injury — no motor or sensory function in S4-S5. <5% chance of walking recovery at 1 year. High risk of complications (UTI, pressure ulcers, autonomic dysreflexia).
Sensory incomplete — sensory preserved at S4-5 but no motor. ~33% chance of walking recovery at 1 year.
Motor incomplete — motor function preserved below NLI, majority of muscles below <3/5. Walking possible with braces/aids. ~75% may achieve ambulation with assistive devices.
Motor incomplete — majority of muscles below NLI grade ≥3/5. Most will walk independently. Good prognosis for functional recovery.
Normal neurological exam. Used when documenting recovery.

citations.text: American Spinal Injury Association. Standards for Neurological Classification of Spinal Cord Injury. Revised 2019. Kirshblum SC, et al. J Spinal Cord Med. 2011;34(6):535-546 (ISNCSCI); Kirshblum SN, et al. Spinal Cord. 2014;52:65-70 (revision)

entries.copyright: ASIA — free for clinical use with proper attribution
entries.limitations: Requires standardized examination protocol — training required. Spinal shock may mask true injury severity in acute period (ASIA exam should be repeated after resolution). Cognitive impairment, pain, or sedation may limit cooperation. Motor examination only covers specific key muscles — doesn't capture all motor function. Zone of partial preservation (in complete injuries) may influence prognosis. Does not capture autonomic function (use ISAFSCI — International Standards for Autonomic Assessment). Doesn't account for cause of injury, imaging findings, or comorbidities.

entries.name: Marshall / Rotterdam CT classification
entries.purpose: TBI CT severity
entries.formula_human: Marshall: diffuse I-IV + evacuated/non-evacuated mass; Rotterdam: basal cisterns, midline shift, epidural mass, tSAH/IVH (1-6)

entries.name: NISS
entries.purpose: Modified ISS that uses the three most severe injuries regardless of body region, improving prediction for patients with multiple injuries in one region.
entries.formula_human: NISS = AIS₁² + AIS₂² + AIS₃² (where AIS₁, AIS₂, AIS₃ are the three highest AIS scores regardless of body region)

inputs.label: Three highest AIS scores
inputs.description: The three highest AIS scores from any body region (not necessarily different regions)

bands.meaning: Minor-moderate injury
Severe injury
Major polytrauma

citations.text: Osler T, Baker SP, Long W. A modification of the injury severity score that both improves accuracy and simplifies scoring. J Trauma. 1997;43(6):922-925. PMID: 9420106

entries.copyright: licensed — verify before use (AIS copyright applies)
entries.limitations: Still requires AIS coding by trained specialists. Does not incorporate age or comorbidities. Not universally adopted (ISS still more common). High correlation with ISS limits added value in many studies.

entries.name: Pediatric Trauma Score
entries.purpose: Pediatric field triage
entries.formula_human: Size, airway, CNS, wounds, skeletal, skin each -1 to +2; total -1 to +11; <8 = high mortality

entries.name: Revised Trauma Score
entries.purpose: Physiologic scoring system for trauma patients. Uses GCS, systolic blood pressure, and respiratory rate to predict survival. Components are coded using the Triage Revised Trauma Score (T-RTS) for prehospital triage or weighted RTS for hospital outcomes.
entries.formula_human:
Triage RTS (T-RTS) = GCS coded + SBP coded + RR coded
Range: 0–12

Weighted RTS = 0.9368×GCS code + 0.7326×SBP code + 0.2908×RR code
Range: 0–7.8408

Coding values:
GCS: 3-4→1, 5-7→2, 8-10→3, 11-13→4, 14-15→4 (simplified 15=4, etc.)
SBP: 0→0, 1-49→1, 50-75→2, 76-89→3, ≥90→4
RR: 0→0, 1-5→1, 6-9→2, 10-29→3, >29→4

Note: Coding is not linear — mapped from probability of survival.

bands.meaning: Normal physiologic parameters. Low physiologic severity.
Near-normal. Mild physiologic derangement.
Significant physiologic derangement. Trauma center activation criteria met (T-RTS ≤11 is used for triage).
Critical physiologic derangement. Predicts high mortality.
High mortality risk (>50%).

citations.text: Champion HR, Sacco WJ, Copes WS, et al. A revision of the Trauma Score. J Trauma. 1989;29(5):623-629. PMID: 2657085

entries.copyright: public domain — published academic scoring system
entries.limitations: GCS may be confounded by intoxication, sedation, intubation. Does not capture anatomic injury (use ISS/NISS for anatomic component). SBP may be maintained by compensation in young patients (normotension despite shock). RR is frequently inaccurately recorded. Does not include age, comorbidities, or mechanism. Superseded by more comprehensive models (e.g., TRISS combines RTS + ISS + age). Not validated in pediatric patients without modification. Single-time measurement — doesn't capture trajectory of deterioration. Intubated patients assigned RR=0 (may not reflect true respiratory status). T-RTS primarily used for triage decisions — weighted RTS for outcomes. Not widely used as standalone anymore (TRISS, ISS, and newer models preferred).

entries.name: TASH score
entries.purpose: Predicts massive transfusion
entries.formula_human: Weighted: SBP, HR, Hb, base excess, sex, FAST+, pelvic fracture, femur fracture (0-28)

entries.name: TRISS
entries.purpose: Combines physiologic (RTS) and anatomic (ISS) severity with age to predict survival probability in trauma patients.
entries.formula_human:
b = b₀ + b₁×RTS + b₂×ISS + b₃×Age_code
P(survival) = 1/(1 + e^(−b))

For blunt trauma: b₀ = −1.2470, b₁ = 0.9544, b₂ = −0.0768, b₃ = −1.9052
For penetrating trauma: b₀ = −0.6029, b₁ = 1.1430, b₂ = −0.1516, b₃ = −2.6676

inputs.label: RTS (Revised Trauma Score)
inputs.description: Physiologic severity from GCS, SBP, RR

bands.meaning: Expected survivor
Expected non-survivor
Higher P(survival) = better prognosis

citations.text: Boyd CR, Tolson MA, Copes WS. Evaluating trauma care: the TRISS method. J Trauma. 1987;27(4):370-378. PMID: 3106646

entries.limitations: Requires ISS coding (AIS specialists). Uses binary age cutoff (55) — misses age-related risk gradients. ISS known limitations apply. Blunt vs penetrating coefficients may not apply to mixed mechanisms. Pre-dates modern trauma systems (coefficients from 1980s MTOS).

entries.name: IMPROVE VTE RAM
entries.purpose: Medical VTE risk
entries.formula_human: Prev VTE 3, thrombophilia 2, lower-limb paralysis 2, immobilization 1, ICU/CCU 1, CVC 1, varicose veins 1, acute infection 1, chronic heart failure 1, chronic lung disease 1; >=2-3? (0-1 low, 2-3 moderate, >=4 high)

entries.name: CHARGE-AF
entries.purpose: Incident AF prediction
entries.formula_human: Cox model: age, height, weight, SBP/DBP, smoking, antihypertensives, DM, HF, MI, stroke

entries.name: HATCH
entries.purpose: AF progression risk
entries.formula_human: HTN=1, Age>75=2, TIA/stroke=2, COPD=1, HF=2; total 0-12

entries.name: Reynolds risk score
entries.purpose: Estimates 10-year risk of cardiovascular events by incorporating family history and hs-CRP in addition to traditional risk factors.
entries.formula_human: Cox proportional hazards model: 10-year risk = 1 − S₀(10)^exp(β₁×ln(age) + β₂×ln(TC) + β₃×ln(HDL) + β₄×ln(SBP) + β₅×smoker + β₆×ln(hsCRP) + β₇×FH). Sex-specific coefficients. S₀(10) is baseline 10-year survival. Exact coefficients published in Ridker PM, et al. 2007/2008. Calculator available at reynoldsriskscore.org.

inputs.label: HbA1c (if diabetic)
inputs.description: Glycated hemoglobin, used in diabetic subgroup model

bands.meaning: Low risk
Intermediate risk
Intermediate-high risk
High risk

citations.text: Ridker PM, Buring JE, Rifai N, Cook NR. Development and validation of improved algorithms for the assessment of global cardiovascular risk in women: the Reynolds Risk Score. JAMA. 2007;297(6):611-619. PMID: 17299196. Male model: Ridker PM, et al. Circulation. 2008;118(22):2243-2251. PMID: 18997196

entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app — calculator at reynoldsriskscore.org
entries.limitations: Requires hs-CRP (not universally measured) and family history data. Re-classification benefit over Framingham is modest. Not widely incorporated into US guidelines (PCE preferred). hs-CRP has significant biological variability.

entries.name: ACUITY/HORIZONS bleeding
entries.purpose: PCI bleeding
entries.formula_human: Age, female sex, Cr, WBC, anemia, STEMI/NSTEMI presentation; 0-50+

entries.name: ATRIA bleeding
entries.purpose: AF bleeding
entries.formula_human: Anemia 3, severe renal disease 3, age>=75 2, prior hemorrhage 1, HTN 1; total 0-10

entries.name: HEMORR2HAGES
entries.purpose: Estimates bleeding risk in patients with atrial fibrillation on warfarin therapy.
entries.formula_human: HEMORR₂HAGES = Hepatic_renal(1) + Ethanol(1) + Malignancy(1) + Older_age(1) + Reduced_platelets(1) + Rebleeding(2) + Hypertension(1) + Anemia(1) + Genetic_factors(1) + Excessive_fall_risk(1) + Stroke(1)

inputs.label: Genetic factors (CYP2C9 polymorphisms)
inputs.description: Known pharmacogenetic variants affecting warfarin metabolism

inputs.label: Excessive fall risk
inputs.description: History of falls or high fall risk

bands.meaning: Low bleeding risk (~1.9% per year)
Moderate risk (~2.5–5.4% per year)
High risk (~8.4–12.3% per year)

citations.text: Gage BF, Yan Y, Milligan PE, et al. Clinical classification schemes for predicting hemorrhagic results from the National Registry of Atrial Fibrillation (NRAF). Am Heart J. 2006;151(3):713-719. PMID: 16504638

entries.limitations: Complex (11 variables, including genetic testing rarely available). Largely superseded by HAS-BLED due to simplicity. Score components like 'genetic factors' and 'excessive fall risk' are hard to standardize. Developed for warfarin — not validated for DOACs.

entries.name: LODS
entries.purpose: Quantifies severity of organ dysfunction in ICU patients with a logistic model calibrated for hospital mortality prediction.
entries.formula_human: LODS = Sum of organ-specific scores (0–5 per organ, 6 organs). Logistic model: logit = −5.7865 + 0.1374 × LODS + diagnostic category coefficients. Predicted mortality = e^logit / (1 + e^logit).

bands.meaning: Low predicted hospital mortality
Moderate mortality
High predicted mortality

citations.text: Le Gall JR, Klar J, Lemeshow S, et al. The Logistic Organ Dysfunction system: a new way to assess organ dysfunction in the intensive care unit. JAMA. 1996;276(10):802-810. PMID: 8769590

entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app
entries.limitations: Complex scoring. Superseded by SAPS 3 and SOFA in clinical use. Original calibration from 1990s data.

entries.name: MPM II / MPM III
entries.purpose: ICU mortality at admission
entries.formula_human: Logistic equation of 15/16 admission variables

entries.name: Rosier (FAST) prehospital stroke screen
entries.purpose: Stroke recognition
entries.formula_human: Facial droop, Arm weakness, Speech, Time + glucose/BP; >=1 = stroke code

entries.name: AIM65
entries.purpose: UGIB risk
entries.formula_human: Albumin<30=1, INR>1.5=1, altered mentation=1, SBP<=90=1, age>65=1; total 0-5

entries.name: BARD score
entries.purpose: NAFLD fibrosis
entries.formula_human: BMI>=28=1, AST/ALT>=0.8=2, DM=1; total 0-4; 2-4 at risk

entries.name: CLIP score
entries.purpose: HCC prognosis
entries.formula_human: TNM points + Child-Pugh (1-3) + portal thrombosis (0-1) + AFP (0-1); 0-6

entries.name: Okuda
entries.purpose: HCC prognosis (legacy)
entries.formula_human: Tumor size, albumin, bilirubin, ascites; stages I-III

entries.name: QUICKI
entries.purpose: Insulin sensitivity
entries.formula_human: QUICKI = 1/(log10 insulin + log10 glucose)

entries.name: CHA2DS2-VASc / VASOGRADE
entries.purpose: Estimates annual stroke risk in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation to guide anticoagulation decisions.
entries.formula_human: CHA₂DS₂-VASc = CHF(1) + Hypertension(1) + Age_≥75(2) + Diabetes(1) + Stroke/TIA/VTE(2) + Vascular_disease(1) + Age_65-74(1) + Female_sex(1)

inputs.label: Congestive heart failure (or LVEF ≤40%)
inputs.description: Clinical HF or reduced ejection fraction

inputs.label: Hypertension
inputs.description: History of hypertension or BP >140/90 on treatment

inputs.label: Diabetes mellitus
inputs.description: History of DM or fasting glucose >126 mg/dL or HbA1c ≥6.5%

inputs.label: Stroke/TIA/thromboembolism
inputs.description: Prior history of ischemic stroke, TIA, or systemic thromboembolism

inputs.label: Vascular disease
inputs.description: Prior MI, PAD, or aortic plaque

bands.meaning: Low risk. Anticoagulation generally not recommended. Annual stroke risk ~0% (male) / ~0.6% (female).
Low-moderate risk. Consider anticoagulation based on individual factors. Annual stroke risk ~1.3%.

Moderate-high risk. Oral anticoagulation recommended (DOAC preferred over warfarin). Annual stroke risk escalates: 2.2% (score 2), 3.2% (3), 4.0% (4), 6.7% (5), 9.8% (6), 9.6% (7), 12.5% (8), 15.2% (9).

citations.text: Lip GYH, Nieuwlaat R, Pisters R, et al. Refining clinical risk stratification for predicting stroke and thromboembolism in atrial fibrillation using a novel risk factor-based approach: the Euro Heart Survey on Atrial Fibrillation. Chest. 2010;137(2):263-272. PMID: 19762550

entries.limitations: Low c-statistic (~0.6) for predicting stroke — discriminative ability is modest. Score of 1 in males vs. 1 solely from female sex have very different risk profiles. Does not account for AF burden (paroxysmal vs persistent). Most beneficial for identifying truly low-risk patients who can safely avoid anticoagulation.

entries.name: Sokal / Hasford / ELTS scores
entries.purpose: CML risk

entries.name: Pediatric Appendicitis Score (PAS)
entries.purpose: Appendicitis in children
entries.formula_human: RLQ pain migration=1, anorexia=1, nausea/vomiting=1, RLQ tenderness=2, cough/percussion/hopping tenderness=2, fever>=38=1, WBC>10k=1, neutrophils>75%=1; total 0-10

entries.name: GHQ-12
entries.purpose: General distress

entries.name: CHART / Craig Handicap
entries.purpose: Community integration (SCI/TBI)

entries.name: DAS28 variants
entries.purpose: DAS28 variants

entries.name: MASI
entries.purpose: Melasma severity
entries.formula_human: MASI = 0.3*(D+A)*Ar + 0.3*(D+A)*Al + 0.3*(D+A)*Rr + 0.1*(D+A)*Rl (forehead, L/R malar, chin; darkness/area 0-4)

entries.name: Goldman / Detsky cardiac risk
entries.purpose: Perioperative cardiac (legacy)
entries.formula_human: Goldman 9 factors weighted 3-11; Detsky 13 items weighted 5-?

entries.name: Sgarbossa criteria
entries.purpose: Identifies acute myocardial infarction in patients with left bundle branch block (LBBB) on ECG.
entries.formula_human: Sgarbossa = Concordant_ST_elevation(5 if yes) + Concordant_ST_depression_V1-V3(3 if yes) + Discordant_ST_elevation_≥5mm(2 if yes)

inputs.label: Concordant ST elevation ≥1 mm
inputs.description: ST-segment elevation ≥1 mm in any lead with a positive QRS complex (concordant with QRS)

inputs.label: Concordant ST depression ≥1 mm in V1–V3
inputs.description: ST depression ≥1 mm in V1, V2, or V3 (concordant with the negative QRS in these leads)

inputs.label: Discordant ST elevation ≥5 mm
inputs.description: ST elevation ≥5 mm in any lead with a negative QRS (discordant)

bands.meaning: High specificity (>90%) for acute MI. Recommended to activate cath lab.
Insufficient specificity to diagnose AMI in LBBB. Consider modified Sgarbossa.

citations.text: Sgarbossa EB, Pinski SL, Barbagelata A, et al. Electrocardiographic diagnosis of evolving acute myocardial infarction in the presence of left bundle-branch block. N Engl J Med. 1996;334(8):481-487. PMID: 8559200

entries.limitations: High specificity but low sensitivity (~20–36%) for AMI. Discordant ST elevation criterion (≥5 mm) was the most weighted but least specific. Modified Sgarbossa (using ST/S ratio ≤-0.25 in discordant leads) improves sensitivity.

entries.name: ATLS shock classification
entries.purpose: Hemorrhage class
entries.formula_human: Class I-IV by blood loss %, HR, BP, pulse pressure, UOP, mental status

entries.name: Baux / modified Baux
entries.purpose: Burn mortality
entries.formula_human: Baux = age + %TBSA; modified adds +17 if inhalation injury

entries.name: Braunwald Classification of Unstable Angina
entries.purpose: Classifies unstable angina by severity, clinical circumstance, and intensity of treatment to guide prognosis and management.
entries.formula_human: Categorical classification (e.g., IB = primary, new-onset/worsening angina on minimal therapy). Not a numerical score.

inputs.label: Severity class
inputs.options_text: I = new-onset or worsening angina; II = angina at rest within past month but not 48 hours; III = angina at rest within 48 hours

inputs.label: Clinical circumstance
inputs.description: Context in which unstable angina occurs
inputs.options_text: A = secondary (extracardiac provocation); B = primary (no extracardiac provocation); C = within 2 weeks of MI

inputs.label: Treatment intensity
inputs.description: Intensity of anti-ischemic therapy at time of angina
inputs.options_text: 1 = no or minimal treatment; 2 = standard oral therapy; 3 = maximal IV anti-ischemic therapy

bands.meaning: Rest angina within 48 hours on maximal IV therapy in post-MI setting — highest risk subgroup
New-onset/worsening angina secondary to extracardiac cause — lowest risk

citations.text: Braunwald E. Unstable angina. A classification. Circulation. 1989;80(2):410-414. PMID: 2502287

entries.limitations: Predates the troponin era and modern ACS management. Largely historical — more commonly referenced conceptually than used as a formal scoring tool. Not quantitative.

entries.name: Killip Classification
entries.purpose: Clinical classification of heart failure severity in acute myocardial infarction to estimate in-hospital mortality.
entries.formula_human:
Assign class I–IV based on clinical findings:
Class I: No heart failure, no rales, no S3
Class II: Mild HF, rales in lower lung fields, S3 gallop
Class III: Pulmonary edema
Class IV: Cardiogenic shock (SBP <90 mmHg, signs of hypoperfusion)

inputs.label: Clinical assessment
inputs.description: Bedside assessment of hemodynamic and pulmonary congestion status
inputs.points_text: Class I = 0; II = 1; III = 2; IV = 3 (classification, not additive)

bands.meaning: No heart failure; in-hospital mortality ~6%
Mild HF/rales; mortality ~17%
Pulmonary edema; mortality ~38%
Cardiogenic shock; mortality ~67–80%

citations.text: Killip T 3rd, Kimball JT. Treatment of myocardial infarction in a coronary care unit. A two year experience with 250 patients. Am J Cardiol. 1967;20(4):457-464. PMID: 6059064

entries.limitations: Subjective assessment (inter-rater variability). Derived from 1960s data before modern reperfusion therapy. Does not capture hemodynamic detail (e.g., PCWP, cardiac index). Mortality estimates likely lower in contemporary practice.

entries.name: Modified Sgarbossa Criteria
entries.purpose: Improved sensitivity for diagnosing acute MI in LBBB by replacing the absolute discordant ST elevation threshold with an ST/S ratio criterion.
entries.formula_human: Modified Sgarbossa = Concordant_ST_elevation(5) + Concordant_ST_depression_V1-V3(3) + ST/S_ratio_≤-0.25(2)

inputs.label: Concordant ST elevation ≥1 mm
inputs.description: ST elevation ≥1 mm in any lead with positive QRS

inputs.label: Concordant ST depression ≥1 mm in V1–V3
inputs.description: ST depression ≥1 mm in V1, V2, or V3

inputs.label: Proportionally excessive discordant ST elevation (ST/S ratio ≤ -0.25)
inputs.description: In any lead with negative QRS, ratio of ST elevation to S-wave depth ≤ -0.25 (i.e., ST elevation is ≥25% of the S-wave depth)

bands.meaning: Positive for acute MI. High sensitivity (~80%) with maintained specificity (~90%).
Negative for acute MI criteria in LBBB.

citations.text: Smith SW, Dodd KW, Henry TD, et al. Diagnosis of ST-elevation myocardial infarction in the presence of left bundle branch block with the ST-elevation to S-wave ratio in a modification of the Sgarbossa criteria. Ann Emerg Med. 2012;59(2):116-123. PMID: 21944788

entries.limitations: ST/S ratio can be difficult to measure when S-wave is very shallow. Requires careful measurement technique. Validation cohorts are relatively small. Not yet incorporated into all guidelines.

entries.name: TIMI Risk Index
entries.purpose: Simplified bedside risk index for 30-day mortality in STEMI using three readily available variables.
entries.formula_human: TIMI Risk Index = (Heart_rate × Age / 10) / Systolic_BP

inputs.label: Heart rate
inputs.description: Heart rate at presentation in beats per minute

inputs.label: Systolic blood pressure
inputs.description: Systolic blood pressure at presentation in mmHg

bands.meaning: Low risk for 30-day mortality (~1%)
Intermediate risk (~3–5%)
High risk (~10–15%)

citations.text: Morrow DA, Antman EM, Giugliano RP, et al. A simple risk index for rapid initial triage of patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction: an InTIME II substudy. Lancet. 2001;358(9293):1571-1575. PMID: 11716882

entries.limitations: Originally validated in STEMI only; less studied in NSTEMI/UA. Does not include troponin or ECG variables. Simplified — may miss nuanced risk captured by GRACE or full TIMI.

entries.name: TIMI Risk Score for ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction
entries.purpose: Predicts 30-day mortality in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction to guide management.
entries.formula_human: TIMI-STEMI = Age_65-74(2) + Age_≥75(3) + DM_or_HTN_or_angina(1) + SBP<100(3) + HR>100(2) + Killip_II-IV(2) + Anterior_or_LBBB(1) + Time>4h(1) + Weight<67kg(1)

inputs.label: Diabetes mellitus or hypertension or angina
inputs.description: History of DM, HTN, or angina

inputs.label: SBP <100 mmHg
inputs.description: Systolic blood pressure less than 100 at presentation

inputs.label: Heart rate >100 bpm
inputs.description: Heart rate greater than 100 at presentation

inputs.label: Anterior ST elevation or LBBB
inputs.description: Anterior STEMI or new/presumably new LBBB

bands.meaning: 30-day mortality ~0.8%
Low risk (~2–7%)
Intermediate risk (~12–16%)
High risk (~23–30%)
Very high risk (~35–50%+)

citations.text: Morrow DA, Antman EM, Charlesworth A, et al. TIMI risk score for ST-elevation myocardial infarction: A convenient, bedside, clinical score for risk assessment at presentation. Circulation. 2000;102(17):2031-2037. PMID: 11044416

entries.limitations: Derived from fibrinolytic-era trial. May underestimate risk in primary PCI era. Some variables (weight) may be difficult to obtain rapidly. Does not include renal function or cardiac biomarkers beyond presentation.

entries.name: Anticoagulation and Risk Factors in Atrial Fibrillation Stroke Score
entries.purpose: Validated stroke risk stratification score for AF using clinical factors from integrated health system data.
entries.formula_human: ATRIA = Anemia(3) + Severe_renal_disease(3) + Age_≥75(2) + Prior_ischemic_stroke(1) + Diabetes(1) + Hypertension(1) + Female(1)

bands.meaning: Low risk (0.6–1.9% annual stroke rate)
Intermediate risk
Intermediate-high risk
High risk (≥8.1% annual stroke rate)

citations.text: Singer DE, Chang Y, Borowsky LH, et al. A new risk scheme to predict ischemic warfarin: ATRIA study. Am J Med. 2013;126(8):725.e9-725.e18. PMID: 23820433

entries.limitations: Derived from a single US health system (Kaiser). Includes renal disease and anemia not present in other scores. External validation limited. Not widely adopted outside the US.

entries.name: European Heart Rhythm Association Symptom Score for Atrial Fibrillation
entries.purpose: Grades symptom severity in patients with atrial fibrillation to guide treatment strategy.
entries.formula_human:
Single categorical classification based on clinician assessment:
1 = No symptoms
2 = Mild (no effect on daily activity)
3 = Severe (daily activity affected)
4 = Disabling (daily activity not possible)

inputs.label: AF-related symptoms
inputs.description: Overall symptom burden related to AF episodes
inputs.options_text: 1 = no symptoms; 2 = mild (normal daily activity not affected); 3 = severe (normal daily activity affected); 4 = disabling (normal daily activity not possible)

bands.meaning: No AF-related symptoms
Mild symptoms; does not affect normal daily activity
Severe symptoms; normal daily activity affected
Disabling symptoms; normal daily activity not possible

citations.text: Kirchhof P, Auricchio A, Bax J, et al. Outcome parameters for trials in atrial fibrillation: executive summary. Eur Heart J. 2007;28(22):2803-2815. PMID: 17925351

entries.limitations: Subjective; requires clinical judgment. Simplified (only 4 categories). Does not capture paroxysmal AF frequency or duration. Revised as EHRA² score in some newer iterations.

entries.name: Outcomes Registry for Better Informed Treatment of Atrial Fibrillation Bleeding Score
entries.purpose: Estimates major bleeding risk in AF patients, validated across both warfarin and DOAC-treated populations.
entries.formula_human: ORBIT = Age_≥75(1) + Reduced_Hgb(2) + eGFR<60(1) + Antiplatelet(1) + Prior_bleed(2)

inputs.label: Reduced hemoglobin/hematocrit
inputs.description: Hgb <13 g/dL (male) or <12 g/dL (female) or Hct <36% (male) or <36% (female)

bands.meaning: Low bleeding risk (~1–2.5% per year)
Moderate risk (~4% per year)
High risk (~6–8%+ per year)

citations.text: O'Brien EC, Simon DN, Thomas LE, et al. The ORBIT bleeding score to stratify major bleeding risk in outpatients with atrial fibrillation: the ORBIT-AF registry. Am J Med. 2015;128(9):996.e9-996.e15. PMID: 25840038

entries.limitations: Developed in a US registry. Less commonly used than HAS-BLED. Not yet widely incorporated into guidelines. Does not include liver disease or alcohol.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: Age, Creatinine, Ejection Fraction Score
entries.purpose: Simple preoperative risk score for cardiac surgery mortality using only three variables: age, creatinine, and ejection fraction.
entries.formula_human: ACEF = (Age / 10) + Creatinine(mg/dL, minimum 2) + (30 / LVEF%)

inputs.label: Serum creatinine
inputs.options_text: continuous; minimum value 2 mg/dL for calculation
inputs.points_text: +2 if Cr ≥2 mg/dL, or continuous formula component

bands.meaning: Low operative risk (~1% mortality)
Intermediate risk (~2–3%)
High risk (~4–10%+)

citations.text: Ranucci M, Castelvecchio S, Menicanti L, et al. Risk of assessing mortality risk in elective cardiac operations: age, creatinine, ejection fraction, and the law of parsimony. Circulation. 2009;119(24):3053-3061. PMID: 19506121

entries.limitations: Very simple — intentionally uses only 3 variables (less granular than EuroSCORE II or STS). Does not capture urgency, procedure type, comorbidities, or frailty. Performance comparable to more complex models in some studies but may miss important risk factors. Designed for elective surgery.

entries.name: Society of Thoracic Surgeons Risk Score
entries.purpose: Predicts operative mortality and morbidity after cardiac surgery (CABG, valve, combined) using the STS national database.
entries.formula_human: Complex multivariable logistic regression model with 40+ variables. Predicted risk = 1/(1 + exp(−(β₀ + Σβᵢxᵢ))). Separate models for isolated CABG, isolated valve, CABG+valve, and other procedures. Coefficients updated periodically from the STS national database. Calculator available at riskcalc.sts.org/stswebriskcalc/

inputs.label: Demographics
inputs.description: Age, sex, race, height, weight, BMI

inputs.label: Risk factors and comorbidities
inputs.description: DM, hypertension, dyslipidemia, renal failure/dialysis, cerebrovascular disease, peripheral vascular disease, chronic lung disease, immunosuppression, endocarditis, etc.

inputs.label: Cardiac-specific variables
inputs.description: NYHA class, CCS class, LVEF, prior MI, arrhythmias, number of diseased vessels, left main disease, cardiogenic shock, IABP/vent support, etc.

bands.meaning: Low operative mortality risk
Moderate risk
High risk
Very high risk

citations.text: Shahian DM, O'Brien SM, Filardo G, et al. The Society of Thoracic Surgeons 2008 cardiac surgery risk models: part 1 — coronary artery bypass grafting surgery. Ann Thorac Surg. 2009;88(1 Suppl):S23-S62. PMID: 19559822

entries.limitations: US-specific (derived from US hospitals); may not perform well internationally. Extremely complex — requires dedicated calculator. Updated periodically (older versions may underestimate contemporary outcomes). Does not capture all frailty measures. Not designed for TAVR or off-pump CABG (separate models exist).
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app — calculator at riskcalc.sts.org

entries.name: SYNTAX Score II
entries.purpose: Integrates anatomic SYNTAX score with clinical variables to predict 4-year mortality after PCI or CABG, guiding individualized revascularization.
entries.formula_human: Nomogram-based: predicted 4-year mortality is derived from the combination of SYNTAX Score and 6 clinical variables via a Cox regression model. Coefficients published in Farooq V, et al. 2013. Use the online calculator at syntaxscore.com for precise predictions. PCI recommendation: if SYNTAX II 4-year mortality is lower with PCI than CABG → PCI; otherwise → CABG.

inputs.label: SYNTAX Score (anatomic)
inputs.description: Original anatomic SYNTAX score from coronary angiogram

bands.range: PCI predicted mortality < CABG predicted mortality
bands.meaning: Recommend PCI

bands.range: CABG predicted mortality ≤ PCI predicted mortality
bands.meaning: Recommend CABG

citations.text: Farooq V, van Klaveren D, Steyerberg EW, et al. Anatomical and clinical characteristics to guide decision making between coronary artery bypass surgery and percutaneous coronary intervention for individual patients: development and validation of SYNTAX score II. Lancet. 2013;381(9867):639-650. PMID:

entries.limitations: Requires both angiographic scoring and clinical data. Validated primarily in left main/3-vVD. Decision-making between PCI and CABG should incorporate Heart Team discussion, not rely solely on SYNTAX II. Inter-observer variability in SYNTAX score applies.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app — syntaxscore.com

entries.name: Framingham Risk Score (2008 General Cardiovascular Risk Profile)
entries.purpose: Estimates 10-year risk of a first cardiovascular event (coronary death, MI, stroke, heart failure, or peripheral vascular disease).
entries.formula_human: Point-based system: assign points for each risk factor per sex-specific lookup tables, then sum. Map total points to 10-year CVD risk from published tables. Cox model underlying: h(t) = h₀(t) × exp(β₁X₁ + β₂X₂ + ...). Exact coefficients published in D'Agostino RB, et al. 2008. Total points → 10-year risk % from published conversion table.

inputs.label: Age
inputs.points_text: sex-specific points assigned by age decade

inputs.label: Systolic BP
inputs.description: Systolic blood pressure (mmHg), stratified by treatment status

bands.meaning: Low risk (<10% 10-year CVD risk)
Intermediate risk (10–20%)
High risk (>20% 10-year CVD risk)

citations.text: D'Agostino RB Sr, Vasan RS, Pencina MJ, et al. General cardiovascular risk profile for use in primary care: the Framingham Heart Study. Circulation. 2008;117(6):743-753. PMID: 18212285

entries.limitations: Developed primarily in a White, middle-class New England cohort. May overestimate or underestimate risk in other populations. Does not include family history, social determinants, or biomarkers. Multiple versions exist (CHD-specific vs general CVD) — use the 2008 general profile. Not validated in patients <30 or >74 years.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: Pooled Cohort Equations for ASCVD Risk
entries.purpose: Estimates 10-year risk of a first atherosclerotic cardiovascular event (MI or stroke) in primary prevention patients aged 40–79.
entries.formula_human:
10-year ASCVD risk = 1 − S₀(10)^exp(individual_sum − mean_sum)

Where:
- individual_sum = β₁×ln(age) + β₂×ln(TC) + β₃×ln(HDL) + β₄×ln(SBP)×(on_treatment) + β₅×ln(SBP)×(not_treatment) + β₆×diabetes + β₇×smoker + β₈×ln(age)×ln(TC) + β₉×ln(age)×ln(HDL) + β₁₀×ln(age)×ln(SBP)×(on_treatment) + β₁₁×ln(age)×ln(SBP)×(not_treatment) + β₁₂×ln(age)×smoker
- Race- and sex-specific β coefficients and S₀(10) baselines are published in Goff et al. 2013, Supplementary Appendix.
- For White males: S₀(10) = 0.91436
- For White females: S₀(10) = 0.96652
- For Black males: S₀(10) = 0.89536
- For Black females: S₀(10) = 0.95334
- Coefficients: verify all exact β values from the published supplementary tables (too numerous to list fully here — 12 coefficients × 4 race-sex groups = 48 values).

inputs.label: Systolic BP
inputs.points_text: ln(SBP) × coefficient, with separate term for BP treatment status

bands.meaning: Low 10-year ASCVD risk
Borderline risk
Intermediate risk — statin therapy recommended per ACC/AHA guidelines
High risk — statin therapy and aggressive risk factor modification recommended

citations.text: Goff DC Jr, Lloyd-Jones DM, Bennett G, et al. 2013 ACC/AHA guideline on the assessment of cardiovascular risk. Circulation. 2014;129(25 Suppl 2):S49-S73. PMID: 24222018

entries.limitations: Tends to overestimate risk in some contemporary cohorts. Not validated for race/ethnicities other than White and African American (e.g., Hispanic, Asian). Not applicable to patients with established CVD (secondary prevention). Age limited to 40–79. Does not incorporate family history, CRP, CAC score, or social determinants of health. Performance varies by subgroup.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: PROCAM Risk Score (Prospective Cardiovascular Münster Study)
entries.purpose: Estimates 10-year risk of major coronary events (MI or cardiac death) using a German occupational cohort.
entries.formula_human: Logistic regression: Risk = 1/(1 + exp(−(β₀ + β₁×age + β₂×LDL + β₃×smoking + β₄×HDL + β₅×SBP + β₆×FH + β₇×DM + β₈×TG))). Exact coefficients published in Assmann G, et al. 2002. Point-based simplified version also published.

bands.meaning: Low risk
Intermediate risk
High risk — treat aggressively

citations.text: Assmann G, Cullen P, Schulte H. Simple scoring scheme for calculating the risk of acute coronary events based on the 10-year follow-up of the prospective cardiovascular Münster (PROCAM) study. Circulation. 2002;105(3):310-315. PMID: 11804985

entries.limitations: Originally derived from male workers only — later adapted for women. German occupational cohort may not generalize to all populations. Includes triglycerides (not in most other calculators). Family history definition varies by study.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: SCORE2 (Systematic COronary Risk Evaluation 2)
entries.purpose: Estimates 10-year risk of first fatal and non-fatal cardiovascular events (MI, stroke) in apparently healthy adults aged 40–69 in Europe.
entries.formula_human: 10-year risk = 1 − S₀(10)^exp(individual_linear_predictor). Coefficients are published in SCORE2 manuscript and risk chart lookup tables. Calibration factors applied based on WHO cardiovascular mortality risk region (low, moderate, high, very high). Use published risk charts or ESC CVD Risk Calculation app for precise values.

inputs.label: Age
inputs.points_text: calibration factor by age and region

bands.meaning: Low risk
Moderate risk
High risk — consider statin therapy
Very high risk

citations.text: SCORE2 working group and ESC Cardiovascular Risk Collaboration. SCORE2 risk prediction algorithms: new models to estimate 10-year risk of cardiovascular disease in Europe. Eur Heart J. 2021;42(25):2439-2454. PMID: 33871026

entries.limitations: Designed for European populations; not directly applicable to US, Asian, or other populations. Age limited to 40–69 (use SCORE2-OP for ≥70). Does not include diabetes (separate SCORE2-Diabetes model published separately). Non-HDL-C may not be routinely reported in all labs.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: H2FPEF Score
entries.purpose: Diagnoses heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) in patients with unexplained dyspnea and LVEF ≥50%.
entries.formula_human: H2FPEF = Heavy_BMI(0-4) + Hypertensive(2) + AF(3) + Pulmonary_HTN(1) + Age>60(1) + E/e'>9(1)

inputs.label: Heavy (BMI)
inputs.options_text: continuous; points assigned by BMI cutoffs

inputs.label: Pulmonary hypertension (PASP >35 mmHg)
inputs.description: Doppler estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure >35 mmHg on echo

inputs.label: E/e' ratio >9
inputs.description: Echocardiographic ratio of mitral inflow E velocity to tissue Doppler e' velocity

bands.meaning: Low probability of HFpEF (P(HFpEF) <25%). Consider alternative diagnoses.
Intermediate probability (25–75%). Further invasive hemodynamic testing (RHC) recommended.
High probability of HFpEF (>90%). Diagnosis likely confirmed.

citations.text: Reddy YNV, Carter RE, Obokata M, et al. A simple, evidence-based approach to help guide diagnosis of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Circulation. 2018;138(9):861-870. PMID: 29792299

entries.limitations: Requires echocardiographic parameters (E/e', PASP). Developed at a single center (Mayo Clinic) with highly selected patients. Intermediate scores (2–5) still require invasive testing. Not yet validated in acute HF or post-discharge settings.

entries.name: Heart Failure Association Pre-test Assessment, Echocardiography, Functional Testing, Final Etiology Score
entries.purpose: Stepwise diagnostic algorithm for HFpEF: combines clinical, echocardiographic, and functional testing criteria.
entries.formula_human: HFA-PEFF Step 1 (pre-test): assess symptoms, risk factors. Step 2 (echo + natriuretic peptides): sum of major (2 points each) and minor (1 point each) criteria across domains. Total ≥5 = definite HFpEF; 2–4 = indeterminate (proceed to Step 3 functional testing); ≤1 = low probability.

inputs.label: Functional (symptoms/risk factors)
inputs.description: Pre-test assessment of HF symptoms, risk factors (obesity, HTN, DM, AF, CAD, age >60)

inputs.label: Echocardiography (major)
inputs.description: Echo parameters including LAVI >34 mL/m², e' septal <7 or lateral <9, E/e' ≥9, SPAP >35 mmHg, LV wall thickness >12 mm or LVMI >115/95 g/m²

inputs.label: Natriuretic peptides
inputs.description: BNP >200 pg/mL or NT-proBNP >220 pg/mL (or age-adjusted NT-proBNP cutoffs)

inputs.label: Functional testing (diastolic stress test)
inputs.description: Exercise E/e' >15 or invasively confirmed elevated PCWP during exercise

bands.meaning: HFpEF diagnosed
Indeterminate; proceed to diastolic stress test or invasive hemodynamic exercise testing
HFpEF unlikely

citations.text: Pieske B, Tschöpe C, de Boer RA, et al. How to diagnose heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: the HFA-PEFF diagnostic algorithm. Eur Heart J. 2019;40(40):3297-3317. PMID: 31504452

entries.limitations: Complex multi-step algorithm. Echo criteria require expert interpretation. Functional testing (step 3) not widely available. No single simple numeric score — requires domain-based assessment.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: Heart Failure Survival Score
entries.purpose: Risk stratifies chronic HF patients for 1-year survival to identify candidates for cardiac transplantation.
entries.formula_human: HFSS = Ischemic_cause(0.6931) + HR(0.0216 × bpm) + LVEF(−0.0464 × %) + MAP(−0.0255 × mmHg) + Peak_VO2(−0.0546 × mL/kg/min) + Sodium(−0.0470 × mEq/L) + QRS(0.0074 × ms). Then: Risk score = exp(HFSS); 1-year survival = S₀^risk_score where S₀ is the baseline survival constant.

inputs.label: Peak VO₂
inputs.description: Peak oxygen consumption on cardiopulmonary exercise testing (mL/kg/min)

bands.meaning: Low risk: 1-year survival >90% (transplant can be deferred)
Medium risk: 1-year survival 70–90% (consider transplant listing)
High risk: 1-year survival <70% (urgent transplant evaluation)

citations.text: Aaronson KD, Schwartz JS, Chen TM, et al. Development and prospective validation of a clinical index to predict survival in ambulatory patients referred for cardiac transplant evaluation. Circulation. 1997;95(12):2660-2667. PMID: 9193435

entries.limitations: Requires cardiopulmonary exercise testing (peak VO₂) — not available in all settings. Derived from single-center transplant referral population. Not validated in HFpEF. BNP/NT-proBNP not included.

entries.name: Meta-Analysis Global Group in Chronic Heart Failure Score
entries.purpose: Predicts 1-year and 3-year mortality in patients with chronic heart failure using individual patient data from 39,372 patients.
entries.formula_human: Complex lookup table with non-linear point assignments for each variable; total points mapped to 1-year and 3-year mortality probabilities. No simple closed-form equation; use published nomogram or online calculator. The score sums the individual variable point assignments.

inputs.label: Age
inputs.points_text: non-linear point assignment increasing with age

inputs.label: NYHA class
inputs.points_text: I = fewest points; IV = most points

inputs.label: BMI
inputs.points_text: non-linear (higher BMI = fewer points — obesity paradox)

bands.meaning: 1-year mortality ~5–10%
1-year mortality ~15–30%
1-year mortality ~40–70%

citations.text: Pocock SJ, Ariti CA, McMurray JJV, et al. Predicting survival in heart failure: a risk score based on 39,372 patients from 30 studies. Eur Heart J. 2013;34(19):1404-1413. PMID: 23300255

entries.limitations: Complex (requires lookup table or calculator). Derived primarily from clinical trial populations (may not represent real-world HF patients). Some variables (e.g., time since HF diagnosis) may be difficult to ascertain. Originally validated in HFrEF; HFpEF validation less robust.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: New York Heart Association Functional Classification
entries.purpose: Functional classification of heart failure based on symptom severity and exercise tolerance.
entries.formula_human:
Categorical classification:
I = No limitation; ordinary physical activity does not cause symptoms
II = Slight limitation; comfortable at rest; ordinary activity causes symptoms
III = Marked limitation; comfortable at rest; less-than-ordinary activity causes symptoms
IV = Unable to carry out any physical activity without symptoms; symptoms at rest

inputs.label: Functional capacity
inputs.description: Patient's subjective and objective exercise tolerance and symptoms

bands.meaning: No limitation of physical activity
Slight limitation; comfortable at rest
Marked limitation; comfortable at rest
Symptoms at rest; any physical activity causes discomfort

citations.text: Nomenclature and Criteria for Diagnosis of Diseases of the Heart and Great Vessels. New York Heart Association, 9th ed. Little, Brown & Co; 1994. (No single PMID — book publication)

entries.limitations: Subjective; significant inter-observer variability. Does not correlate perfectly with objective measures (e.g., peak VO₂, BNP). Patient classification can fluctuate day-to-day.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: Seattle Heart Failure Model
entries.purpose: Quantitative model predicting 1-, 2-, and 3-year survival in heart failure patients, incorporating medications, devices, and laboratory values.
entries.formula_human: Linear predictor (LP) = Σ(coefficients × variable values). Then: 1-year survival = S₀(1)^exp(LP − mean_LP). S₀(1) = baseline 1-year survival at mean LP. Exact S₀ values and all coefficients are published in the original paper and calculator. Verify precise coefficients and baseline survival functions from Levy WC, et al. 2006.

inputs.label: NYHA class
inputs.description: NYHA class III vs IV (reference I/II)

inputs.label: Lymphocyte percentage
inputs.description: Percentage of lymphocytes on WBC differential

bands.meaning: Low annual mortality risk
Moderate risk
High risk; consider advanced therapies (LVAD, transplant evaluation)

citations.text: Levy WC, Mozaffarian D, Linker DT, et al. The Seattle Heart Failure Model: prediction of survival in heart failure. Circulation. 2006;113(11):1424-1433. PMID: 16534094

entries.limitations: Requires multiple lab values and medication data. Original derivation from clinical trial populations. Less validated in HFpEF. Does not capture right ventricular function, iron status, or advanced biomarkers (galectin-3, ST2). Online calculator required for precise predictions.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app — online calculator available at seattleheartfailure.org

entries.name: Nutrition Risk in the Critically Ill Score
entries.purpose: Identifies ICU patients most likely to benefit from aggressive nutrition therapy; stratifies nutrition-related risk.
entries.formula_human: NUTRIC (modified, without IL-6) = APACHE_II(0-6) + SOFA(0-3) + Comorbidities(0-1) + Days_to_ICU(0-2) + Age(0-2). Full NUTRIC adds IL-6(0-1).

inputs.label: Days from hospital admission to ICU

bands.meaning: Low nutrition risk. Nutrition therapy less likely to change outcomes.
High nutrition risk. Aggressive nutrition therapy is most likely beneficial.

citations.text: Heyland DK, Dhaliwal R, Jiang X, Day AG. Identifying critically ill patients who benefit the most from nutrition therapy: the development and initial validation of a novel risk assessment tool. Crit Care. 2011;15(6):R268. PMID: 22078164

entries.limitations: Requires APACHE II and SOFA scores (complex). IL-6 not widely available (hence modified version preferred). Not a calorie/fat calculator — it's a risk stratification tool. Validated primarily in mixed medical-surgical ICU populations.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist
entries.purpose: Validated screening tool for delirium in ICU patients using eight items assessed over an 8-hour nursing shift.
entries.formula_human: ICDSC = Sum of all 8 items (0 or 1 each)

inputs.label: Altered level of consciousness
inputs.description: A (alert), V (voice), P (pain), U (unresponsive), C (combative), S (sedated). A = 0; other = consider scoring

bands.meaning: Delirium not detected (below threshold)
Delirium present (ICDSC ≥4 has sensitivity ~99%, specificity ~64%)

citations.text: Bergeron N, Dubois MJ, Dumont M, et al. Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist: evaluation of a new screening tool. Intensive Care Med. 2001;27(5):859-864. PMID: 11430542

entries.limitations: Lower specificity than CAM-ICU (more false positives). Requires nursing observation over a shift. Does not distinguish delirium subtypes (hyperactive vs hypoactive). Some items are subjective.

entries.name: Mortality Probability Model at ICU Admission (MPM₀)
entries.purpose: Predicts hospital mortality at ICU admission using data collected at the time of ICU admission (not 24 hours).
entries.formula_human: MPM₀: Logit = −5.5291 + 0.8998(logit_coma/stupor) + 0.6098(logit_emergency) + 0.5775(logit_cancer) + 1.4024(logit_CPR_24h) + 0.9639(logit_chronic_renal) + 1.0905(logit_ICU_after_surgery) + 0.5172(logit_medical) + 0.1158(logit_heart_rate) + 0.0458(logit_systolic_BP) − 0.0299(logit_temperature) + 0.9637(logit_respiratory_support) + 0.6929(logit_cerebrovascular_disease). Predicted mortality = 1/(1 + e^(-logit)).

bands.meaning: Low predicted mortality
Moderate predicted mortality
High predicted mortality
Very high predicted mortality

citations.text: Lemeshow S, Teres D, Klar J, et al. Mortality Probability Models (MPM II) based on an international cohort of intensive care unit patients. JAMA. 1993;270(20):2478-2486. PMID: 8230626

entries.limitations: Calibrated to 1990s data. MPM₀-III updated but less widely used. Requires assessment at ICU admission time — cannot be used at 24h. Some variables are binary (less granular than APACHE/SAPS).
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program Surgical Risk Calculator
entries.purpose: Predicts 8 postoperative outcomes (including serious complications, cardiac complications, pneumonia, death) for specific CPT-coded surgical procedures.
entries.formula_human: Multivariable logistic regression: predicted risk = 1/(1 + exp(−(β₀ + Σβᵢxᵢ))). Separate models for each of 8 outcomes. Over 1.4 million cases from 680+ hospitals used to derive coefficients. Use calculator at riskcalculator.facs.org/

inputs.label: CPT code
inputs.description: Current Procedural Terminology code for the specific surgery
inputs.options_text: Specific CPT codes from the NSQIP database

inputs.label: Additional comorbidities
inputs.description: 12 additional variables: ascites, ventilator dependence, disseminated cancer, diabetes, hypertension, COPD, CHF, dyspnea, smoke, dialysis, acute renal failure, BMI, etc.

bands.meaning: Provides individualized risk estimates for: serious complication, any complication, pneumonia, cardiac complication, surgical site infection, UTI, VTE, renal failure, readmission, death

citations.text: Bilimoria KY, Liu Y, Paruch JL, et al. Development and evaluation of the universal ACS NSQIP surgical risk calculator: a decision aid and informed consent source for patients and surgeons. J Am Coll Surg. 2013;217(5):833-842. PMID: 24055393
