entries.limitations: Requires CPT code (procedure-specific). May overestimate or underestimate risk for rare procedures. Does not capture all surgeon-specific or hospital-specific factors. Updated periodically. Used for informed consent and shared decision-making, not as a sole decision tool.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app — riskcalculator.facs.org

entries.name: Mehran Risk Score for Contrast-Induced Nephropathy
entries.purpose: Predicts risk of contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) after percutaneous coronary intervention.
entries.formula_human: Mehran = Hypotension(5) + IABP(5) + CHF(5) + Age>75(4) + Anemia(3) + DM(3) + Contrast_volume(1 per 100mL) + Cr>1.5(4)

inputs.label: Hypotension
inputs.description: SBP <80 mmHg requiring inotropes or IABP for ≥1 hour (within 24h post-procedure)

inputs.label: CHF (Class III/IV or history of pulmonary edema)

bands.meaning: Low risk (~7.5% CIN risk)
Moderate risk (~14%)
High risk (~26%)
Very high risk (~57% CIN risk; ~13% dialysis needed)

citations.text: Mehran R, Aymong ED, Nikolsky E, et al. A simple risk score for prediction of contrast-induced nephropathy after percutaneous coronary intervention: development and initial validation. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2004;44(7):1393-1399. PMID: 15464318

entries.limitations: Derived from PCI population — less validated for contrast CT. Contrast volume estimation may be imprecise pre-procedure. Does not capture hydration strategy or type of contrast (iso-osmolar vs low-osmolar). Pre-dates routine use of pre-hydration protocols.

entries.name: Parsonnet Score
entries.purpose: Preoperative risk stratification for mortality in cardiac surgery, originally developed for valvular surgery.
entries.formula_human: Sum of individual risk factor points. Detailed point assignments published in Parsonnet V, et al. 1989. Not a simple additive formula — some items are interactions. Total score mapped to predicted mortality via published tables.

inputs.label: Age
inputs.description: Points assigned by age decades (highest for >70)

inputs.label: Preoperative use of inotropes
inputs.description: IV inotropes at time of surgery

inputs.label: Valvular disease specifics
inputs.description: Mitral valve vs aortic valve pathology

bands.meaning: Low operative risk (<2% mortality)
Moderate risk (2–5%)
High risk (>5% mortality)

citations.text: Parsonnet V, Dean D, Bernstein AD. A method of uniform stratification of risk for evaluating the results of surgery in acquired adult heart disease. Circulation. 1989;79(6 Pt 2):I3-I12. PMID: 2720932

entries.limitations: Historical — largely superseded by EuroSCORE II and STS Score. Derivation from single center in 1980s (outdated operative mortality). Does not capture modern techniques. Some variables are subjective. Complex point assignments not all intuitive.

entries.name: Emergency Department Assessment of Chest Pain Score
entries.purpose: Identifies low-risk ED chest pain patients who can be safely discharged after a single troponin or short observation protocol.
entries.formula_human: EDACS = Age(0–8) + Sex(0–2) + CAD_risk_factors(2) + Diaphoresis(3) + Exertional(2) + Radiation(2) + Pleuritic(−4) + Reproducible(−6)

inputs.label: Known CAD or ≥3 risk factors
inputs.description: History of CAD or ≥3 cardiovascular risk factors

bands.range: EDACS <16 AND non-ischemic ECG AND negative troponin (0 and/or 2h)
bands.meaning: Low risk. Safe for discharge with outpatient follow-up. <1% 30-day MACE.

bands.range: EDACS ≥16 OR ischemic ECG OR positive troponin
bands.meaning: Not low risk. Requires further workup.

citations.text: Than M, Flaws D, Sanders S, et al. Development and validation of the Emergency Department Assessment of Chest pain Score and 2 h accelerated diagnostic protocol. Emerg Med Australas. 2014;26(1):34-44. PMID: 24460788

entries.limitations: Negative points for pleuritic and reproducible pain may seem counterintuitive. Requires knowledge of the full scoring system. Not yet adopted into major guidelines. Performance may vary by troponin assay.

entries.name: Vancouver Chest Pain Rule
entries.purpose: Identifies low-risk chest pain patients suitable for early discharge from the ED without troponin testing at 2 hours.
entries.formula_human: Decision tree algorithm (not additive score): If age <40, no prior CAD, non-ischemic ECG, normal hs-troponin at 0 and 2h, and pain is pleuritic/positional/palpable → ACS excluded. Additional branches for age 40–60 and >60 with different criteria. See original publication for complete algorithm.

bands.meaning: Patient safe for discharge. <1% 30-day MACE.
Requires further observation/investigation.

citations.text: Scheuermeyer FX, Innes G, Grafstein E, et al. Safety and efficiency of a chest pain diagnostic algorithm with selective outpatient stress testing for emergency department patients with potential ischemic chest pain. Ann Emerg Med. 2012;59(4):256-264. PMID: 22265560

entries.limitations: Single-center derivation. Requires hs-troponin assay. Complex decision tree not easily memorized. Not widely adopted outside Canada. Limited external validation.

entries.name: ADD-RS (Aortic Dissection Detection Risk Score)
entries.purpose: Screening tool to identify patients at risk for acute aortic dissection in the emergency department, triggering definitive imaging.
entries.formula_human: ADD-RS = Aortic_pain(0/1) + High_risk_conditions(0/1) + High_risk_exam(0/1). Range 0–3.

inputs.label: High-risk features: Aortic pain, high-risk conditions, high-risk exam
Aortic pain
inputs.description: Chest/abdominal/back pain that is abrupt, severe, ripping/tearing

inputs.label: High-risk conditions
inputs.description: Marfan syndrome, known aortic valve disease, known aortic aneurysm, prior aortic surgery, family history of aortic disease

inputs.label: High-risk examination features
inputs.description: Pulse deficit, new aortic regurgitation murmur, focal neurological deficit, hypotension/shock/tamponade

bands.meaning: Low risk for aortic dissection (0.5%). Further testing only if clinical suspicion persists.
Intermediate risk (~5%). Consider D-dimer or CTA.
High risk (~30–50%). Proceed directly to definitive imaging (CTA, TEE, or MRA). D-dimer may be used to rule out in ADD-RS <1.

citations.text: Rogers AM, Hermann LK, Booher AM, et al. Sensitivity of the Aortic Dissection Detection Risk Score, a novel guideline-based tool for identification of acute aortic dissection at initial presentation: results from the International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection. Circulation. 2011;123(20):2213-2

entries.limitations: Sensitivity is high (~95%) but specificity is low — many false positives. Best used as a screening tool to prompt further investigation, not to rule in diagnosis. Some components (e.g., Marfan syndrome) are uncommon. Requires clinical assessment of all three categories.

entries.name: Respiratory Distress Assessment Instrument
entries.purpose: Assesses severity of respiratory distress in infants with bronchiolitis by evaluating wheezing and retractions.
entries.formula_human: RDAI = Wheezing_score(0–4) + Retraction_score(0–17). Different versions exist with variable numbers of retraction sites assessed.

inputs.label: Wheezing
inputs.description: Wheezing score based on location and severity
inputs.options_text: 0 = no wheezing; 1 = end-expiratory; 2 = expiratory only; 3 = inspiratory and expiratory; 4 = audible without stethoscope

inputs.label: Retractions
inputs.description: Chest retractions (7 locations assessed: suprasternal, supraclavicular, intercostals, subcostal, supraclavicular, lateral chest wall, scalene)
inputs.options_text: Each site: 0 = none; 1 = just detectable; 2 = mild; 3 = moderate; 4 = severe. Max total retractions = 0–17 (or various versions)

bands.meaning: Mild respiratory distress
Moderate distress
Severe distress; consider hospitalization and escalation of care

citations.text: Lowell DI, Lister G, Von Koss H, McCarthy P. Wheezing in infants: the response to epinephrine. Pediatrics. 1987;79(6):939-945. PMID: 3588151

entries.limitations: Inter-rater variability for wheezing and retractions. Different versions exist (12-point vs 17-point retraction scales). Wheezing may be absent in severe bronchiolitis (silent chest). Not designed for treatment decisions but often used as outcome measure. Does not capture oxygen requirement.

entries.name: Westley Croup Score
entries.purpose: Quantifies severity of croup (laryngotracheobronchitis) in children to guide treatment decisions (e.g., racemic epinephrine, steroids).
entries.formula_human: Westley = Stridor(0–3) + Retractions(0–3) + Air_entry(0–2) + Cyanosis(0/3/4) + LOC(0/5)

inputs.label: Stridor at rest
inputs.options_text: 0 = none; 1 = when agitated; 2 = intermittent at rest; 3 = continuous at rest

inputs.label: Retractions
inputs.options_text: 0 = none; 1 = mild; 2 = moderate; 3 = severe (with nasal flaring)

bands.meaning: Mild croup
Moderate croup
Severe croup. Racemic epinephrine and corticosteroids indicated.
Impending respiratory failure. Consider ICU admission and intubation.

citations.text: Westley CR, Cotton EK, Brooks JG. Nebulized racemic epinephrine by IPPB for the treatment of croup: a double-blind study. Am J Dis Child. 1978;132(5):484-487. PMID: 347921

entries.limitations: Inter-rater variability for air entry and retractions. Cutoffs for mild/moderate/severe vary slightly by source. Score may fluctuate rapidly with agitation. Not validated as a discharge criterion. Designed for research — clinical management often driven by overall impression.

entries.name: Canadian C-Spine Rule
entries.purpose: Identifies alert, stable trauma patients who do not require cervical spine imaging.
entries.formula_human:
Step 1: Any high-risk factor? → Yes = image.
Step 2: Any low-risk factor allowing safe assessment? → No = image.
Step 3: Can actively rotate neck 45° both directions? → Yes = no imaging; No = imaging.

inputs.label: High-risk factors
inputs.description: Age ≥65, dangerous mechanism (fall >3 ft or 5 stairs, axial load injury, high-speed MVC, bicycle collision, diving), paresthesias in extremities

inputs.label: Low-risk factors
inputs.description: Simple rear-end MVC, ambulatory at any time, delayed onset of neck pain, no midline C-spine tenderness, sitting position in ED, able to rotate neck 45°
inputs.options_text: Must have low-risk factor AND no high-risk factor to assess ROM
inputs.points_text: safety net for safe ROM testing

bands.meaning: No high-risk factor AND low-risk factor present AND able to rotate neck 45°. <1% risk of clinically significant C-spine injury.
Any high-risk factor, no low-risk factors for safe assessment, or inability to rotate neck.

citations.text: Stiell IG, Wells GA, Vandemheen KL, et al. The Canadian C-spine rule for radiography in alert and stable trauma patients. JAMA. 2001;286(15):1841-1848. PMID: 11597285

entries.limitations: Not applicable to patients <16 years, GCS <15, acute paralysis, or known vertebral disease. Requires active ROM assessment (some patients cannot cooperate). More complex than NEXUS (5 criteria). Inter-observer reliability better than NEXUS but requires training. Dangerous mechanism definition may be subjective.

entries.name: National Emergency X-Radiography Utilization Study Criteria
entries.purpose: Identifies blunt trauma patients who do not require cervical spine imaging, using five low-risk clinical criteria.
entries.formula_human: All 5 criteria must be negative for C-spine imaging to be safely omitted. Any single positive criterion = imaging required.

bands.meaning: C-spine imaging not required. ~99% sensitivity for clinically significant C-spine injury.
C-spine imaging indicated.

citations.text: Hoffman JR, Mower WR, Wolfson AB, et al. Validity of a set of clinical criteria to rule out injury to the cervical spine in patients with blunt trauma. N Engl J Med. 2000;343(2):94-99. PMID: 10891516

entries.limitations: Lower specificity than Canadian C-Spine Rule (more imaging). 'Distracting injury' is subjective and broad. 'Altered mental status' can be hard to define. Intoxication assessment can be imprecise. Largely replaced by the Canadian C-Spine Rule in non-US settings.

entries.name: Ottawa Ankle Rules
entries.purpose: Identifies patients with ankle injuries who require radiography, reducing unnecessary imaging by ~30%.
entries.formula_human: Decision rule: Ankle X-ray required if bone tenderness at either malleolus OR inability to weight bear for 4 steps both immediately and in ED.

inputs.label: Bone tenderness at posterior edge or tip of lateral malleolus
Bone tenderness at posterior edge or tip of medial malleolus
Inability to weight bear (4 steps) both immediately and in ED

bands.meaning: No X-ray needed. ~99% sensitivity for clinically significant fractures.
Ankle X-ray required.

citations.text: Stiell IG, Greenberg GH, McKnight RD, et al. Decision rules for the use of radiography in acute ankle injuries. Refinement and prospective validation. JAMA. 1993;269(9):1127-1132. PMID: 8433468

entries.limitations: Not applicable to children <5 years, pregnant women, or patients with isolated skin injuries. Does not apply to hindfoot or midfoot injuries. Requires patient to attempt weight bearing (pain limits compliance). Not validated for pathologic or stress fractures.

entries.name: Ottawa Knee Rules
entries.purpose: Identifies patients with knee injuries requiring radiography to detect clinically significant fractures.
entries.formula_human: Decision rule: Knee X-ray required if age ≥55 OR tenderness at fibular head OR isolated tibial tenderness OR inability to flex 90° OR inability to weight bear for 4 steps.

inputs.label: Inability to weight bear (4 steps) both immediately and in ED

bands.meaning: No X-ray needed. ~99% sensitivity for fractures.
Knee X-ray required.

citations.text: Stiell IG, Greenberg GH, Wells GA, et al. Derivation of a decision rule for the use of radiography in acute knee injuries. J Emerg Med. 1995;13(5):621-628. PMID: 8530782

entries.limitations: Not applicable to isolated patellar injuries, children <18, or patients with altered consciousness. Does not apply to open fractures or gross deformity. Tenderness criteria are subjective. Weight-bearing requirement limits use in very painful injuries.

entries.name: Canadian CT Head Rule
entries.purpose: Identifies patients with minor head injury (GCS 13–15) who require CT head imaging based on high-risk and medium-risk criteria.
entries.formula_human:
CT head required if ANY high-risk criterion present:
1. GCS <15 at 2 hours post-injury
2. Suspected open/depressed skull fracture
3. Basal skull fracture signs (hemotympanum, raccoon eyes, CSF leak, Battle sign)
4. ≥2 episodes of vomiting
5. Age ≥65

CT may be considered if medium-risk criterion present (for clinically important brain injury but not necessarily neurosurgical).

Sensitivity for need for neurosurgical intervention: ~100%; for brain injury on CT: ~95%.

inputs.label: Medium-risk factors (for brain injury on CT)

bands.meaning: CT not needed (if medium-risk criteria also absent). ~100% sensitive for neurosurgically important injury.
CT head required.

citations.text: Stiell IG, Wells GA, Vandemheen K, et al. The Canadian CT Head Rule for patients with minor head injury. Lancet. 2001;357(9266):1391-1396. PMID: 11356436

entries.limitations: Not applicable to patients <16 years, GCS <13, anticoagulant use, or previous neurosurgery. Requires 2-hour observation period for GCS assessment. Does not apply to penetrating injuries. Vomiting may be related to alcohol intoxication rather than injury.

entries.name: New Orleans Criteria
entries.purpose: Alternative clinical decision rule for CT imaging in minor head injury patients with GCS 15.
entries.formula_human: CT head indicated if any of 7 criteria present. All 7 must be absent to safely forgo CT.

bands.meaning: CT not needed. ~100% sensitivity for brain injury.
CT indicated.

citations.text: Haydel MJ, Preston CA, Mills TJ, et al. Indications for computed tomography in patients with minor head injury. N Engl J Med. 2000;343(2):100-105. PMID: 10891517

entries.limitations: Less specific than CCHR — higher CT rate (more false positives). Only includes GCS 15 patients. 'Visible trauma above clavicles' is very sensitive but non-specific (almost all trauma patients). Not widely adopted outside the US.

entries.name: Bacterial Meningitis Score
entries.purpose: Identifies children at very low risk for bacterial meningitis who may not require lumbar puncture or empirical antibiotics.
entries.formula_human: BMS = CSF_protein≥100(1) + CSF_ANC≥1000(1) + Peripheral_ANC≥10000(1) + Gram_stain_positive(1) + Seizure(1). Low risk if score = 0.

bands.meaning: Very low risk of bacterial meningitis (<0.1%). Consider observation without antibiotics if viral etiology likely.
Higher risk. Treat as bacterial meningitis until excluded.

citations.text: Nigrovic LE, Kuppermann N, Macias CG, et al. Clinical prediction rule for identifying children with cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis at very low risk of bacterial meningitis. JAMA. 2007;297(1):52-60. PMID: 17200475

entries.limitations: Requires CSF (LP must be done to use the score). Not applicable if LP not performed. Less validated in neonates (<29 days) and immunocompromised. Gram stain sensitivity varies by lab. Pre-LP antibiotics reduce sensitivity of Gram stain and culture.

entries.name: LRINEC (Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis)
entries.purpose: Identifies patients with soft tissue infection at risk for necrotizing fasciitis using routine laboratory tests.
entries.formula_human: LRINEC = CRP(0/4) + WBC(0-2) + Hemoglobin(0-2) + Sodium(0/2) + Creatinine(0/2) + Glucose(0/1)

bands.meaning: Low risk of necrotizing fasciitis (<50% PPV).
Intermediate risk (~50–75% risk).
High risk (~>75% risk of necrotizing fasciitis). Urgent surgical consultation recommended.

citations.text: Wong CH, Khin LW, Heng KS, et al. The LRINEC (Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis) score: a tool for distinguishing necrotizing fasciitis from other soft tissue infections. Crit Care Med. 2004;32(7):1535-1541. PMID: 15241098

entries.limitations: Low sensitivity (~60-80%) — a low LRINEC score should NOT exclude necrotizing fasciitis if clinical suspicion is high. CRP may not be elevated early in disease. Not validated in all populations. Should supplement, not replace, clinical judgment and surgical evaluation.

entries.name: Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network Head CT Decision Rule
entries.purpose: Identifies children at very low risk of clinically important traumatic brain injury (ciTBI) who do not require CT head imaging.
entries.formula_human:
Decision algorithm:
HIGH-RISK (any → CT recommended): GCS <15, palpable skull fracture, signs of basilar skull fracture, altered behavior/mental status

HIGHER-RISK (observation vs CT based on clinical judgment): scalp hematoma, vomiting ≥2, severe headache, dangerous mechanism

If NO high-risk or higher-risk features → observation safe (no CT needed).
Sensitivity for ciTBI: 98–100%.

inputs.label: Age group
inputs.description: Two separate rules: <2 years vs ≥2 years

inputs.label: (<2): Occipital/parietal/temporal scalp hematoma or large hematoma

bands.meaning: <0.1% risk of ciTBI. Observation and no CT.
0.5–4% risk. Clinical judgment for CT vs observation.
CT head recommended. Higher risk of ciTBI and neurosurgical intervention.

citations.text: Kuppermann N, Holmes JF, Dayan PS, et al. Identification of children at very low risk of clinically-important brain injuries after head trauma: a prospective cohort study. Lancet. 2009;374(9696):1160-1170. PMID: 19758692

entries.limitations: Validated in children with GCS 14–15 (minor head trauma only). Parents may under/over-report symptoms. Clinical judgment still required for higher-risk group. External validation in non-US settings limited. CT avoidance must be balanced against missed ciTBI risk.

entries.name: Pediatric Glasgow Coma Scale
entries.purpose: Age-adapted Glasgow Coma Scale for children under 4 years, with modified verbal component using age-appropriate responses.
entries.formula_human: PGCS = Eye(1–4) + Verbal(1–5) + Motor(1–6). Verbal scale differs for children <4 years.

inputs.label: Verbal response (modified for age)
inputs.options_text: 5 = Coos/babbles (age-appropriate); 4 = Irritable/cries; 3 = Cries to pain; 2 = Moans to pain; 1 = None

bands.meaning: Mild (13–15), Moderate (9–12), Severe (3–8) traumatic brain injury

citations.text: James HE. Neurologic evaluation and support in the child with an acute brain insult. Pediatr Ann. 1986;15:16-22. PMID: 3945549; Teasdale G, Jennett B. Lancet. 1974;2:81-84 (original GCS concept)

entries.limitations: Verbal scale modification for children <4 is based on developmental norms that vary. Inter-rater variability is greater in pediatrics. Less validated than adult GCS. Behaviorally challenged children may be difficult to assess.

entries.name: Revised Geneva Score
entries.purpose: Standardized, fully objective clinical prediction rule for estimating pretest probability of PE (no clinical gestalt component).
entries.formula_human: Revised Geneva = Age>65(1) + Prior_VTE(3) + Surgery_fracture(2) + Active_cancer(2) + Unilateral_leg_pain(3) + Hemoptysis(2) + HR_75-94(3) + HR_≥95(5) + Clinical_DVT_signs(4)

inputs.label: Surgery or fracture within 1 month
inputs.description: Recent surgery or lower extremity fracture

inputs.label: Unilateral lower-limb pain
inputs.description: Pain on palpation of deep veins or unilateral leg pain

inputs.label: Pain on lower limb deep vein palpation and unilateral edema

bands.meaning: Low probability (~8% PE prevalence). D-dimer can rule out if negative.
Intermediate probability (~23%). D-dimer or imaging.
High probability (~74%). Proceed to imaging.

citations.text: Le Gal G, Righini M, Roy PM, et al. Prediction of pulmonary embolism in the emergency department: the revised Geneva score. Ann Intern Med. 2006;144(3):165-171. PMID: 16461960

entries.limitations: Fully objective (advantage over Wells) but slightly lower discrimination than Wells with gestalt. Complex point system (non-integer values). Derived in European academic centers. D-dimer threshold may vary by age (age-adjusted D-dimer now recommended).

entries.name: Predisposition, Infection, Response, Organ Dysfunction Score
entries.purpose: Staging system for sepsis that classifies patients based on predisposition, infection, response, and organ dysfunction for better risk stratification.
entries.formula_human: PIRO = Predisposition(0–6) + Infection(0–6) + Response(0–8) + Organ_dysfunction(0–12). Exact item scoring varies by PIRO version. See Rubulotta FM, et al. 2009 for full scoring table.

inputs.label: Predisposition
inputs.description: Baseline comorbidities and factors affecting susceptibility (comorbidity score, age, prior infection, etc.)

inputs.label: Infection
inputs.description: Site and type of infection (respiratory, urinary, abdominal, skin, blood culture positivity, etc.)

inputs.label: Response
inputs.description: Systemic response (SIRS criteria, sepsis criteria, shock, metabolic acidosis)

inputs.label: Organ dysfunction
inputs.description: Number and type of organ failures (SOFA-based)

bands.meaning: Higher predicted mortality from sepsis. Mortality increases stepwise with score.

citations.text: Rubulotta FM, Marshall JC, Ramsay G, et al. Predisposition, insult/infection, response, and organ dysfunction: A new model for staging severe sepsis. Crit Care Med. 2009;37(4):1329-1335. PMID: 19242331

entries.limitations: Complex scoring system. Multiple versions exist. Not widely adopted in clinical practice. Less intuitive than SOFA for tracking organ failure. Validated mainly in ICU populations.

entries.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign Hour-1 Bundle Compliance
entries.purpose: Evidence-based treatment bundle for sepsis and septic shock; not a scoring system per se but a compliance metric used for quality improvement.
entries.formula_human: Percentage of bundle elements completed within 1 hour of sepsis recognition. Compliance = (# elements completed / 5) × 100%

inputs.label: Fluid resuscitation (30 mL/kg crystalloid for hypotension/lactate ≥4)
Vasopressors if hypotension during/after fluid resuscitation

bands.meaning: All 5 elements completed within 1 hour — associated with reduced mortality

citations.text: Levy MM, Evans LE, Rhodes A. The Surviving Sepsis Campaign Bundle: 2018 update. Crit Care Med. 2018;46(6):997-1000. PMID: 29794444

entries.limitations: Not a scoring system — treatment bundle. Compliance measurement relies on accurate time documentation. 1-hour target is debated (some evidence suggests longer windows are acceptable). Bundled approach may lead to unnecessary fluid administration in some patients.

entries.name: Hemorrhage After Thrombolysis Score
entries.purpose: Predicts risk of symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage after IV thrombolysis (tPA) for acute ischemic stroke.
entries.formula_human: HAT = Glucose>200(1) + NIHSS(0–4) + CT_hypodensity(0–2)

inputs.label: Hypodensity on CT
inputs.description: Early ischemic changes (hypoattenuation) on pre-tPA CT scan

bands.meaning: Low risk of sICH (~3%)
Moderate risk (~5–10%)
High risk (~12–25% sICH risk)

citations.text: Lou M, Safdar A, Mehdiratta M, et al. The HAT Score: a simple grading scale for predicting hemorrhagic risk after intravenous tissue plasminogen activator. J Stroke Cerebrovasc Dis. 2008;17(4):201-206. PMID: 18589344

entries.limitations: Simpler than some competing scores (SITS, SEDAN). Does not capture all risk factors (e.g., age, anticoagulation, leukoaraiosis). Single-center derivation. Should not be used to withhold tPA — risk is generally acceptable relative to benefit of treatment.

entries.name: Canadian Syncope Risk Score
entries.purpose: Predicts 30-day serious outcomes in ED patients presenting with syncope, enabling safe discharge of low-risk patients.
entries.formula_human: CSRS = Vasovagal_predisposition(−1) + Heart_disease(1) + BP_abnormal(2) + Troponin_positive(2) + ECG_abnormal(2) + Vasovagal_diagnosis(−2) + Supine/exertion_syncope(2) + SOB(1) + Q_wave/T_wave_inversion(1)

inputs.label: Predisposition to vasovagal symptoms
inputs.description: Prolonged standing, warm environment, pain, emotional stress, etc.

inputs.label: ECG abnormal
inputs.description: New ST changes, T-wave inversions, BBB, Q waves, arrhythmia, sinus bradycardia <40, paced rhythm, or 1st degree HB with PR >200ms

inputs.label: Syncope while supine or during exertion
inputs.description: Syncope at rest or during exercise

inputs.label: Q wave or T wave inversion on ECG

bands.meaning: Very low risk. Safe for immediate discharge.
Low risk.
Medium risk. Short-term observation recommended.
High risk. Urgent investigation and admission.

citations.text: Thiruganasambandamoorthy V, Kwong K, Wells GA, et al. Development of the Canadian Syncope Risk Score to predict serious adverse events after emergency department assessment of syncope. CMAJ. 2016;188(12):E289-E298. PMID: 27241783

entries.limitations: Requires troponin and ECG (more data than simpler scores). Complex point system with negative values. External validation outside Canada is limited. ECG abnormality definitions are broad. Physician gestalt incorporated in some components (vasovagal diagnosis).

entries.name: FOUR Score (Full Outline of UnResponsiveness)
entries.purpose: Alternative to GCS for assessing level of consciousness in intubated patients; captures brainstem reflexes and respiratory patterns.
entries.formula_human: FOUR = Eye(0–4) + Motor(0–4) + Brainstem(0–4) + Respiration(0–4)

inputs.label: Eye response
inputs.options_text: 4 = eyelids open, tracks or blinks to command; 3 = eyelids open but no tracking; 2 = eyelids closed but open to pain; 1 = eyelids closed to pain; 0 = eyelids remain closed with pain

inputs.label: Motor response
inputs.options_text: 4 = thumbs-up/fist/peace sign; 3 = localizes to pain; 2 = flexion response to pain; 1 = extension to pain; 0 = no response to pain or generalized myoclonus

inputs.label: Brainstem reflexes
inputs.options_text: 4 = pupil and corneal reflexes present; 3 = one pupil wide and fixed; 2 = pupil OR corneal absent; 1 = pupil AND corneal absent; 0 = absent pupil, corneal, and cough reflex

inputs.label: Respiration
inputs.options_text: 4 = not intubated, regular breathing; 3 = not intubated, Cheyne-Stokes; 2 = not intubated, irregular breathing; 1 = breathes above ventilator rate; 0 = breathes at ventilator rate or apnea

bands.meaning: Fully alert
Mild-moderate impairment
Moderate-severe impairment
Deep coma; locked-in syndrome can score 0–1

citations.text: Wijdicks EFM, Bamlet WR, Maramattom BV, et al. Validation of a new coma scale: The FOUR Score. Ann Neurol. 2005;58(4):585-593. PMID: 16178024

entries.limitations: Less widely used and studied than GCS. Brainstem reflex testing may be difficult in some clinical settings. Respiratory scoring complicated by sedation and ventilator settings. Training required for consistent use.

entries.name: Asthma Control Test
entries.purpose: Patient-completed questionnaire assessing asthma control over the previous 4 weeks to guide treatment adjustments.
entries.formula_human: ACT = Sum of all 5 items (each 1–5)

inputs.label: Asthma symptom interference with daily activities
inputs.description: How much did asthma interfere with daily activities? (1–5)
inputs.options_text: 1 = all of the time; 5 = not at all

inputs.label: Shortness of breath frequency
inputs.description: How often had shortness of breath? (1–5)
inputs.options_text: 1 = more than once a day; 5 = not at all

inputs.label: Nighttime symptoms
inputs.description: How often did asthma symptoms wake you at night or earlier than usual? (1–5)

inputs.label: Overall asthma control rating
inputs.description: How would you rate asthma control? (1–5)
inputs.options_text: 1 = not controlled at all; 5 = completely controlled

bands.meaning: Not well controlled asthma. Step up therapy.
Partly controlled. Consider step-up.
Well controlled. Maintain current therapy.

citations.text: Nathan RA, Sorkness CA, Kosinski M, et al. Development of the asthma control test: a survey for assessing asthma control. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2004;113(1):59-65. PMID: 14713908

entries.limitations: Patient-reported (may overestimate control). Does not capture lung function (FEV1). 4-week recall period. Cannot distinguish asthma from COPD. Not validated in children <12 (cACT version for ages 4–11). Does not predict exacerbations as well as ACQ.
entries.copyright: licensed — verify before use (©QualityMetric Incorporated / GlaxoSmithKline; free for clinical use but verify for commercial app)

entries.name: ATLAS Score
entries.purpose: Predicts 30-day mortality in CAP caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae to guide antibiotic treatment decisions.
entries.formula_human: ATLAS = Age_points(0–3) + Temp≥38.5(−1) + Altered_MS(1) + Low_BP(1) + Effusion(1) + Smoking(1)

bands.meaning: Low risk (~1% mortality)
Moderate risk (~5–8%)
High risk (~15–40%)

citations.text: Aspa J, Rajas O, de Castro FR, et al. A prospective study of clinical features and mortality in Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteremia with identification of prognostic factors using a new scoring system (ATLAS). Clin Infect Dis. 2011;52:1085-1092. PMID: 21460315

entries.limitations: Specific to pneumococcal CAP only. Less widely used than CURB-65/PSI. Negative point for fever (counterintuitive to some clinicians). Validation limited to specific populations.

entries.name: Infectious Diseases Society of America / American Thoracic Society Minor Criteria
entries.purpose: Identifies patients with severe CAP requiring ICU admission based on minor severity criteria.
entries.formula_human: ≥3 minor criteria OR 1 major criterion (septic shock requiring vasopressors, or mechanical ventilation) = severe CAP requiring ICU

bands.meaning: Severe CAP. ICU admission recommended.
Non-severe CAP. Ward-level care.

citations.text: Mandell LA, Wunderink RG, Anzueto A, et al. Infectious Diseases Society of America/American Thoracic Society consensus guidelines on the management of community-acquired pneumonia in adults. Clin Infect Dis. 2007;44(Suppl 2):S27-S72. PMID: 17278083

entries.limitations: Not a single numeric score but a criteria-count system. Different from CURB-65/PSI in that it predicts need for ICU, not mortality. Some criteria overlap with sepsis definitions. Does not capture severity within ICU. Used alongside major criteria for triage.

entries.name: GOLD 2024 Classification (ABCD)
entries.purpose: Groups COPD patients by symptom burden and exacerbation history to guide initial pharmacotherapy per Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease.
entries.formula_human:
2024 GOLD Groups:
Group A: 0–1 exacerbation/year (none hospitalized) + low symptoms (CAT <10 or mMRC 0–1)
Group B: 0–1 exacerbation/year (none hospitalized) + high symptoms (CAT ≥10 or mMRC ≥2)
Group E (Elevated risk): ≥2 exacerbations/year OR ≥1 hospitalized + either symptom level
Note: GOLD 2024 simplified from ABCD to ABE grouping.

inputs.label: FEV1 % predicted (spirometric severity)
inputs.points_text: used in old ABCD; now primarily for spirometric grade only in GOLD 2024

inputs.label: Exacerbation history
inputs.description: Number of moderate-to-severe exacerbations in past year

inputs.label: Symptom burden
inputs.description: CAT score or mMRC dyspnea score
inputs.options_text: CAT <10 or mMRC 0–1 = less symptoms; CAT ≥10 or mMRC ≥2 = more symptoms
inputs.points_text: categorizes into A/B or E groups

bands.meaning: Low risk, low symptoms. Bronchodilator (SABA/SAMA or LABA or LAMA).
Low risk, high symptoms. LABA + LAMA.
High exacerbation risk. LABA + LAMA; consider LABA + LAMA + ICS if eosinophils ≥300.

citations.text: Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD). Global Strategy for Prevention, Diagnosis and Management of COPD: 2024 Report. Available at goldcopd.org

entries.limitations: Classification scheme rather than a validated scoring system. Cutoffs are somewhat arbitrary. Does not capture frailty, comorbidities, or biomarkers (blood eosinophils now incorporated separately for ICS decisions). 2024 update changed from ABCD to ABE (confusing for those familiar with older versions).
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app — GOLD guidelines available at goldcopd.org

entries.name: DECAF Score
entries.purpose: Predicts in-hospital mortality in acute exacerbations of COPD using five readily available clinical variables.
entries.formula_human: DECAF = Dyspnea(0-2) + Eosinopenia(1) + Consolidation(1) + Acidemia(1) + atrial_Fibrillation(1)

inputs.label: Dyspnea (eMRCD 5a or 5b)
inputs.description: Extended MRC Dyspnea scale: 5a = dyspnea after washing/dressing; 5b = housebound due to breathlessness

inputs.label: atrial Fibrillation
inputs.description: AF on ECG or known AF

bands.meaning: Low risk of in-hospital death (~1%). Consider ward-level care.
Moderate risk (~4%). Consider closer monitoring.
High risk (~10–50%). Consider HDU/ICU, palliative care discussion.

citations.text: Steer J, Gibson J, Bourke SC. The DECAF Score: predicting hospital mortality in exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Thorax. 2012;67(11):970-976. PMID: 22863759

entries.limitations: Validated primarily in UK. Requires ABG. eMRCD 5a vs 5b may be difficult to assess acutely. Eosinopenia cutoff is laboratory-dependent. Not validated for non-COPD breathlessness.

entries.name: PRE-DELIRIC (PREdiction of DELIRium in ICu patients)
entries.purpose: Predicts delirium within 24 hours of ICU admission using data available at admission, enabling early intervention.
entries.formula_human: logit = β₀ + Σβᵢxᵢ. P(delirium) = 1/(1 + e^(−logit)). Exact coefficients published in van den Boogaard M, et al. 2012 and updated in 2014. Available at www.pre-deliric.nl.

bands.meaning: Low delirium risk
Moderate risk; implement delirium prevention bundle
High risk; intensive delirium prevention measures indicated

citations.text: van den Boogaard M, Pickkers P, Slooter AJC, et al. Development and validation of PRE-DELIRIC (PREdiction of DELIRium in ICu patients) delirium prediction model for intensive care patients: observational multicentre study. BMJ. 2012;344:e420. PMID: 22323493

entries.limitations: Requires APACHE II score. Sedative/opioid use may be a confounder (risk factor AND treatment). Not validated in all international settings. Cannot be used in patients already delirious.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app — pre-deliric.nl

entries.name: Prediction of Activity and Cognitive Trajectory
entries.purpose: Early prediction model for ICU delirium using only variables available at the moment of ICU admission (before full 24h assessment).
entries.formula_human: logit = β₀ + Σβᵢxᵢ. P(delirium) = 1/(1 + e^(−logit)). Exact coefficients in Wassenaar A, et al. 2015.

bands.meaning: Low risk of ICU delirium
Moderate risk
High risk; early delirium prevention recommended

citations.text: Wassenaar A, van den Boogaard M, van Achterberg T, et al. Multinational development and validation of an early prediction model for delirium in ICU patients. Intensive Care Med. 2015;41(6):1048-1056. PMID: 25940968

entries.limitations: Does not require APACHE II (advantage over PRE-DELIRIC). Lower discrimination than PRE-DELIRIC. Limited international validation outside Europe. Does not incorporate ICU-specific interventions.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: National Early Warning Score
entries.purpose: Standardized track-and-trigger system for detecting clinical deterioration in acute care settings; endorsed by the Royal College of Physicians (UK).
entries.formula_human: NEWS = RR_points + SpO2_points + Supplemental_O2(2) + Temperature_points + SBP_points + HR_points + Consciousness_points

bands.meaning: Low clinical risk
Low-moderate risk; continue routine monitoring
Urgent review by ward-based clinical team
Medium risk; urgent or emergency assessment by clinician with competence in acute illness
High risk; emergency response by critical care outreach team; consider ICU transfer

citations.text: Royal College of Physicians. National Early Warning Score (NEWS): Standardising the assessment of acute-illness severity in the NHS. Report of a working party. London: RCP; 2012.

entries.limitations: UK-developed; may need local validation for other healthcare systems. AVPU consciousness measure is less granular than GCS. Does not capture lab values. SpO₂ can be unreliable in patients on high-flow oxygen. Various electronic implementations may differ slightly.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: Mortality Probability Model III (at ICU Admission)
entries.purpose: Predicts hospital mortality using data available at ICU admission (time zero), avoiding the 24-hour collection delay.
entries.formula_human: logit = β₀ + Σβᵢxᵢ. Hospital mortality = 1/(1 + e^(−logit)). All coefficients published in Higgins TL, et al. 2007. About 15 variables at time zero.

inputs.label: Other variables
inputs.description: Emergency admission, medical vs surgical, etc.

bands.meaning: Low predicted mortality
Moderate predicted mortality
High predicted mortality

citations.text: Higgins TL, Teres D, Copes WS, et al. Assessing contemporary ICU outcome using an original Mortality Probability Model. Crit Care Med. 2007;35(5):1285-1291. PMID: 17414091

entries.limitations: US-centric calibration. Less commonly used than APACHE or SAPS. Requires sedation assessment for GCS. Not widely available outside US hospital systems.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: Simplified Acute Physiology Score 3
entries.purpose: Updated ICU mortality prediction using data available at ICU admission (first hour) and before ICU, eliminating the 24-hour collection delay.
entries.formula_human: SAPS 3 = Σ of all variable points from 20 variables. Then: ln(R/(1−R)) = a + b × SAPS3 + c × ln(SAPS3 + 1) with region-specific (Europe, Australasia, Central/South America, North America) calibration constants a, b, c. Exact coefficients published in Moreno RP, et al. 2005.

inputs.label: Demographics
inputs.description: Age, sex, comorbidities (cancer, heart failure, cirrhosis, renal failure, HIV, immunosuppression, etc.)

inputs.label: Physiologic variables before ICU
inputs.description: GCS, HR, SBP, bilirubin, creatinine, platelets, WBC, pH, PaO₂/FiO₂, lactate, etc.
inputs.options_text: worst values in hour before or at ICU admission

inputs.label: Circumstances of ICU admission
inputs.description: Location before ICU, use of vasoactive drugs, intubation, planned/unplanned, reason for admission, surgical status

bands.meaning: Low predicted hospital mortality
Moderate predicted mortality
High predicted mortality (regionally calibrated)

citations.text: Moreno RP, Metnitz PGH, Almeida E, et al. SAPS 3 — From evaluation of the patient to evaluation of the intensive care unit. Part 2: Development of a prognostic model for hospital mortality at ICU admission. Intensive Care Med. 2005;31(10):1345-1355. PMID: 16132892

entries.limitations: Region-specific calibration needed. More complex than SAPS II. Requires variables available at admission (may miss patients with rapid deterioration after admission). Less widely used than APACHE for benchmarking in some regions.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: Glasgow Outcome Scale — Extended
entries.purpose: 8-point scale assessing global functional outcome after brain injury, providing more granularity than the original GOS.
entries.formula_human:
Categorical classification:
1 = Dead
2 = Vegetative state
3 = Lower severe disability (conscious but dependent on others for daily support)
4 = Upper severe disability (independent at home but dependent outside)
5 = Lower moderate disability (independent at home, limited outside; unable to return to work/school)
6 = Upper moderate disability (independent at home and outside; reduced social/work participation)
7 = Lower good recovery (resumption of normal life with minor neurological/psychological deficits)
8 = Upper good recovery (fully recovered)

inputs.label: Functional outcome
inputs.description: Patient's overall functional status based on consciousness, independence, social participation, and return to work

bands.meaning: Unfavorable outcome (dead, vegetative, or severely disabled)
Favorable outcome (moderate disability to good recovery)

citations.text: Jennett B, Bond M. Assessment of outcome after severe brain damage: a practical scale. Lancet. 1975;305(7905):480-484. PMID: 46957 (original GOS); Wilson JTL, et al. J Neurotrauma. 1998;15:581-588 (extended version)

entries.limitations: Coarse scale even in extended form. Significant ceiling effect in mild TBI. Requires structured interview for reliable assessment. May not capture subtle cognitive deficits. Proxy-assessed versions may differ from self-report.

entries.name: Modified Nutrition Risk in Critically Ill Score
entries.purpose: Identifies ICU patients at high nutritional risk who may benefit most from aggressive nutrition therapy.
entries.formula_human: mNUTRIC = Age(0–2) + APACHE_II(0–3) + SOFA(0–3) + Comorbidities(0–2) + Days_to_ICU(0–1). Total = 0–9 (without IL-6) or 0–13 (full NUTRIC with IL-6).

inputs.label: Days from hospital admission to ICU
inputs.description: Length of stay before ICU admission

inputs.label: IL-6 (optional in full NUTRIC; removed in mNUTRIC)
inputs.description: IL-6 level (not required in modified version)

bands.meaning: Low nutritional risk. Minimal benefit from aggressive nutrition therapy.
High nutritional risk. Aggressive nutrition therapy may improve outcomes.

citations.text: Heyland DK, Dhaliwal R, Jiang X, Day AG. Identifying critically ill patients who benefit the most from nutrition therapy: the development and initial validation of a novel risk assessment tool. Crit Care. 2011;15(6):R268. PMID: 22122716

entries.limitations: Requires APACHE II and SOFA scores (not available immediately at admission). IL-6 removed in mNUTRIC but may limit discrimination. Does not account for pre-ICU nutrition status or BMI. Not widely used in all settings.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: Multiple Organ Dysfunction Score
entries.purpose: Quantifies organ dysfunction in ICU patients across six organ systems using physiologic and laboratory data.
entries.formula_human: MODS = Respiratory(0–4) + Renal(0–4) + Hepatic(0–4) + Cardiovascular(0–4) + Hematologic(0–4) + Neurologic(0–4). Total = 0–24.

bands.meaning: No organ dysfunction
Mild dysfunction
Moderate dysfunction
Severe dysfunction
Critical multiorgan failure

citations.text: Marshall JC, Cook DJ, Christou NV, et al. Multiple organ dysfunction score: a reliable descriptor of a complex clinical outcome. Crit Care Med. 1995;23(10):1638-1652. PMID: 7587228

entries.limitations: Cardiovascular subscore uses Pressure-Adjusted Heart Rate (PAR = HR × RAP/MAP), requiring CVP measurement (invasive). Less commonly used than SOFA in current practice. Single-center derivation.

entries.name: Sepsis-related Organ Failure Assessment — Cardiovascular
entries.purpose: Cardiovascular subscore of SOFA used specifically to define septic shock in Sepsis-3 (vasopressor requirement + lactate).
entries.formula_human: Septic shock (Sepsis-3 definition) = SOFA-CV ≥2 (requiring vasopressors to maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg) AND serum lactate >2 mmol/L despite adequate fluid resuscitation

inputs.label: Serum lactate
inputs.points_text: defined by Sepsis-3 for septic shock

bands.meaning: Septic shock — in-hospital mortality ≥40%

entries.limitations: Operational definition — the SOFA-CV subscore in isolation is less informative than full SOFA. Lactate measurement may be delayed. Fluid resuscitation adequacy is subjective.

entries.name: Cardiac Arrest Survival Post (CASP) Score
entries.purpose: Predicts poor neurological outcome at hospital discharge in OHCA patients who achieve return of spontaneous circulation.
entries.formula_human: CAHP score = Σ(coefficients × variables). Exact coefficients published in Maupain C, et al. 2016. Score mapped to probability of poor neurological outcome (CPC 3-5).

bands.meaning: Low probability of poor neurological outcome
Intermediate probability
High probability of poor neurological outcome (CPC 3–5)

citations.text: Maupain C, Boughariou W, Deye N, et al. The CAHP (Cardiac Arrest Hospital Prognosis) score: a tool for risk stratification after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Eur Heart J. 2016;37(42):3222-3228. PMID: 27567053

entries.limitations: Requires admission labs (pH, lactate). Resuscitation duration may be imprecise. Developed in Paris — external validation limited. Should not be used alone for withdrawal decisions (requires multimodal assessment per guidelines).

entries.name: Glasgow-Pittsburgh Cerebral Performance Category
entries.purpose: Standardized outcome scale for neurological recovery after cardiac arrest, used in the Utstein reporting template.
entries.formula_human:
Categorical classification:
1 = Good cerebral performance (conscious, alert, normal function)
2 = Moderate cerebral disability (conscious, sufficient cerebral function for independent activities of daily life)
3 = Severe cerebral disability (conscious, dependent on others for daily activities)
4 = Coma or vegetative state
5 = Death

inputs.label: Neurological function
inputs.description: Overall cerebral performance based on consciousness, independence, and cognitive function

bands.meaning: Favorable neurological outcome
Unfavorable neurological outcome

citations.text: Brain Resuscitation Clinical Trial I Study Group. Randomized clinical study of thiopental loading in comatose survivors of cardiac arrest. N Engl J Med. 1986;314:397-403. PMID: 3511384 (CPC concept); Jennett B, Bond M. Lancet. 1975;1:480-484 (Glasgow outcome concept)

entries.limitations: Crude categorical scale with significant ceiling and floor effects. Inter-rater reliability moderate. Category 2 vs 3 distinction can be subjective. Does not capture specific cognitive domains.

entries.name: CROP Index (Compliance, Rate, Oxygenation, Pressure)
entries.purpose: Integrates respiratory mechanics, gas exchange, and respiratory drive to predict weaning outcome from mechanical ventilation.
entries.formula_human: CROP = (Compliance × MIP × (PaO₂/PAO₂)) / RR

inputs.label: PaO₂/PAO₂ ratio
inputs.description: Ratio of arterial to alveolar oxygen tension

bands.meaning: Predicts successful weaning
Predicts weaning failure

citations.text: Yang KL, Tobin MJ. N Engl J Med. 1991;324(21):1445-1450. PMID: 2023603

entries.limitations: Requires MIP measurement (effort-dependent, variable). More complex to calculate than RSBI. Requires ABG. Less widely validated than RSBI. Rarely used in clinical practice compared to simpler indices.

entries.name: Pediatric Asthma Severity Score
entries.purpose: Clinical scoring system for assessing acute asthma severity in children in the emergency department.
entries.formula_human: PASS = RR(0–2) + Accessory_muscles(0–2) + Wheezing(0–3) + SpO2(0–2)

inputs.label: Respiratory rate
inputs.options_text: 0 = normal for age; 1 = moderately increased; 2 = markedly increased

inputs.label: Accessory muscle use
inputs.description: Use of accessory muscles of respiration

inputs.label: Wheezing
inputs.options_text: 0 = none; 1 = end-expiratory; 2 = throughout expiration; 3 = inspiratory and expiratory or absent (silent chest)

bands.meaning: Mild asthma exacerbation
Moderate exacerbation
Severe/life-threatening exacerbation

citations.text: Carroll CL, et al. Development and validation of a Pediatric Asthma Severity Score. J Asthma. 2009;46:659-664. PMID: 19657899

entries.limitations: Requires auscultation (subjective). Age-adjusted RR cutoffs must be referenced. SpO2 dependent on supplemental O2. Inter-rater variability in wheezing assessment. Not as widely used as PRAM or other pediatric respiratory scores.

entries.name: Pediatric Respiratory Assessment Measure
entries.purpose: Validated acute asthma severity score for children in the ED, based on clinical examination without requiring auscultation.
entries.formula_human: PRAM = Suprasternal_retraction(1) + Scalene(1) + Air_entry(0–2) + SpO2(0/1/3) + Wheezing(0/1/2)

inputs.label: Wheezing
inputs.options_text: 0 = none; 1 = expiratory only; 2 = inspiratory + expiratory or absent

bands.meaning: Mild exacerbation
Moderate exacerbation
Severe exacerbation

citations.text: Chalut DS, Ducharme FM, Davis GM. The Preschool Respiratory Assessment Measure (PRAM): a responsive index of acute asthma severity. J Pediatr. 2000;137(6):762-768. PMID: 11113832

entries.limitations: Requires auscultation for air entry and wheezing (subjective). Not validated in infants <1 year. SpO2 cutoffs vary slightly by source. May be difficult to assess in crying child. Validated primarily in Canadian populations.

entries.name: European Society of Cardiology Prognostic Model for PE
entries.purpose: Stepwise risk stratification of PE patients from low-risk to high-risk for early mortality to guide treatment intensity.
entries.formula_human:
Stepwise algorithm:
1. High-risk: hemodynamic instability → primary reperfusion (systemic thrombolysis or catheter-directed therapy)
2. Intermediate-high: sPESI ≥1 + RV dysfunction + elevated troponin → consider reperfusion if deterioration
3. Intermediate-low: sPESI ≥1 + only one of RV dysfunction or troponin elevation → hospital monitoring
4. Low-risk: sPESI = 0 → consider early discharge or outpatient treatment

inputs.label: PESI/sPESI
inputs.description: Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index or simplified version

bands.meaning: Early mortality >15%. Primary reperfusion therapy.
Early mortality 3–15%. Close monitoring; consider reperfusion if deterioration.
Early mortality 1–3%. Hospital admission for monitoring.
Early mortality <1%. Early discharge possible.

citations.text: Konstantinides SV, Meyer G, Becattini C, et al. 2019 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism. Eur Heart J. 2020;41(4):543-603. PMID: 31504429

entries.limitations: Algorithm rather than a single numeric score. RV assessment requires echo or CT (availability). Troponin and BNP assays vary by institution. Different cutoffs for 'elevated' across assays. Treatment thresholds for reperfusion are debated.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index (PESI) and simplified PESI (sPESI)
entries.purpose: Estimates 30-day mortality in patients with acute pulmonary embolism to guide decisions on outpatient vs inpatient treatment and monitoring intensity.
entries.formula_human:
FULL PESI = Age(years) + Male(10) + Cancer(30) + Heart_failure(10) + Chronic_lung_disease(10) + HR≥110(20) + SBP<100(30) + RR≥30(20) + Temp<36°C(20) + Altered_mental_status(60) + SpO₂<90%(20)

Risk classes: I ≤65 | II 66–85 | III 86–105 | IV 106–125 | V >125

sPESI = Age>80(1) + Cancer(1) + Chronic_cardiopulmonary_disease(1) + HR≥110(1) + SBP<100(1) + SpO₂<90%(1); range 0–6

inputs.label: Age
inputs.description: Age in years (full PESI: 1 point per year of age; sPESI: age >80 = 1 point)
inputs.points_text: full PESI: age in years; sPESI: >80 = 1

bands.meaning: 30-day mortality 0–1.6% — very low risk; consider outpatient treatment.
30-day mortality 1.7–3.5% — low risk; consider outpatient treatment.
30-day mortality 3.2–7.1% — moderate risk; consider inpatient treatment.
30-day mortality 4.0–11.4% — high risk; inpatient treatment.
30-day mortality 10.0–24.5% — very high risk; inpatient treatment, consider ICU.
Low risk (30-day mortality ~1.0%) — candidate for outpatient treatment.
High risk (30-day mortality ~10.9%) — inpatient treatment.

citations.text: Full PESI: Aujesky D et al., Eur Respir J 2006 (as cited by the corrections dossier; original derivation Aujesky D et al., Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2005 — resolve exact citation/PMID at build time, do not guess). sPESI: Jiménez D et al., Eur Respir J 2010 (resolve PMID at build time).

entries.limitations: Full PESI requires 11 variables; sPESI is simpler but dichotomous. Neither incorporates imaging (RV dysfunction) or biomarkers (troponin/BNP) — combine with ESC risk stratification for intermediate-risk decisions. Age dominates the full PESI score.

entries.name: Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes AKI Criteria
entries.purpose: Defines and stages acute kidney injury using serum creatinine rise and urine output criteria. Standard international definition.
entries.formula_human:
Staging system:

Stage 1: SCr increase ≥0.3 mg/dL (≥26.5 µmol/L) within 48h OR SCr increase ≥1.5–1.9× baseline within 7 days OR UO <0.5 mL/kg/h for 6–12 hours

Stage 2: SCr increase 2.0–2.9× baseline within 7 days OR UO <0.5 mL/kg/h for ≥12 hours

Stage 3: SCr increase ≥3.0× baseline within 7 days OR SCr ≥4.0 mg/dL (≥353.6 µmol/L) OR initiation of RRT OR (if <18 years) eGFR decrease to <35 mL/min/1.73m² OR UO <0.3 mL/kg/h for ≥24 hours OR anuria for ≥12 hours

inputs.label: Serum creatinine change
inputs.description: Change in serum creatinine from baseline within 48 hours or 7 days
inputs.options_text: Increase ≥0.3 mg/dL within 48h OR increase ≥1.5× baseline within 7 days OR UO criteria

bands.meaning: No creatinine or urine output criteria met
Mild AKI. Identify and treat underlying cause. Monitor closely.
Moderate AKI. Nephrology consultation recommended.
Severe AKI. Nephrology consultation mandatory. Evaluate for RRT. Mortality significantly increased.

citations.text: Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Acute Kidney Injury Work Group. KDIGO clinical practice guideline for acute kidney injury. Kidney Int Suppl. 2012;2(1):1-138. (Consensus guideline, no single PMID for the guideline itself)

entries.limitations: Requires baseline creatinine (may be unknown in 50% of cases). Creatinine-based criteria may not detect early AKI (biomarker lag). Urine output criteria require accurate measurement (difficult in non-catheterized patients). Non-specific — many causes of creatinine rise. Does not incorporate biomarkers (NGAL, KIM-1) which may detect AKI earlier.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published academic guideline

entries.name: CKD-EPI Cystatin C Equation (2012)
entries.purpose: Estimates GFR from serum cystatin C, an alternative to creatinine-based equations, less affected by muscle mass.
entries.formula_human:
If cystatin C ≤0.8 mg/L:
eGFR = 133 × (Scys/0.8)^(−0.499) × 0.996^Age × (0.932 if female)

If cystatin C >0.8 mg/L:
eGFR = 133 × (Scys/0.8)^(−1.328) × 0.996^Age × (0.932 if female)

eGFR in mL/min/1.73 m²

bands.meaning: Normal or high (G1)
Mildly decreased (G2)
Moderately decreased (G3a/G3b)
Severely decreased (G4)
Kidney failure (G5)

citations.text: Inker LA, Schmid CH, Tighiouart H, et al. Estimating glomerular filtration rate from serum creatinine and cystatin C. N Engl J Med. 2012;367(1):20-29. PMID: 22762315

entries.limitations: Cystatin C is more expensive than creatinine and not universally available. Cystatin C can be affected by thyroid dysfunction, corticosteroids, inflammation, and obesity (higher in obese patients). Accuracy may be lower in transplant recipients. Combined creatinine-cystatin C equation is more accurate than either alone but requires both assays.

entries.name: Cockcroft-Gault Equation
entries.purpose: Estimates creatinine clearance (not GFR) for drug dosing in adults. One of the oldest and most widely used equations for medication adjustment.
entries.formula_human:
CrCl (mL/min) = [(140 − Age) × Weight(kg)] / (72 × Scr(mg/dL)) × 0.85 if female

Note: Weight should be adjusted for obesity (use ideal body weight or adjusted body weight = IBW + 0.4 × (actual − IBW)).

inputs.label: Weight
inputs.description: Body weight in kg (ideally ideal body weight; use actual weight if not obese)

bands.meaning: Normal renal function
Mild impairment
Moderate impairment. Drug dose adjustments may be needed.
Severe impairment. Significant drug dose reductions required.
End-stage renal disease. Dialysis consideration.

citations.text: Cockcroft DW, Gault MH. Prediction of creatinine clearance from serum creatinine. Nephron. 1976;16(1):31-41. PMID: 1244564

entries.limitations: Overestimates GFR at low GFR. Less accurate than CKD-EPI for estimating GFR (systematically biased). Original derivation in 249 hospitalized men (poor generalizability). Weight-dependent — problematic in obese, malnourished, or edematous patients. Still recommended for aminoglycoside and vancomycin dosing. Not recommended for GFR reporting by KDIGO (use CKD-EPI). Does not account for race (by design).

entries.name: Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration Equation
entries.purpose: Estimates glomerular filtration rate (GFR) from serum creatinine, age, and sex; preferred equation for CKD staging per KDIGO guidelines.
entries.formula_human:
CKD-EPI 2009 (creatinine-based):
eGFR = 141 × min(Scr/κ, 1)^α × max(Scr/κ, 1)^(−1.209) × 0.993^Age × [1.018 if female]

Where:
- κ = 0.7 (female) or 0.9 (male)
- α = −0.329 (female) or −0.411 (male)
- min = minimum of Scr/κ or 1
- max = maximum of Scr/κ or 1

CKD-EPI 2021 (race-free): Same formula without the race coefficient (removed 2021).
CKD-EPI 2021 equation: eGFR = 142 × min(Scr/κ, 1)^α × max(Scr/κ, 1)^(−1.200) × 0.9938^Age × [1.012 if female]

bands.meaning: G1: Normal or high GFR
G2: Mildly decreased
G3a: Mildly to moderately decreased
G3b: Moderately to severely decreased
G4: Severely decreased
G5: Kidney failure (dialysis or transplant needed)

citations.text: Levey AS, Stevens LA, Schmid CH, et al. A new equation to estimate glomerular filtration rate. Ann Intern Med. 2009;150(9):604-612. PMID: 19414839

entries.limitations: Less accurate at extremes of muscle mass (very muscular, amputees, malnourished). Not accurate in AKI (rapidly changing creatinine). Does not account for race (2021 update) but this was debated. Less accurate above eGFR 60. Cystatin C-based CKD-EPI equation may be more accurate in some subgroups. Not validated in children.

entries.name: CKD-EPI Creatinine-Cystatin C Combined Equation
entries.purpose: Most accurate estimating equation for GFR, combining both creatinine and cystatin C. Recommended by KDIGO when confirmatory GFR estimate is needed.
entries.formula_human:
2021 race-free equation:
eGFR = 135 × min(Scr/κ, 1)^α × max(Scr/κ, 1)^(−0.544) × min(Scys/0.8, 1)^(−0.323) × max(Scys/0.8, 1)^(−0.778) × 0.9961^Age × [0.963 if female]

Where: κ and α are sex-specific (same as CKD-EPI Cr 2021)

bands.range: Same GFR staging as CKD-EPI Cr (G1–G5)
bands.meaning: Same KDIGO GFR categories apply

citations.text: Inker LA, Eneanya ND, Coresh J, et al. New creatinine- and cystatin C-based equations to estimate GFR without race. N Engl J Med. 2021;385(19):1737-1749. PMID: 34554658

entries.limitations: Requires both creatinine and cystatin C (limited availability). More expensive. Same limitations of individual markers apply (though combination is more accurate). Not yet widely implemented in all laboratories.

entries.name: CKD-EPI Cystatin C Equation
entries.purpose: Estimates GFR from serum cystatin C (an alternative to creatinine-based equations, less affected by muscle mass).
entries.formula_human:
CKD-EPI CysC (2012): eGFR = 133 × min(Scys/0.8, 1)^(−0.499) × max(Scys/0.8, 1)^(−1.328) × 0.996^Age × [0.932 if female]

Where:
- Scys = serum cystatin C in mg/L
- min = minimum of Scys/0.8 or 1
- max = maximum of Scys/0.8 or 1

inputs.label: Serum cystatin C
inputs.description: Serum cystatin C level in mg/L

bands.meaning: G1: Normal or high
G2: Mildly decreased
G3a: Mildly to moderately decreased
G3b: Moderately to severely decreased
G4: Severely decreased
G5: Kidney failure

citations.text: Inker LA, Schmid CH, Tighiouart H, et al. Estimating glomerular filtration rate from serum creatinine and cystatin C. N Engl J Med. 2012;367(1):20-29. PMID: 22762315

entries.limitations: Cystatin C not universally available. More expensive than creatinine. May be affected by thyroid dysfunction, corticosteroids, obesity, inflammation, and smoking. Less studied than creatinine-based equations. Race-free version available (2021).

entries.name: Modification of Diet in Renal Disease Equation
entries.purpose: Estimates GFR from serum creatinine, age, sex, and race. Historically the standard equation for CKD staging before CKD-EPI.
entries.formula_human:
MDRD 4-variable (IDMS-traceable): eGFR = 175 × Scr(mg/dL)^(−1.154) × Age^(−0.203) × [0.742 if female] × [1.212 if Black]

Units: mL/min/1.73 m²

bands.range: Same KDIGO GFR staging as CKD-EPI

citations.text: Levey AS, Bosch JP, Lewis JB, et al. A more accurate method to estimate glomerular filtration rate from serum creatinine: a new prediction equation. Modification of Diet in Renal Disease Study Group. Ann Intern Med. 1999;130(6):461-470. PMID: 10075613 (original); Levey AS, et al. Ann Intern Med. 200

entries.limitations: Inaccurate at GFR >60 mL/min (underestimates normal kidney function). Includes race coefficient (no longer recommended). Derived in CKD patients only (not validated in general population). Largely superseded by CKD-EPI 2021. Some laboratories still report MDRD-derived eGFR.

entries.name: Modified CT Severity Index / CT Severity Index
entries.purpose: Assesses severity of acute pancreatitis based on CT findings of pancreatic necrosis and peripancreatic fluid collections.
entries.formula_human:
CTSI = Inflammation(0–6) + Necrosis(0–6)

Modified CTSI (MCTSI):
- Normal pancreas = 0
- Intrinsic pancreatic abnormalities (with or without peripancreatic changes) = 2
- Pancreatic/peripancreatic fluid collections or peripancreatic fat necrosis = 4
- Necrosis: none = 0; <30% = 2; ≥30% = 4
MCTSI = Inflammation(0–4) + Necrosis(0–4)

Extrapancreatic complications (pleural effusion, ascites, vascular complications, GI tract involvement) = +2 in MCTSI

options.value: Two or more fluid collections or retroperitoneal gas
options.label: Two or more fluid collections or retroperitoneal gas = 6

inputs.label: Necrosis
inputs.description: Percentage of pancreatic necrosis on contrast-enhanced CT

bands.meaning: Mild pancreatitis. Low complication rate (~3%).
Moderate. Complication rate ~20%.
Severe. Complication rate ~60%. Mortality ~17%.

citations.text: Balthazar EJ, Robinson DL, Megibow AJ, Ranson JH. Acute pancreatitis: value of CT in establishing prognosis. Radiology. 1990;174(2):331-336. PMID: 2296641 (CTSI); Mortele KJ, et al. Radiology. 2004;233(1):63-72 (MCTSI)

entries.limitations: Requires contrast-enhanced CT (not indicated in mild pancreatitis). CT timing matters (early CT may underestimate necrosis). Inter-rater variability in assessing necrosis percentage. Necrosis scoring assumes CT performed at 72+ hours. Does not capture extrapancreatic complications well (addressed in MCTSI).

entries.name: Ranson Criteria for Acute Pancreatitis
entries.purpose: Predicts severity and mortality of acute pancreatitis using clinical and laboratory data at admission and at 48 hours.
entries.formula_human:
Ranson = admission criteria (5 points) + 48-hour criteria (6 points).

Note: Separate criteria exist for gallstone vs non-gallstone pancreatitis (gallstone criteria differ slightly in some age thresholds).
Non-gallstone: Age >55, WBC >16k, Glucose >200, LDH >350, AST >250 at admission; Hct drop >10, BUN rise >5, Ca <8, PaO₂ <60, Base deficit >4, Fluid sequestration >6L at 48h.
Gallstone: Age >70, WBC >18k, Glucose >220, LDH >400, AST >250 at admission; same 48h criteria.

bands.meaning: Mild pancreatitis. Mortality <1%.
Moderate severity. Mortality ~15%.
Severe. Mortality ~40%.
Very severe. Mortality ~100% historically (lower with modern ICU care).

citations.text: Ranson JHC, Rifkind KM, Roses DF, et al. Objective early identification of severe acute pancreatitis. Am J Gastroenterol. 1974;61:443-451. PMID: 4826868 (original); Ranson JH. Surg Gynecol Obstet. 1978;146:185-190

entries.limitations: Requires 48 hours for complete scoring (not available at presentation). Cannot be used for early triage. Many criteria (LDH, fluid sequestration) may not be measured routinely. Separate criteria for gallstone vs non-gallstone cause confusion. Outdated mortality estimates (1970s ICU era). Superseded by BISAP and APACHE II in many guidelines. Subjective component (fluid sequestration).

entries.name: Revised Atlanta Classification Severity
entries.purpose: Standardizes definitions and severity classification of acute pancreatitis (mild, moderately severe, severe) based on organ failure.
entries.formula_human:
Severity classification:

Mild: No organ failure, no local or systemic complications. Mortality <1%.

Moderately severe: Transient organ failure (<48h) OR local/systemic complications without persistent organ failure. Mortality ~1–20%.

Severe: Persistent organ failure (>48h) — single organ or multiorgan. Mortality 20–50%.

bands.meaning: No organ failure, no complications. Supportive care. Mortality <1%.
Transient organ failure or local complications. May require HDU. Mortality ~1–20%.
Persistent organ failure (>48h). ICU care mandatory. Mortality 20–50%.

citations.text: Banks PA, Bollen TL, Dervenis C, et al. Classification of acute pancreatitis — 2012: revision of the Atlanta classification and definitions by international consensus. Gut. 2013;62(1):102-111. PMID: 23100216

entries.limitations: Organ failure assessment requires serial monitoring (modified Marshall score — see separate entry). Cannot fully assess at presentation. Local complications require imaging and are time-dependent. Definitions are consensus-based, not empirically derived. Does not directly predict mortality numerically (unlike Ranson or BISAP).
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published academic guideline

entries.name: Maddrey Discriminant Function for Alcoholic Hepatitis
entries.purpose: Identifies severe alcoholic hepatitis with high short-term mortality; determines benefit of corticosteroid therapy.
entries.formula_human:
MDF = 4.6 × (PT_patient − PT_control) + Bilirubin(mg/dL)

Note: Can also be calculated using INR: MDF = 4.6 × (INR − 1) + Bilirubin(mg/dL) — this is an approximation and the original formula uses raw PT seconds.

bands.meaning: Non-severe alcoholic hepatitis. 1-month mortality ~10%. Corticosteroids not routinely recommended.
Severe alcoholic hepatitis. 1-month mortality ~30–50%. Consider corticosteroid trial (prednisolone 40 mg/day × 28 days). Lille score at 7 days should guide response.

citations.text: Maddrey WC, Boitnott JK, Bedine MS, et al. Corticosteroid therapy of alcoholic hepatitis. Gastroenterology. 1978;75(2):193-199. PMID: 352788

entries.limitations: Threshold of 32 is somewhat arbitrary and does not perfectly discriminate responders from non-responders. INR-based approximation may not be exact (varies by thromboplastin). Bilirubin may rise with cholestasis independent of alcoholic hepatitis. Should be used in combination with Lille score to assess treatment response. Confounded by anticoagulant use. Does not capture encephalopathy or renal function (use MELD for broader assessment).

entries.name: Glasgow-Blatchford Score for Upper GI Bleeding
entries.purpose: Predicts need for intervention (blood transfusion, endoscopy, surgery) or death in upper GI bleeding to identify low-risk patients suitable for outpatient management.
entries.formula_human: GBS = BUN(0–6) + Hemoglobin(0–6, sex-specific) + SBP(0–3) + HR≥100(1) + Melena(1) + Syncope(2) + Hepatic_disease(2) + Cardiac_failure(2)

bands.meaning: Very low risk. No intervention needed. Safe for outpatient management. NPV ~99%.
Low risk. Consider outpatient management with close follow-up.
Moderate-high risk. Inpatient admission and endoscopy recommended.
High likelihood of needing intervention.

citations.text: Blatchford O, Murray WR, Blatchford M. A risk score to predict need for treatment for upper-gastrointestinal haemorrhage. Lancet. 2000;356(9238):1318-1321. PMID: 11073021

entries.limitations: Does not predict mortality directly (predicts need for intervention). Score of 0 does not guarantee no need for endoscopy (varicose bleeds may present with score 0 initially). Does not capture antiplatelet/anticoagulant use. Not validated for lower GI bleeding. Hepatic disease criterion is broad (may include mild disease).

entries.name: Rockall Score for Upper GI Bleeding
entries.purpose: Predicts mortality after upper GI bleeding using clinical and endoscopic findings. Requires endoscopy for complete scoring.
entries.formula_human:
Rockall = Age(0–2) + Shock(0–2) + Comorbidity(0–3) + Diagnosis(0–2) + Stigmata(0–2)

Pre-endoscopy score = Age + Shock + Comorbidity (range 0–7)
Full score = all 5 components (range 0–11)

options.value: Renal failure, liver failure, disseminated malignancy
options.label: Renal failure, liver failure, disseminated malignancy = 3

inputs.label: Major stigmata of recent hemorrhage
inputs.description: Active bleeding, visible vessel, or adherent clot at endoscopy

options.value: Blood in upper GI, adherent clot, visible vessel, spurting
options.label: Blood in upper GI, adherent clot, visible vessel, spurting = 2

bands.meaning: Very low mortality risk. Consider early discharge from ED.
Low mortality risk (~0–2%). Low rebleeding risk.
Low-moderate risk (~3–5% mortality).
Moderate-high risk (~10–15% mortality).
High mortality risk (~25–40%+).

citations.text: Rockall TA, Logan RFA, Devlin HB, et al. Risk assessment after acute upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage. Gut. 1996;38(3):316-321. PMID: 8675081

entries.limitations: Requires endoscopy for complete scoring (endoscopic variables unavailable at presentation). Mortality prediction is better than rebleeding prediction. Comorbidity categories are imprecise (where does 'significant' begin?). Does not capture antiplatelet/anticoagulant use. Subjective endoscopic assessment (inter-observer variability). GBS is preferred for pre-endoscopy risk stratification.

entries.name: Child-Turcotte-Pugh Score
entries.purpose: Assesses severity of liver cirrhosis and predicts survival. Used for transplant eligibility and surgical risk stratification.
entries.formula_human:
CTP = Bilirubin(1–3) + Albumin(1–3) + INR(1–3) + Ascites(1–3) + Encephalopathy(1–3)

Note: For primary biliary cholangitis and primary sclerosing cholangitis, bilirubin thresholds differ: <4 = 1; 4–10 = 2; >10 = 3.

inputs.label: Ascites
inputs.description: Ascites on clinical exam or imaging

bands.meaning: Well-compensated cirrhosis. 1-year survival ~100%. Low surgical risk.
Significant functional compromise. 1-year survival ~80%. Moderate surgical risk.
Decompensated cirrhosis. 1-year survival ~45%. High surgical risk. Transplant evaluation recommended.

citations.text: Pugh RNH, Murray-Lyon IM, Dawson JL, et al. Transection of the oesophagus for bleeding oesophageal varices. Br J Surg. 1973;60(8):646-649. PMID: 4541913 (original concept: Child CG, Turcotte JG. Surgery and portal hypertension. Major Probl Clin Surg. 1964;1:1-85)

entries.limitations: Two subjective components (ascites and encephalopathy) are inter-observer variable. Does not differentiate well within Class A (ceiling effect) or Class C (floor effect). Does not include renal function (major predictor). Superseded by MELD for transplant allocation in most countries. Crude discrimination compared to MELD. Does not incorporate etiology of liver disease.

entries.name: AIMS65 Score (for Upper GI Bleeding)
entries.purpose: Predicts in-hospital mortality in patients presenting with upper gastrointestinal bleeding.
entries.formula_human: AIMS65 = Albumin<3(1) + INR>1.5(1) + Mental_status(1) + SBP≤90(1) + Age>65(1)

bands.meaning: Low mortality risk (~0.3–1%). Consider outpatient management.
Moderate risk.
High mortality risk (~10–25%). Inpatient admission and aggressive management.

citations.text: Saltzman JR, Tabak YP, Hyett BH, et al. A simple risk score accurately predicts in-hospital mortality, length of stay, and cost in acute upper GI bleeding. Gastrointest Endosc. 2011;74(6):1215-1224. PMID: 21963067

entries.limitations: Does not identify source of bleeding or need for intervention. Albumin may not be available at presentation. GCS <14 cutoff is relatively insensitive (most UGIB patients are alert). Does not include heart rate, hemoglobin drop, or endoscopic findings. Mixed validation results for rebleeding and intervention outcomes.

entries.name: Spetzler-Martin Grading Scale for Arteriovenous Malformations
entries.purpose: Predicts surgical risk (morbidity) of microsurgical resection of brain arteriovenous malformations (AVMs).
entries.formula_human: Spetzler-Martin = Size(1–3) + Eloquence(0/1) + Venous_drainage(0/1)

inputs.label: Size of nidus
inputs.description: Maximum diameter of the AVM nidus

options.value: Deep venous drainage (deep veins, Galen system, or internal
options.label: Deep venous drainage (deep veins, Galen system, or internal cerebral veins) = 1

bands.meaning: Low surgical risk (~0% major morbidity). Surgery recommended.
Low risk (~3–5% major morbidity).
Moderate risk (~8–12%). Individualized decision.
High risk (~20–30%). Surgery generally not recommended; consider radiosurgery/embolization.
Very high surgical risk (~30–50%+ major morbidity). Conservative management or multimodality treatment.

citations.text: Spetzler RF, Martin NA. A proposed grading system for arteriovenous malformations. J Neurosurg. 1986;65(4):476-483. PMID: 3760956

entries.limitations: Subjective (eloquence assessment may vary). Does not capture patient age, hemorrhagic presentation, or nidal compactness. Supplemented Spetzler-Martin (addition of patient age) may improve accuracy. Does not apply to dural arteriovenous fistulas. Grade III patients have the most decision ambiguity.

entries.name: Headache Impact Test-6
entries.purpose: Validated 6-item questionnaire assessing the overall impact of headache on daily life, useful for migraine and chronic headache monitoring.
entries.formula_human: HIT-6 = Sum of all 6 item scores (each 6, 8, 10, 11, or 13)

inputs.label: Pain severity
inputs.description: How often headache pain is severe (never/ rarely/ sometimes/ very often/ always)

inputs.label: Daily activity limitation
inputs.description: How often headache limits daily activities

inputs.label: Fatigue/weariness
inputs.description: How often headache causes feeling of fatigue

inputs.label: Concentration difficulty
inputs.description: How often headache makes it hard to concentrate

inputs.label: Feeling fed up/irritable
inputs.description: How often headache makes you feel fed up or irritable

inputs.label: Activity restriction
inputs.description: How often headache limits ability to participate in activities

bands.meaning: Little or no impact
Some impact
Substantial impact
Severe impact

citations.text: Kosinski M, Bayliss MS, Bjorner JB, et al. A six-item short-form survey for measuring headache impact: the HIT-6. Qual Life Res. 2003;12(8):963-974. PMID: 14651415

entries.limitations: Generic headache impact tool (does not distinguish migraine from tension-type). Self-reported. Scoring of items uses unequal increments (6, 8, 10, 11, 13). Less commonly used clinically than MIDAS for migraine-specific disability. Performance varies by headache frequency.
entries.copyright: licensed — verify before use (©QualityMetric Incorporated; standard use free, commercial use requires license)

entries.name: Migraine Disability Assessment Score
entries.purpose: Patient-completed questionnaire assessing headache-related disability over the prior 3 months to guide migraine treatment intensity.
entries.formula_human: MIDAS = Days_missed_work + Days_reduced_work + Days_missed_household + Days_reduced_household + Days_missed_social

inputs.label: Days of missed work/school
inputs.description: Number of days in last 3 months you missed work or school because of headaches

inputs.label: Days of reduced productivity at work/school
inputs.description: Number of days with reduced productivity (>50% reduction) at work/school

inputs.label: Days missed household work
inputs.description: Days missed doing household work because of headaches

inputs.label: Days of reduced household productivity
inputs.description: Days with reduced productivity in household work

inputs.label: Days missed family/social/leisure activities
inputs.description: Days missed from family, social, or leisure activities

bands.meaning: Grade I: Minimal or infrequent disability. Simple analgesics.
Grade II: Mild disability. Consider migraine-specific therapy.
Grade III: Moderate disability. Migraine prophylaxis should be considered.
Grade IV: Severe disability. Referral to specialist; aggressive prophylaxis.

citations.text: Stewart WF, Lipton RB, Kolodner K, et al. Validity of the Migraine Disability Assessment (MIDAS) score in comparison to a diary-based measure in a population sample of migraine sufferers. Pain. 2000;88(1):41-52. PMID: 11098098

entries.limitations: Patient-reported (subject to recall bias over 3-month period). Does not capture headache frequency or intensity directly. Does not distinguish migraine from other headache types. Cultural variations in disability perception. Equally weights work, household, and social disability.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: Expanded Disability Status Scale
