entries.purpose: Standardized neurological examination-based scale quantifying disability in multiple sclerosis patients.
entries.formula_human:
EDSS is a composite rating based on neurological examination of 8 functional systems. No simple formula — assigned by trained neurologist based on the Kurtzke system:
0 = Normal neurological exam
1.0–3.5 = Minimal to moderate disability (based on FS scores, no or minimal walking impairment)
4.0–5.5 = Increasing ambulatory disability (distance-based)
6.0–6.5 = Requires walking aid
7.0–7.5 = Wheelchair-bound
8.0–8.5 = Bed-bound with some arm function
9.0 = Helpless bed-bound
9.5 = Death due to MS
10 = Death due to MS (by definition)

inputs.label: Functional systems
inputs.description: Eight functional systems assessed: Pyramidal, Cerebellar, Brainstem, Sensory, Bowel/Bladder, Visual, Cerebral, Other
inputs.options_text: Each FS graded 0–5 or 0–6 depending on system

inputs.label: Ambulation
inputs.options_text: EDSS 0–3: based on functional systems; 4.0–9.5: primarily based on ambulation milestones (unilateral/bilateral assistive device, wheelchair, bed-bound)

bands.meaning: Normal neurological exam
Fully ambulatory with mild-moderate disability
Limited walking distance without aid
Requires cane/crutch to walk
Wheelchair-bound
Bed-bound

citations.text: Kurtzke JF. Rating neurologic impairment in multiple sclerosis: an expanded disability status scale (EDSS). Neurology. 1983;33(11):1444-1452. PMID: 6685237

entries.limitations: Non-linear (the difference between EDSS 4 and 6 is not the same as between 0 and 2). Relies heavily on walking in the middle ranges (6.0–7.0). Subject to inter-rater variability. Relatively insensitive to upper extremity/cognitive changes. Not ordinal in a statistical sense. Requires trained neurologist.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America Classification
entries.purpose: Clinical classification of myasthenia gravis severity for treatment planning and research.
entries.formula_human:
Class I: Ocular muscle weakness only
Class II: Mild weakness (IIa: predominantly limb/axial; IIb: predominantly oropharyngeal/respiratory)
Class III: Moderate weakness (IIIa/IIIb same distinction)
Class IV: Severe weakness (IVa/IVb)
Class V: Intubation needed for respiratory failure

inputs.label: Disease class
inputs.description: Distribution and severity of muscle weakness
inputs.options_text: Class I through V (with subclass a/b)

bands.meaning: Ocular MG only
Generalized MG, mild to moderate
Severe generalized MG
Myasthenic crisis requiring intubation

citations.text: Jaretzki A 3rd, Barohn RJ, Ernstoff RM, et al. Myasthenia gravis: recommendations for research standards from the Myasthenia Foundation of America. Neurology. 2000;55(1):16-23. PMID: 10891902

entries.limitations: Classification only (not a continuous score). Subjective assessment. Does not capture quality of life. Single time-point assessment (does not capture fluctuation). The 'a' vs 'b' subclass may be difficult to assign when weakness is mixed.

entries.name: Hoehn and Yahr Scale
entries.purpose: Describes the progression of Parkinson's disease symptoms in 5 stages from unilateral involvement to severe disability.
entries.formula_human:
Staging classification:
0 = No signs of disease
1 = Unilateral involvement only
1.5 = Unilateral and axial involvement
2 = Bilateral involvement without impairment of balance
2.5 = Bilateral involvement with recovery on pull test
3 = Bilateral involvement; mild postural instability; physically independent
4 = Severe disability; still able to walk or stand unassisted
5 = Wheelchair-bound or bedridden unless aided

inputs.label: Clinical stage
inputs.description: Overall level of PD disability based on motor symptoms, balance, and functional independence
inputs.options_text: Stage 0–5 (with 1.5 and 2.5 as intermediate stages in Modified H&Y)

bands.meaning: Early-stage PD. Independent with activities.
Moderate PD. Balance impairment beginning.
Advanced PD. Significant disability.

citations.text: Hoehn MM, Yahr MD. Parkinsonism: onset, progression, and mortality. Neurology. 1967;17(5):427-442. PMID: 6067254

entries.limitations: Crude (only 5–7 levels). Does not capture specific symptoms (tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia individually). Does not capture non-motor symptoms (cognition, mood, autonomic). Middle stages (2–3) capture a wide range of disability. Subjective staging.

entries.name: Field Assessment Stroke Triage for Emergency Destination
entries.purpose: Prehospital screening tool derived from NIHSS to detect large vessel occlusion strokes for direct transport to thrombectomy-capable centers.
entries.formula_human: FAST-ED = Face(0–2) + Arm(0–4) + Speech(0–3) + Eye(0–2) + Denial(0–2)

inputs.label: Arm weakness
inputs.options_text: 0 = normal; 1 = drift; 2 = some effort; 3 = no effort; 4 = no movement

inputs.label: Speech changes
inputs.options_text: 0 = normal; 1 = mild aphasia; 2 = severe aphasia; 3 = mute/global

inputs.label: Eye deviation
inputs.options_text: 0 = normal; 1 = partial gaze palsy; 2 = forced deviation

bands.meaning: Low probability of LVO. Transport to nearest stroke-capable facility.
High probability of LVO. Bypass nearest hospital for comprehensive stroke center.

citations.text: Lima FO, Silva GS, Furie KL, et al. Field assessment stroke triage for emergency destination: a simple and accurate prehospital scale to detect large vessel occlusion strokes. Stroke. 2016;47(8):1997-2002. PMID: 27406107

entries.limitations: Derived from NIHSS (requires accurate prehospital neurological assessment). Training requirements. Sensitivity varies by LVO location. Multi-center validation still limited.

entries.name: Rapid Arterial oCclusion Evaluation Scale
entries.purpose: Prehospital scale to detect large vessel occlusion (LVO) acute stroke for direct transport to comprehensive stroke centers.
entries.formula_human: RACE = Face(0–2) + Arm(0–3) + Leg(0–3) + Head_eyes(0–1) + Aphasia_neglect(0–1) + LOC(0–1)

inputs.label: Arm motor function
inputs.options_text: 0 = normal; 1 = mild-moderate weakness; 2 = severe weakness (drift/fall); 3 = no movement

inputs.label: Leg motor function
inputs.options_text: 0 = normal; 1 = mild-moderate weakness; 2 = severe weakness; 3 = no movement

inputs.label: Head/eye deviation
inputs.description: Gaze deviation or forced head/eye turning

inputs.label: Aphasia/Neglect
inputs.options_text: 0 = absent; 1 = present (only test one side depending on clinical suspicion)

inputs.label: Level of consciousness (commands)
inputs.description: GCS motor response or ability to follow commands

bands.meaning: Low probability of LVO. Transport to nearest stroke center.
High probability of LVO. Transport directly to comprehensive stroke center with thrombectomy capability.

citations.text: Perez de la Ossa N, Carrera D, Gorchs M, et al. Design and validation of a prehospital stroke scale to predict large arterial occlusion: the rapid arterial occlusion evaluation scale. Stroke. 2014;45(1):87-91. PMID: 24253543

entries.limitations: Requires training for reliable prehospital use. Aphasia vs neglect testing in prehospital field is challenging. Leg strength difficult to assess in obtunded patients. Score threshold varies by study (some use ≥5, others ≥4).

entries.name: Fisher Grading Scale for SAH
entries.purpose: CT-based grading of subarachnoid hemorrhage to predict risk of symptomatic vasospasm after aneurysmal SAH.
entries.formula_human:
Fisher Grade (original):
1 = No subarachnoid blood detected
2 = Diffuse or thin (<1mm) vertical layers of SAH
3 = Localized thick clots and/or vertical layers ≥1mm thick
4 = Intracerebral or intraventricular clot with diffuse or no SAH

Modified Fisher Scale (Frontera 2006):
0 = No SAH or IVH
1 = Thin SAH, no IVH
2 = Thin SAH with IVH
3 = Thick SAH, no IVH
4 = Thick SAH with IVH

inputs.label: SAH pattern on CT
inputs.description: Amount and distribution of subarachnoid blood on non-contrast CT head
inputs.options_text: Grade 1: No SAH or IVH visible; Grade 2: Diffuse or thin (<1mm) SAH, no clots; Grade 3: Localized thick clots (≥1mm) or vertical layer ≥1mm; Grade 4: Diffuse or no SAH, but with intracerebral or ventricular clots

bands.meaning: Highest risk of symptomatic vasospasm (~30–70% of cases in older studies). Prophylactic nimodipine and monitoring for vasospasm essential.
Lower vasospasm risk (~10–20%).

citations.text: Fisher CM, Kistler JP, Davis JM. Relation of cerebral vasospasm to subarachnoid hemorrhage visualized by computerized tomographic scanning. Neurosurgery. 1980;6(1):1-6. PMID: 7354892; Modified Fisher: Frontera JA, et al. Stroke. 2006;37:1389-1396

entries.limitations: Subjective (inter-rater variability in clot thickness measurement). Original Fisher scale does not account for IVH as a separate category (addressed in Modified Fisher). CT timing matters (very early or late scans may misgrade). Does not capture intracerebral hemorrhage well in original version.

entries.name: Hunt and Hess Grading Scale
entries.purpose: Clinical grading of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage severity to predict surgical risk and prognosis.
entries.formula_human:
Grade I: Asymptomatic or mild headache, slight nuchal rigidity
Grade II: Moderate-severe headache, nuchal rigidity, no neurological deficit except cranial nerve palsy
Grade III: Drowsiness, confusion, mild focal deficit
Grade IV: Stupor, moderate-severe hemiparesis, possible early decerebrate rigidity
Grade V: Deep coma, decerebrate rigidity, moribund appearance

inputs.label: Clinical grade
inputs.options_text: Grade I–V based on clinical findings

bands.meaning: Operative mortality ~0–2%.
Operative mortality ~2–10%.
Operative mortality ~15–20%.
Operative mortality ~40–60%.
Operative mortality ~70–100%.

citations.text: Hunt WE, Hess RM. Surgical risk as related to time of intervention in the repair of intracranial aneurysms. J Neurosurg. 1968;28(1):14-20. PMID: 5635959

entries.limitations: Subjective (significant inter-rater variability, especially between Grade II and III). Predates modern neurocritical care (mortality estimates may be outdated). Does not capture CT findings (use Fisher scale). Grade V patients may have improved outcomes with modern treatment.

entries.name: Rotterdam CT Score for SAH
entries.purpose: CT-based grading system for aneurysmal SAH predicting 6-month outcome, improving on the Fisher scale.
entries.formula_human:
Rotterdam = SAH(0–2) + IVH(0/1) + ICH(0/1) + Hydrocephalus(0/1) + 1
Note: Scale adds 1 to the sum so the minimum score is 1

inputs.label: SAH amount
inputs.description: Amount of subarachnoid blood on CT

bands.meaning: Best prognosis. Low risk of poor outcome.
Good prognosis.
Moderate prognosis.
Poor prognosis.
Very poor prognosis. High likelihood of unfavorable 6-month outcome.

citations.text: Vergouwen MD, Vermeulen M, van Gijn J, et al. Definition of delayed cerebral ischemia after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage as an outcome event in clinical trials and observational studies: proposal of a multidisciplinary research group. Stroke. 2010;41:2391-2395 (Rotterdam CT Score referenced);

entries.limitations: CT timing relative to ictus may affect grading (early scan may underestimate blood). Does not capture aneurysm location or treatment. Predicts overall outcome, not vasospasm specifically (original Fisher did that). Inter-rater reliability is acceptable but not perfect.

entries.name: CRASH Prognostic Model for TBI
entries.purpose: Predicts 14-day mortality and 6-month unfavorable outcome in adults with traumatic brain injury using simple admission variables.
entries.formula_human:
Cox proportional hazards model: 14-day risk = 1 − baseline_survival^exp(LP). LP = β₀ + Σβᵢxᵢ.
Two models: Basic (country income, age, GCS, pupils, major extracranial injury) and CT model (adds CT findings). Coefficients published in CRASH-CT Collaborators. Calculator: crash2.lshtm.ac.uk/Risk%20calculator/

inputs.label: Pupillary reactivity
inputs.options_text: Both reacting / One reacting / Neither reacting

inputs.label: CT findings
inputs.description: CT abnormalities: petechial hemorrhages, contusion, traumatic SAH, midline shift, none/evacuated mass, non-evacuated mass

bands.meaning: Provides probability estimates to support clinical decision-making and goals-of-care discussions. Designed for use in low- and middle-income countries as well as high-income settings.

citations.text: MRC CRASH Trial Collaborators. Predicting outcome after traumatic brain injury: practical prognostic models based on large cohort of international patients. BMJ. 2008;336(7641):425-429. PMID: 18270239

entries.limitations: No UK/US hospitals in derivation cohort (mainly LMICs). CT model requires availability of CT (not always accessible in LMIC). Country income may serve as proxy for treatment quality. Does not capture hypoxia, hypotension, glucose, or biomarkers. 14-day mortality may not capture all TBI deaths.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app — calculator at crash2.lshtm.ac.uk

entries.name: IMPACT Prognostic Model for TBI
entries.purpose: Predicts 6-month outcome (Glasgow Outcome Scale) after moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury for individual patient prognostication.
entries.formula_human:
Logistic regression: P(outcome) = 1/(1 + exp(−LP)) where LP = β₀ + Σβᵢxᵢ.
Three models: Core (age + motor GCS + pupils), Extended Core (adds CT, hypoxia, hypotension), Extended (adds glucose, Hb, EDH, tSAH). Coefficients published in MRC CRASH Trial Investigators and Steyerberg EW, et al. 2008. Online calculator: impactcalc.org

inputs.label: Pupillary reactivity
inputs.options_text: Both reacting / One reacting / Neither reacting

inputs.label: CT characteristics
inputs.description: Marshall CT classification or Traumatic Coma Data Bank CT class
inputs.options_text: Diffuse injury I–IV, Evacuated mass, Non-evacuated mass

bands.meaning: Use predicted probabilities to guide goals-of-care, stratify clinical trials, and support shared decision-making with families. E.g., >90% predicted mortality → poor prognosis.

citations.text: Steyerberg EW, Mushkudiani N, Perel P, et al. Predicting outcome after traumatic brain injury: development and international validation of prognostic scores based on admission characteristics. PLoS Med. 2008;5(8):e165. PMID: 18684008

entries.limitations: Requires CT and laboratory data. Model predictions should be used as decision support, not sole decision criterion. External validity depends on treatment context. Does not capture penetrating TBI well. Intubation/sedation confounds GCS assessment. Supplemented by biomarkers (UCH-L1, GFAP) in newer models.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app — calculator at impactcalc.org

entries.name: Glasgow Prognostic Score / Modified Glasgow Prognostic Score
entries.purpose: Simple inflammation-based prognostic score for cancer patients using CRP and albumin, independent of tumor type.
entries.formula_human:
Modified GPS (mGPS):
Score 0: CRP ≤10 mg/L (regardless of albumin)
Score 1: CRP >10 mg/L and albumin ≥35 g/L
Score 2: CRP >10 mg/L and albumin <35 g/L

Note: mGPS differs from original GPS in that low albumin alone (with normal CRP) = score 0.

bands.meaning: Low systemic inflammation. Best prognosis across cancer types.
Intermediate prognosis. Elevated CRP without hypoalbuminemia.
Worst prognosis. Systemic inflammation with nutritional compromise.

citations.text: Forrest LM, McMillan DC, McArdle CS, et al. Evaluation of cumulative prognostic scores based on the systemic inflammatory response in patients with inoperable non-small-cell lung cancer. Br J Cancer. 2003;89:1028-1030. PMID: 12966417; original GPS: McMillan DC, et al. Br J Cancer. 2001;85:1051-1057

entries.limitations: Affected by non-cancer causes of inflammation (infection, autoimmune disease). CRP and albumin cutoffs may need adjustment for different assays and populations. Does not capture tumor-specific factors (stage, molecular profile). Two laboratory values only — simplistic. Albumin may be low for non-inflammatory reasons (liver disease, nephrotic syndrome).

entries.name: Gleason Grading System / Grade Group
entries.purpose: Histological grading of prostate cancer based on glandular architecture patterns to predict prognosis and guide treatment.
entries.formula_human:
Gleason Score = Primary pattern + Secondary pattern (e.g., 3+4=7 or 4+3=7)

ISUP Grade Groups (2014 WHO):
Grade Group 1: Gleason score ≤6 (3+3)
Grade Group 2: Gleason score 3+4=7
Grade Group 3: Gleason score 4+3=7
Grade Group 4: Gleason score 8 (4+4, 3+5, 5+3)
Grade Group 5: Gleason score 9–10 (4+5, 5+4, 5+5)

inputs.label: Primary pattern
inputs.description: Most prevalent Gleason pattern in the biopsy/prostatectomy specimen

bands.meaning: Low-grade cancer. Favorable prognosis. Active surveillance appropriate for many patients.
Intermediate (favorable). Treatment depends on other risk factors.
Intermediate (unfavorable). Treatment recommended.
High-grade. Aggressive treatment recommended.
Very high-grade. Poor prognosis. Multimodal therapy.

citations.text: Gleason DF, Mellinger GT. Prediction of prognosis for prostatic adenocarcinoma by combined histological grading and clinical staging. J Urol. 1974;111(1):58-64. PMID: 4813554; ISUP 2014: Epstein JI, et al. Am J Surg Pathol. 2016;40:244-252

entries.limitations: Inter-pathologist variability (especially patterns 3 vs 4, and 4 vs 5). Biopsy grading may underestimate final prostatectomy grade (upgrading in 30–40%). Pattern 5 percentage is increasingly recognized as important. Does not capture molecular markers (PTEN loss, TMPRSS2-ERG). Biopsy core involvement percentage and number of positive cores not captured by Gleason alone.

entries.name: Khorana Score for Cancer-Associated VTE
entries.purpose: Predicts risk of venous thromboembolism in ambulatory cancer patients receiving chemotherapy to guide thromboprophylaxis decisions.
entries.formula_human: Khorana = Very_high_risk_cancer(2) + High_risk_cancer(1) + Platelets≥350(1) + Hb<10_or_ESA(1) + WBC>11(1) + BMI≥35(1)

inputs.label: Cancer site (high risk)
inputs.description: Lung, lymphoma, gynecologic, genitourinary (excluding prostate), or testicular cancer

inputs.label: Hemoglobin <10 g/dL or use of erythropoiesis-stimulating agents

bands.meaning: Low VTE risk (~0.3–0.8% over 6 months). Thromboprophylaxis generally not recommended.
Intermediate risk (~2–7%). Consider thromboprophylaxis based on individual factors.
High risk (~6.7–11%+). Thromboprophylaxis recommended (LMWH or DOAC per CASSINI/SELECT-D trials).

citations.text: Khorana AA, Kuderer NM, Culakova E, et al. Development and validation of a predictive model for chemotherapy-associated venous thromboembolism. J Clin Oncol. 2008;26(11):1904-1908. PMID: 18180983

entries.limitations: Low c-statistic (~0.65–0.7) — modest discrimination. Score ≥3 identifies ~10% of patients as high risk but sensitivity is low (~40%). Cancer site classification may be oversimplified. Not validated for all cancer types. BMI ≥35 cutoff excludes many obese patients. Performance may vary by tumor type and treatment regimen.

entries.name: Modified DKA Severity Index
entries.purpose: Classifies DKA severity based on serum bicarbonate, pH, mental status, and anion gap per ADA consensus guidelines.
entries.formula_human:
Classification system (not numerical score):

Mild DKA: HCO₃⁻ 15–18 mEq/L, pH 7.25–7.30, alert
Moderate DKA: HCO₃⁻ 10–14.9 mEq/L, pH 7.00–7.24, alert or drowsy
Severe DKA: HCO₃⁻ <10 mEq/L, pH <7.00, stupor or coma

Anion gap should be elevated (>12 mEq/L) to confirm DKA

inputs.label: Mental status
inputs.options_text: Alert = mild; Alert/drowsy = moderate; Stupor/coma = severe

bands.meaning: Subcutaneous insulin protocol may be appropriate. ED observation or short stay.
IV insulin, fluid resuscitation, electrolyte monitoring. Ward or HDU admission.
ICU admission. Continuous IV insulin, aggressive fluid resuscitation, frequent electrolyte monitoring. High mortality risk if untreated.

citations.text: Kitabchi AE, Umpierrez GE, Miles JM, Fisher JN. Hyperglycemic crises in adult patients with diabetes. Diabetes Care. 2009;32(7):1335-1343. PMID: 19564476; updated: Umpierrez GE, et al. Diabetes Care. 2022;45:2885-2914

entries.limitations: Severity classification is somewhat subjective (mental status component). Bicarbonate and pH may be discordant (venous vs arterial). Anion gap may be normal in hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis (post-resuscitation). DKA with euglycemia (glucose <250 mg/dL) is a distinct entity not captured well. Concurrent illness (sepsis, MI) complicates management. Classification doesn't directly predict specific outcomes (mortality, ICU length of stay).
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published academic guideline

entries.name: IMPROVE VTE Risk Assessment Model
entries.purpose: Predicts VTE risk in hospitalized medically ill patients using clinical variables; can incorporate D-dimer for enhanced discrimination.
entries.formula_human:
IMPROVE VTE = Previous_VTE(3) + Thrombophilia(2) + Paralysis(2) + Active_cancer(2) + Immobilized(1) + ICU(1) + Age>60(1) + Heart_failure(1) + Respiratory_failure(1) + Prophylaxis(−1)

Enhanced model adds D-dimer ≥2× ULN (+2 points)

VTE risk at 40 days: if clinical score ≥2, baseline risk ~2.7%; if D-dimer ≥2× ULN, risk ~4.9%

bands.meaning: Low VTE risk (<0.4% at 40 days). Extended prophylaxis not needed.
Moderate risk (~1.5%). Consider in-hospital prophylaxis.
High risk (~4.9%). Extended thromboprophylaxis (post-discharge) may be beneficial.

citations.text: Spyropoulos AC, Anderson FA Jr, FitzGerald G, et al. Predictive and associative models to identify hospitalized medical patients at risk for VTE. J Thromb Haemost. 2011;9:1123-1131. PMID: 21481172

entries.limitations: D-dimer timing relative to admission affects results. D-dimer is non-specific (elevated in many medical conditions). Score ≥2 includes many patients (low specificity). Extended prophylaxis benefit debated. Not validated in surgical patients. IMPROVE-bleed score used separately for bleeding risk.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: Padua Prediction Score
entries.purpose: Predicts risk of VTE in hospitalized medical patients to guide thromboprophylaxis decisions.
entries.formula_human: Padua = Active_cancer(3) + Previous_VTE(3) + Reduced_mobility(3) + Thrombophilia(3) + Recent_trauma(2) + Age≥70(1) + Heart/respiratory_failure(1) + MI/stroke(2) + Infection/rheum(1) + Obesity(1) + Hormones(1)

inputs.label: Active cancer
inputs.description: Active malignancy within 6 months or ongoing treatment

inputs.label: Reduced mobility
inputs.description: Bed rest with bathroom privileges for ≥3 days

inputs.label: Recent trauma/surgery (≤1 month)
inputs.description: Trauma or surgery within the past month

inputs.label: Heart/respiratory failure
inputs.description: Congestive heart failure and/or respiratory failure

inputs.label: Acute MI/ischemic stroke
inputs.description: Acute MI or ischemic stroke (including lower extremity paralysis)

inputs.label: Ongoing hormonal treatment
inputs.description: Hormone replacement therapy or oral contraceptives

bands.meaning: Low VTE risk (~0.3%). Pharmacological thromboprophylaxis generally not recommended.
High VTE risk (~2.2% in original study). Pharmacological thromboprophylaxis recommended.

citations.text: Barbar S, Noventa F, Rossetto V, et al. A risk assessment model for the identification of hospitalized medical patients at risk for venous thromboembolism: the Padua Prediction Score. J Thromb Haemost. 2010;8(11):2450-2457. PMID: 20738765

entries.limitations: Low specificity (many high-score patients will not develop VTE). Does not capture admission diagnosis. Reduced mobility definition is subjective. Not validated in surgical patients. IMPROVE VTE score is an alternative (incorporates D-dimer). Cutoff ≥4 may result in over-prophylaxis in many centers.

entries.name: Age-Related Eye Disease Study Severity Scale
entries.purpose: Classifies AMD severity to predict 5-year risk of progression to advanced AMD and guide AREDS supplement use.
entries.formula_human:
Severity scale (11-step based on fundus photographs):
Step 1: No drusen or small drusen only in both eyes
Step 2–3: Intermediate drusen without pigment abnormalities
Step 4–5: Intermediate/large drusen with pigment changes
Step 6–8: Large drusen, confluent drusen, extensive pigment changes
Step 9: Geographic atrophy not involving center
Step 10: Geographic atrophy involving center
Step 11: Neovascular AMD

Simplified for clinical use: AREDS Category 1–4
Category 1: No AMD (no drusen or small drusen only)
Category 2: Early AMD (small/intermediate drusen, pigment changes)
Category 3: Intermediate AMD (≥1 large drusen, extensive intermediate drusen, GA not involving center)
Category 4: Advanced AMD (GA involving center, or neovascular AMD in at least one eye)

inputs.label: Drusen size and type
inputs.description: Size (small, medium, large) and character (hard, soft, confluent, calcified) of drusen in each eye
inputs.options_text: No drusen, small drusen (<63 µm), intermediate drusen (63–124 µm), large drusen (≥125 µm)

bands.meaning: ~0.5% 5-year risk of advanced AMD. AREDS supplements not indicated.
~3% 5-year risk. AREDS supplements may be considered.
~12% 5-year risk. AREDS supplements recommended (vitamin C 500mg, vitamin E 400IU, zinc 80mg, copper 2mg, ± lutein 10mg, zeaxanthin 2mg — AREDS2 formulation).
~43% 5-year risk for fellow eye. AREDS supplements strongly recommended.

citations.text: Age-Related Eye Disease Study Research Group. The Age-Related Eye Disease Study severity scale for age-related macular degeneration. Arch Ophthalmol. 2005;123(11):1484-1498. PMID: 16286604; AREDS Research Group. Arch Ophthalmol. 2001;119:1417-1436

entries.limitations: Requires detailed fundus photography for accurate grading. Clinical assessment without photography may miss subtle drusen or pigment changes. Risk estimates are from a clinical trial population (selected patients). Does not capture genetic risk factors (CFH, ARMS2). Diet, smoking, and cardiovascular disease not incorporated into stage. AREDS supplements do not prevent AMD onset — only slow progression in intermediate/advanced stages.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published academic guideline

entries.name: Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study Severity Scale
entries.purpose: Standardized severity grading of diabetic retinopathy for research and clinical management.
entries.formula_human:
12-step classification system based on 7-field stereo fundus photography:
Level 10: No retinopathy (DR absent)
Level 20: Microaneurysms only (very mild NPDR)
Level 35: Mild NPDR
Level 43: Moderate NPDR
Level 47: Moderately severe NPDR
Level 53: Severe NPDR (4-2-1 rule)
Level 60: PDR — no high-risk characteristics
Level 61–85: PDR — with high-risk characteristics

4-2-1 rule: hemorrhages in 4 quadrants, venous beading in 2 quadrants, IRMA in 1 quadrant

Simplified clinical classification:
NPDR: Mild, Moderate, Severe (no neovascularization)
PDR: Neovascularization present ± vitreous hemorrhage

inputs.label: Retinal findings on fundus photography/ophthalmoscopy
inputs.description: Presence and extent of microaneurysms, hemorrhages, hard exudates, cotton-wool spots, IRMA, venous beading, neovascularization

bands.meaning: Annual screening. No treatment needed.
Annual follow-up. Optimize glucose, BP, lipids.
Follow-up every 6–9 months. Closer monitoring.
High risk of progression to PDR. 4-2-1 rule. Consider PRP laser.
Pan-retinal photocoagulation or anti-VEGF injection recommended. High-risk PDR (NV disc or NV iris) = emergent treatment.

citations.text: Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study Research Group. Grading diabetic retinopathy from stereoscopic color fundus photographs — an extension of the modified Airlie House classification. ETDRS Report Number 10. Ophthalmology. 1991;98(5 Suppl):786-806. PMID: 2062513

entries.limitations: Full ETDRS grading requires 7-field stereo fundus photography (complex, not routine). Simplified clinical grading (ICDR) is more practical but less precise. Does not capture diabetic macular edema (DME) separately. Grading requires experienced ophthalmologist/photographer. Automated AI-based DR detection is being validated.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published academic system

entries.name: Hodapp-Parrish-Anderson Glaucoma Staging System
entries.purpose: Classifies glaucoma severity by combining visual field indices and optic disc appearance for treatment and monitoring guidance.
entries.formula_human:
Staging system combining VF and disc parameters:

Early (Stage 1): MD ≥−6 dB, PSD <5 dB, C/D <0.6
Moderate (Stage 2): MD −6.01 to −12 dB, PSD ≥5 dB, C/D 0.6–0.9
Severe (Stage 3): MD <−12 dB, PSD variable, C/D ≥0.9

Additional criteria based on number of points in the pattern deviation plot with p<0.05 and p<0.01.

inputs.label: Mean deviation (MD)
inputs.description: Mean deviation on automated perimetry (Humphrey Visual Field)

inputs.label: Pattern standard deviation (PSD)
inputs.description: Pattern standard deviation on visual field

bands.meaning: Mild visual field loss. Intraocular pressure (IOP) target: 20% reduction from baseline.
Moderate VF loss. IOP target: 30% reduction.
Advanced VF loss. IOP target: lower the better (often <15 mmHg). Consider surgical intervention.

citations.text: Hodapp E, Parrish RK II, Anderson DR. Clinical Decisions in Glaucoma. St. Louis: Mosby; 1993. (Book publication — no PMID)

entries.limitations: Visual field testing has inherent variability (learning effect, fatigue, artifacts). Does not capture rate of progression (single time-point only). Disc appearance is subjective. Staging does not directly guide specific treatment (medical, laser, surgical). Different systems exist (GSS, AGIS, etc.) with slightly different criteria. Does not capture corneal thickness or diurnal IOP fluctuation.

entries.name: Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Score
entries.purpose: Composite index combining patient-reported outcomes with CRP or ESR to objectively assess disease activity in axial spondyloarthritis. Developed by ASAS (Assessment of SpondyloArthritis International Society) to overcome BASDAI's limitation of lacking acute phase reactants.
entries.formula_human:
ASDAS-CRP = 0.121 × back pain + 0.058 × duration of morning stiffness + 0.110 × patient global + 0.073 × peripheral pain/swelling + 0.579 × ln(CRP+1)

ASDAS-ESR = 0.113 × back pain + 0.086 × duration of morning stiffness + 0.069 × patient global + 0.051 × peripheral pain/swelling + 0.075 × ESR

CRP used: mg/L (raw, not log-transformed before formula)

inputs.label: Back pain (VAS)
inputs.description: Total back pain in last week (0–10 cm)

inputs.label: Peripheral pain/swelling (VAS)
inputs.description: Duration of morning stiffness (0–10 cm) — alternative: peripheral joint pain/swelling

inputs.label: Patient global (VAS)
inputs.description: Patient global assessment of disease activity (0–10 cm)

inputs.label: CRP (mg/L)
inputs.description: C-reactive protein (two versions: ASDAS-CRP or ASDAS-ESR)

bands.meaning: Inactive disease (remission)
Moderate disease activity
High disease activity
Very high disease activity
Clinically important improvement
Change in disease activity state

citations.text: Lukas C, Landewé R, Sieper J, et al. Development of an ASAS-endorsed disease activity score (ASDAS) in patients with ankylosing spondylitis. Ann Rheum Dis. 2009;68(1):18-24. PMID: 18625618; van der Heijde D, et al. Ann Rheum Dis. 2009;68:1811-1818

entries.limitations: Requires CRP or ESR — not purely clinical. CRP may be normal in up to 40% of axSpA patients with active disease. Formula is complex for bedside calculation (calculator or app recommended). ASDAS-CRP and ASDAS-ESR give slightly different results — not interchangeable. Does not capture peripheral spondyloarthritis features well. May not reflect MRI findings (sacroiliitis on MRI may be active despite low ASDAS).
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — ASAS (Assessment of SpondyloArthritis International Society)

entries.name: 2012 ACR Preliminary Diagnostic Criteria for Fibromyalgia
entries.purpose: Simplified criteria for fibromyalgia diagnosis replacing 1990 ACR criteria. Eliminates tender point examination, incorporates Widespread Pain Index (WPI) and Symptom Severity Scale (SSS).
entries.formula_human:
A patient satisfies diagnostic criteria for fibromyalgia if ALL three conditions met:
1. WPI ≥7 AND SSS ≥5 OR WPI 3–6 AND SSS ≥9
2. Symptoms present at similar level for ≥3 months
3. Patient does not have another disorder that would sufficiently explain the pain

Alternative (physician-based): Modified 2010 criteria = WPI + SSS ≥13 (original ACR 2010)

inputs.label: Widespread Pain Index (WPI)
inputs.description: Count of 19 body areas where patient has had pain in the past week (shoulder girdle, hip, jaw, upper arm, lower arm, upper leg, lower leg, upper back, lower back, abdomen, neck, chest — all bilateral)

inputs.label: Symptom Severity Scale (SSS)
inputs.description: Sum of: (a) Fatigue, (b) Waking unrefreshed, (c) Cognitive symptoms (each scored 0–3: 0=no problem, 1=mild/intermittent, 2=moderate/considerable, 3=severe/continuous/continuous) + (d) Somatic symptoms (0–3: 0=no symptoms, 1=few, 2=moderate, 3=great deal)

bands.meaning: Meets fibromyalgia criteria (if symptoms ≥3 months and no other explanation)
Meets fibromyalgia criteria (if symptoms ≥3 months and no other explanation)
Does not meet criteria

citations.text: Wolfe F, Clauw DJ, Fitzcharles MA, et al. The American College of Rheumatology preliminary diagnostic criteria for fibromyalgia and measurement of symptom severity. Arthritis Care Res. 2010;62(5):600-610. PMID: 20461783; Wolfe F, et al. Semin Arthritis Rheum. 2013 (2012 modification)

entries.limitations: Fibromyalgia remains a clinical diagnosis of exclusion. Criteria capture symptom burden, not disease mechanism. Self-reported WPI and SSS subject to recall bias. Significant overlap with other chronic pain conditions, depression, and anxiety. Somatic symptoms (SSS item d) criticized as vague and unreliable. Criteria not designed for self-diagnosis. Some patients with classic fibromyalgia features may not meet threshold. High false-positive rate in some validation studies. 'Another disorder that would sufficiently explain the pain' is subjective.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — ACR publication

entries.name: 2015 ACR/EULAR Gout Classification Criteria
entries.purpose: Classification criteria for gout using a scoring system with entry criterion, sufficient criterion, and additive domains. First classification criteria to use a points-based system for gout.
entries.formula_human:
If MSU crystals present → Gout (sufficient criterion)
Otherwise: Clinical + Laboratory + Imaging domain scores
≥8 points out of available 22 → Classifies as gout

Domain 1 (Pattern): MTP1 involvement alone=+2
Domain 2 (Characteristics): 1 feature=+1, ≥2 features=+2
Domain 3 (Time course): ≥2 typical episodes=+2 (if criteria met)
Domain 4 (Tophus): Present=+4
Domain 5 (Serum urate): <4=-2, 4-<6=0, 6-<8=+2, 8-<10=+3, ≥10=+4 (subtract 2 if on ULLT)
Domain 6 (Imaging): DECT/US urate deposition=+4, X-ray erosions=+4

inputs.label: Entry criterion
inputs.description: At least one episode of swelling, pain, or tenderness in a peripheral joint or bursa (required to proceed)

inputs.label: Sufficient criterion
inputs.description: Presence of monosodium urate (MSU) crystals in symptomatic joint/bursa or tophus → automatically classifies as gout

inputs.label: Clinical domains
inputs.description: Domain 1: Pattern of joint involvement (monoarticular ankle/MTP1=+2, polyarticular symmetric=0, other=0); Domain 2: Characteristics of episode (erythema, rapid onset (<24h), severe pain, difficulty walking, resolution in 14 days — 1 feature=+1, ≥2 features=+2); Domain 3: Time course (recurrent typical episodes=+1, episodes complete resolution between attacks=+1); Domain 4: Tophus present=+4; Domain 5: Serum urate (<4 mg/dL=-2, 4–<6=0, 6–<8=+2, 8–<10=+3, ≥10=+4); Domain 6: Urate lowering therapy (-2 if on ULLT); Domain 7: Imaging (urate deposition on DECT or US double contour sign=+4; Erosions on X-ray=+4)

bands.meaning: Definite gout (gold standard)
Classified as gout
Does not meet classification criteria

citations.text: Neogi T, Jansen TL, Dalbeth N, et al. 2015 Gout Classification Criteria: an American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism collaborative initiative. Ann Rheum Dis. 2015;74(10):1789-1798. PMID: 26314789

entries.limitations: Classification criteria, not diagnostic — designed for research. MSU aspiration (gold standard) required for definitive classification — many patients won't have synovial fluid analysis. Serum urate may be normal during acute gout attack (≤40%). Imaging (DECT, US double contour) not widely available. Serum urate measurement timing relative to attack variable. Doesn't capture triggers, comorbidities, or treatment response.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — ACR/EULAR joint publication

entries.name: CASPAR Classification Criteria for Psoriatic Arthritis
entries.purpose: Classification criteria for psoriatic arthritis developed by the ClASsification for Psoriatic ARthritis study group. Used in research to define PsA populations.
entries.formula_human:
To classify as PsA: Inflammatory articular disease (required) + ≥3 points from remaining criteria
Current psoriasis (2 points) OR personal history (1) OR family history (1)
Dactylitis (1) + Nail changes (1) + RF negative (1) + Juxta-articular new bone (1)

inputs.label: Inflammatory articular disease
inputs.description: Current inflammatory joint disease (peripheral arthritis, spondylitis, or enthesitis). Required entry criterion.

inputs.label: Psoriasis (current)
inputs.description: Current psoriatic skin or scalp disease diagnosed by rheumatologist or dermatologist

inputs.label: Psoriasis (personal history)
inputs.description: History of psoriasis (if current psoriasis not present)

inputs.label: Family history of psoriasis
inputs.description: First- or second-degree relative with psoriasis

inputs.label: Dactylitis
inputs.description: Current or history of dactylitis (sausage digit), diagnosed by rheumatologist

inputs.label: Juxta-articular new bone formation
inputs.description: X-ray evidence of new bone formation near joints (excluding osteophytes)

inputs.label: Rheumatoid factor
inputs.description: RF negative by any method (except latex in past 6 months)

inputs.label: Nail changes
inputs.description: Onycholysis, pitting, or hyperkeratosis on examination

bands.meaning: Classified as psoriatic arthritis. Sensitivity 91.4%, specificity 98.7%
Does not meet CASPAR classification criteria

citations.text: Taylor W, Gladman D, Helliwell P, et al. Classification criteria for psoriatic arthritis: development of new criteria from a large international study. Arthritis Rheum. 2006;54(8):2665-2673. PMID: 16871531

entries.limitations: Classification criteria, not diagnostic — research use. Requires rheumatologist assessment (dactylitis, enthesitis). Family history of psoriasis may be unreliable. RF negativity assumed (seronegative RA misclassified?). X-ray changes (juxta-articular new bone formation) may be late finding — early PsA may not show this. Doesn't capture severity or extent of PsA. Enthesitis alone (without peripheral arthritis) doesn't score well.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published academic tool

entries.name: Disease Activity Score 28 joints
entries.purpose: Quantitative measure of disease activity in rheumatoid arthritis based on 28 joint counts, ESR or CRP, and patient global assessment. Guides treatment decisions and defines remission, low, moderate, and high disease activity.

inputs.label: Tender Joint Count (TJC28)
inputs.description: Number of tender joints out of 28 assessed joints (MCP 1–5, PIP 1–5, wrist, elbow, shoulder bilaterally, plus knees)

inputs.label: Swollen Joint Count (SJC28)
inputs.description: Number of swollen joints out of same 28 joints

inputs.label: ESR or CRP
inputs.description: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate (mm/h) or C-reactive protein (mg/L). Two versions: DAS28-ESR and DAS28-CRP

inputs.label: Patient Global Assessment (VAS)
inputs.description: Patient global assessment of disease activity on visual analog scale (0–100 mm)

bands.meaning: Remission
Low disease activity
Moderate disease activity
High disease activity

citations.text: Prevoo ML, van 't Hof MA, Kuper HH, et al. Modified disease activity scores that include twenty-eight-joint counts. Development and validation in a prospective longitudinal study of patients with rheumatoid arthritis. Arthritis Rheum. 1995;38(1):44-48. PMID: 7818570

entries.limitations: 28-joint count excludes feet (MTP, ankle) — may underestimate activity with predominantly lower extremity disease. Patient global VAS introduces subjectivity. ESR influenced by age, sex, anemia. CRP version tends to yield slightly lower scores. Remission defined as DAS28 <2.6 does not always equate to absence of residual disease (Boolean remission by ACR/EULAR preferred). Inability to distinguish synovitis from osteoarthritis in assessed joints.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published academic tool

entries.name: Routine Assessment of Patient Index Data 3
entries.purpose: Simplest composite RA measure — entirely patient-reported, no joint counts, no lab tests, no physician assessment. Designed for rapid point-of-care screening in busy clinics.
entries.formula_human:
RAPID3 = Function (0–10) + Pain (0–10) + Patient Global (0–10)
Total 0–30 (each component 0–10)

inputs.label: Function (MDHAQ)
inputs.description: Multidimensional HAQ physical function (0–10 scale, converted from 0–3 HAQ)

inputs.label: Patient Global Estimate (VAS)
inputs.description: Patient global assessment of status (0–10 cm)

bands.meaning: Near remission
Low severity
Moderate severity
High severity

citations.text: Pincus T, Swearingen CJ, Bergman M, et al. RAPID3 (Routine Assessment of Patient Index Data) on an MDHAQ can be completed in virtually all usual care of patients with rheumatic diseases. J Rheumatol. 2008;35(6):1072-1078. PMID: 18412313

entries.limitations: Entirely patient-reported — cannot distinguish active synovitis from fibromyalgia, depression, or other non-inflammatory causes of pain and disability. No joint count component. Pain and global assessment confounded by non-inflammatory factors. Cut-offs for severity categories not as well-validated as DAS28/CDAI categories. Not recommended as sole basis for major treatment decisions (particularly biologic initiation).
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — Health Assessment Questionnaire, Stanford University

entries.name: ACR/EULAR 2010 Rheumatoid Arthritis Classification Criteria
entries.purpose: Classification criteria for rheumatoid arthritis designed for early identification of patients with RA who would benefit from early DMARD therapy. Replaced 1987 ACR criteria.
entries.formula_human:
Total = Joint involvement (0–5) + Serology (0–3) + Acute phase (0–1) + Duration (0–1)
Score ≥6/10 = definite RA classification
Score <6 = 'undifferentiated' — may evolve to RA

inputs.label: Joint involvement
inputs.description: Number and size of involved joints (tender and/or swollen). Large joints: shoulders, elbows, hips, knees, ankles; Small joints: MCP, PIP (2nd–5th), thumb IP, MTP 2–5, wrists; Distal interphalangeal joints, 1st CMC, 1st MTP excluded
inputs.options_text: 1 large joint=0, 2–10 large joints=1, 1–3 small joints=2, 4–10 small joints=3, >10 joints (at least 1 small)=5

inputs.label: Acute phase reactants
inputs.options_text: Normal CRP and ESR=0, Abnormal CRP or ESR=1

bands.meaning: Classified as definite rheumatoid arthritis (with synovitis in ≥1 joint, no alternative diagnosis)
Does not meet criteria — 'undifferentiated arthritis.' May develop RA over time.

citations.text: Aletaha D, Neogi T, Silman AJ, et al. 2010 Rheumatoid arthritis classification criteria: an American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism collaborative initiative. Arthritis Rheum. 2010;62(9):2569-2581. PMID: 20872595

entries.limitations: Classification criteria, not diagnostic criteria — designed for research to identify homogeneous RA populations. Requires exclusion of alternative diagnoses. Joint involvement assessment requires clinical examination. Serology (RF, ACPA) may take time to result. Duration threshold of 6 weeks is arbitrary. Some RA patients (seronegative with few joints) may not meet threshold. Not validated in established RA — only early arthritis. Specificity in non-rheumatology settings unknown.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published jointly by ACR and EULAR

entries.name: Health Assessment Questionnaire Disability Index
entries.purpose: Patient-reported outcome measure evaluating functional disability in RA and other rheumatic diseases. Captures impact on activities of daily living across 8 domains.
entries.formula_human:
Each domain: highest score among items in that domain (with or without aids/devices)
HAQ-DI = mean of 8 domain scores (range 0–3)
If aids/devices used and score improves with their use, still counted as using aid (automatic ≥1 for that domain in some versions)

inputs.label: Dressing and Grooming
inputs.description: Ability to dress, shampoo hair, etc.

inputs.label: Arising
inputs.description: Ability to get out of bed, stand up from chair

inputs.label: Eating
inputs.description: Ability to cut meat, lift cup, etc.

inputs.label: Walking
inputs.description: Ability to walk outdoors on flat ground

inputs.label: Reach
inputs.description: Ability to reach and retrieve objects

inputs.label: Grip
inputs.description: Ability to open jars, turn faucets

inputs.label: Activities
inputs.description: Ability to run errands, do chores

bands.meaning: No disability
Mild to moderate disability
Moderate to severe disability
Severe to very severe disability
Minimum clinically important difference: 0.22 points

citations.text: Fries JF, Spitz P, Kraines RG, Holman HR. Measurement of patient outcome in arthritis. Arthritis Rheum. 1980;23(2):137-145. PMID: 7362664; Bruce B, Fries JF. Clin Exp Rheumatol. 2005;23(Suppl 39):S14-S18

entries.limitations: Patient-reported — subject to recall bias and subjective interpretation. Ceiling effect in early/mild disease. Floor effect in severe disease (maxed at 3). Does not capture pain, fatigue, or psychological impact directly. Aid/device use scoring debated. Different versions exist (HAQ-II, MHAQ, HAQ-DI with or without aids).
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — Stanford University (used with permission, widely distributed)

entries.name: British Isles Lupus Assessment Group Index 2004
entries.purpose: Organ-specific disease activity index for SLE that grades each system from A (severe activity) to E (never affected). Unlike SLEDAI, captures improvement and worsening within systems. Preferred by some for treatment decision-making.
entries.formula_human:
Each of 8 systems scored independently: A (9), B (3), C (1), D (0), E (0)
Total BILAG-2004 = sum of 8 system scores (0–72)
Scoring based on treatment decision approach:
- A = Severe activity requiring steroids/cytotoxics
- B = Moderate activity requiring steroids/antimalarials/NSAIDs
- C = Mild activity requiring no treatment change
- D = Previously active, improving
- E = System never affected by SLE

inputs.label: General
inputs.description: Constitutional symptoms: fever, weight loss, lymphadenopathy, fatigue

inputs.label: Neurological
inputs.description: CNS lupus: seizures, psychosis, cranial neuropathy, myelitis, etc.

inputs.label: Cardiorespiratory
inputs.description: Serositis, myocarditis, endocarditis, pulmonary hypertension, ILD

inputs.label: Renal
inputs.description: Proteinuria, hematuria, casts, renal function, biopsy class

inputs.label: Vasculitis
inputs.description: Vasculitic lesions, DVT, PE, thrombosis attributed to vasculitis (not APS alone)

inputs.label: Hematology
inputs.description: Thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, hemolytic anemia, PTT prolongation

bands.meaning: Severe activity in that organ — typically requires systemic corticosteroids and/or immunosuppression
Moderate activity — requires treatment increase or close monitoring
Mild or inactive disease — may maintain current therapy
Higher total = more global activity; A=9 scoring means any 'A' system dominates total

citations.text: Isenberg DA, Rahman A, Allen E, et al. BILAG 2004. Development and initial validation of an updated version of the British Isles Lupus Assessment Group's disease activity index for patients with systemic lupus erythematosus. Rheumatology (Oxford). 2005;44(7):902-906. PMID: 15814579

entries.limitations: Complex scoring — requires trained assessor reviewing detailed organ-specific definitions for each of 8 systems. Treatment-based decision approach (A = treat aggressively) may differ between centers. Some organ systems overlap (vasculitis vs. general). D grade (improving) captures response but may not reflect current activity. Training materials available but learning curve is steeper than SLEDAI. No widely agreed-upon numerical cut-offs for remission/flares.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — University College London

entries.name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Disease Activity Index 2000
entries.purpose: Global disease activity index for SLE covering 24 descriptors across 9 organ systems. Updated 2000 version allows persistent activity scoring (SLEDAI-2K). Widely used in clinical trials and practice.
entries.formula_human:
Sum of all descriptor scores for items present in preceding 10 days.
Descriptors scored if present regardless of cause attribution (with specific exclusions noted).
SLEDAI-2K modification: persistent active lesions in rash, alopecia, mucosal ulcers, and proteinuria scored even if present >10 days.

inputs.label: Visual disturbance
inputs.description: Retinal changes or optic neuritis from SLE

inputs.label: Vasculitis
inputs.description: Ulceration, gangrene, painful nodules, periungual infarction, biopsy-proven vasculitis

inputs.label: Urinary casts
inputs.description: Heme, granular, RBC, or tubular casts

inputs.label: Alopecia
inputs.description: Abnormal patchy or diffuse hair loss

inputs.label: Low complement
inputs.description: CH50, C3, or C4 below normal

inputs.label: Increased DNA binding
inputs.description: Anti-dsDNA above normal (>25% by Farr assay or above lab reference)

bands.meaning: No disease activity
Mild activity
Moderate activity
High activity
Very high activity
Definition of DORIS (Definition of Remission in SLE) remission

citations.text: Bombardier C, Gladman DD, Urowitz MB, et al. Derivation of the SLEDAI. Arthritis Rheum. 1992;35(6):630-640. PMID: 1599520; Gladman DD, Ibañez D, Urowitz MB. J Rheumatol. 2002;29:288-291 (SLEDAI-2K)

entries.limitations: Physician-completed — requires clinical assessment of 24 descriptors. Some descriptors (e.g., lupus headache) controversial and may not reflect true SLE activity. 10-day window may miss waxing/waning symptoms (partially addressed by SLEDAI-2K persistent scoring). Does not capture damage or cumulative organ injury (use SLICC/ACR Damage Index — SDI). Laboratory values (complement, dsDNA) need clinical context. Low sensitivity for mild activity changes. Cannot differentiate between active disease and damage in some organ systems.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published academic tool

entries.name: SLICC 2012 SLE Classification Criteria
entries.purpose: Classification criteria for SLE by the Systemic Lupus International Collaborating Clinics (SLICC). Revised to improve sensitivity for early/atypical SLE compared to 1997 ACR criteria.
entries.formula_human:
Classification = ≥4 criteria out of 17 clinical + 6 immunologic, with at least 1 clinical AND at least 1 immunologic criterion
OR biopsy-proven lupus nephritis with positive ANA or anti-dsDNA

bands.meaning: Classified as SLE
Classified as SLE regardless of other criteria count
Does not meet SLICC classification criteria for SLE

citations.text: Petri M, Orbai AM, Alarcón GS, et al. Derivation and validation of the Systemic Lupus International Collaborating Clinics classification criteria for systemic lupus erythematosus. Arthritis Rheum. 2012;64(8):2677-2686. PMID: 22553077

entries.limitations: Classification criteria, not diagnostic — developed for research cohort homogeneity. Requires ANA as entry criterion (positive ANA ≥1:80 on HEp-2 cells or equivalent). Some criteria may overlap (e.g., acute cutaneous lupus with malar rash counted once). Doesn't capture disease activity or severity. Ignores medication-induced lupus. Weight given to each criterion is equal (1 point each) — some criteria may be more specific than others.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published academic tool

entries.name: Pneumonia Severity Index / PORT Score
entries.purpose: Stratifies CAP patients into 5 risk classes for 30-day mortality using 20 variables to guide hospitalization decisions.
entries.formula_human:
PSI = Age_points + Nursing_home(10) + Cancer(30) + Liver(20) + CHF(10) + CVD(10) + Renal(10) + AMS(20) + HR≥125(10) + RR≥30(20) + SBP<90(20) + Temp_extremes(15) + pH<7.35(30) + BUN≥30(20) + Na<130(20) + Glucose≥250(10) + Hct<30(10) + Hypoxemia(10) + Effusion(10).
Age points = age (males) or age − 10 (females). BUN points only counted once (in the BUN≥30 variable OR in the renal disease variable, but BUN≥30 appears as both — verify original scoring rules carefully: in the original, BUN appears as 'renal dysfunction' worth 10 points AND 'BUN≥30 mg/dL' worth 20 points — count both if applicable).

inputs.label: Age (male)
inputs.description: Age in years for male patients

inputs.label: Age (female)
inputs.description: Age in years minus 10 for female patients

inputs.label: Nursing home resident
inputs.description: Resides in nursing home or long-term care facility

inputs.label: Congestive heart failure
inputs.description: History of CHF or reduced EF

inputs.label: Renal disease
inputs.description: BUN ≥30 mg/dL or Cr >1.5 mg/dL (or GFR <60)

bands.range: Class I (score ≤0 for males; ≤0 for females — i.e., age<50 with no comorbidities, vital signs normal)
bands.meaning: Very low risk (<0.6% mortality). Outpatient treatment.
Low risk (0.6–2.8% mortality). Outpatient treatment.
Moderate risk (2.8–8.2% mortality). Consider brief inpatient or ED observation.
High risk (8.2–29.2% mortality). Hospitalize.
Very high risk (29.2–40%+ mortality). Hospitalize, consider ICU.

citations.text: Fine MJ, Auble TE, Yealy DM, et al. A prediction rule to identify low-risk patients with community-acquired pneumonia. N Engl J Med. 1997;336(4):243-250. PMID: 8995086

entries.limitations: Complex (20 variables — not easy at bedside). May overestimate mortality in younger patients and underestimate in frail elderly. Class I requires young age with normal vitals and no comorbidities (exceptions have occurred). Does not capture bilateral multilobar disease severity well. CURB-65 is simpler and has similar discrimination. Internet calculator needed.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use, check for commercial app

entries.name: AO/OTA Comprehensive Classification of Fractures
entries.purpose: Universal alphanumeric classification system for all fractures of the musculoskeletal system. Based on fracture location, morphology, and severity. Used in research, trauma registries, and treatment planning.
entries.formula_human: [MISSING IN SOURCE — descriptive alphanumeric classification; reconstruct from AO/OTA 2007 Compendium, PMID 18277234]

inputs.label: Bone segment
inputs.description: Which bone and segment: 1=Humerus, 2=Radius/Ulna, 3=Femur, 4=Tibia/Fibula, etc. Segment: A=proximal, B=diaphyseal, C=distal

inputs.label: Fracture type
inputs.description: A=Simple (extra-articular for periarticular), B=Wedge/Partial articular, C=Complex (comminuted/articular)
inputs.points_text:
A<lteral, D=Multi-fragmentary spiral
  - B (Wedge): B1=Spiral wedge, B2=Bending wedge, B3=Fragmentary wedge
  - C (Complex): C1=Spiral, C2=Segmental, C3=Irregular

  For periarticular fractures:
  - A: Extra-articular
  - B: Partial articular
  - C: Complete articular (split)**

citations.text: Müller ME, Nazarian S, Koch P, Schatzker J. The Comprehensive Classification of Fractures of Long Bones. Springer-Verlag, 1990; Marsh JL, Slongo TF, Agel J, et al. Fracture and dislocation classification compendium - 2007. J Orthop Trauma. 2007;21(10 Suppl):S1-S133. PMID: 18277234

entries.limitations: Complex system requiring training — steep learning curve. Detailed sub-classifications (3 groups × 3 subgroups × 3 sub-subgroups = 27 categories per segment) may not all influence treatment. Interobserver reliability decreases with increasing sub-classification detail. Primarily descriptive — does not incorporate soft tissue injury, vascular status, or patient factors. Not all classifications influence treatment equally.
entries.copyright: AO Foundation — free for clinical and educational use

entries.name: Oxford Hip Score / Oxford Knee Score
entries.purpose: Patient-reported outcome measures specifically designed to assess function and pain after hip (OHS) or knee (OKS) joint replacement surgery. Validated, short, easy to complete.
entries.formula_human:
OHS/OKS = Sum of 12 items (each 0–4)
Converted to 0–48 scale: 48 - raw score = final score (higher = better)
Or: raw sum (12–60, lower = better — depends on version)

inputs.label: 12 questions
inputs.description: 12 questions assessing pain and function over the past 4 weeks. Each scored 0–4 (best to worst). Examples: pain severity, limping, interference with daily activities, ability to walk, ability to climb stairs, kneeling, night pain, washing/dressing, shopping, walking duration, sudden pain, work limitations.

bands.meaning: Good outcome
Fair/moderate outcome
Poor outcome
Minimum clinically important difference
Score above which patients consider their state acceptable

citations.text: Dawson J, Fitzpatrick R, Carr A, Murray D. Questionnaire on the perceptions of patients about total hip replacement. J Bone Joint Surg Br. 1996;78(2):185-190. PMID: 8666944; Dawson J, et al. J Bone Joint Surg Br. 1998;80(4):677-682 (Oxford Knee Score)

entries.limitations: Designed for arthroplasty patients — less validated in non-surgical populations. Ceiling effect in excellent outcomes. Doesn't capture sports or high-demand activities. Self-reported, subject to recall bias. Score version confusion (raw vs. converted, best-worst vs. worst-best). May not capture all aspects of hip/knee dysfunction (e.g., instability, stiffness). Patient acceptable symptom state (PASS) thresholds vary by population.
entries.copyright: Oxford University Innovation — permission may be required for commercial use, free for clinical/academic use

entries.name: Garden Classification of Femoral Neck Fractures
entries.purpose: Radiographic classification of femoral neck (intracapsular) fractures based on degree of displacement. Guides treatment decisions (internal fixation vs. arthroplasty) and predicts risk of avascular necrosis (AVN) and nonunion.
entries.formula_human:
Garden Type I: Incomplete fracture (valgus impacted)
Garden Type II: Complete fracture without displacement
Garden Type III: Complete fracture with partial displacement (distal fragment externally rotated)
Garden Type IV: Complete fracture with full displacement (fragments not in contact)

inputs.label: Radiographic fracture pattern
inputs.description: AP and lateral radiograph assessment of femoral neck fracture displacement

bands.meaning: Incomplete/valgus impacted — generally stable, good prognosis. Internal fixation (cannulated screws or sliding hip screw). AVN risk ~10%.
Complete but undisplaced — internal fixation. AVN risk ~15%.
Displaced — controversy regarding treatment. Young patients: anatomical reduction + internal fixation. Elderly: hemiarthroplasty or THA. AVN risk ~30%.
Fully displaced — poor prognosis with internal fixation. Elderly: hemiarthroplasty or THA. AVN risk ~40-60%.

citations.text: Garden RS. Low-angle fixation in fractures of the femoral neck. J Bone Joint Surg Br. 1961;43-B:647-663

entries.limitations: Interobserver reliability is moderate — different surgeons may classify the same fracture differently, particularly between types II and III (displacement threshold ambiguous). Garden described 4 types but practical treatment is often binary (undisplaced I-II vs. displaced III-IV). Doesn't capture posterior comminution or basicervical vs. transcervical location. Radiograph quality significantly affects classification accuracy. Does not account for patient age, bone quality, or functional status.

entries.name: Harris Hip Score
entries.purpose: Clinician-administered and patient-reported outcome measure for hip function, widely used to assess outcomes after hip arthroplasty, hip fractures, and hip pathology. One of the most frequently used hip-specific outcome scores.
entries.formula_human:
HHS = Pain (0–44) + Function-Gait (0–33) + Function-Activities (0–14) + Absence of deformity (0–4) + ROM (0–5)
Maximum = 100 points
ROM scored: (actual degrees / normal degrees) × 5

inputs.label: Pain
inputs.options_text: None (44), Slight/occasional (40), Mild (30), Moderate (20), Marked (10), Totally disabled (0)

inputs.label: Function — Activities (14 points max)
inputs.description: Stairs (0–4), Shoes/socks (0–4), Sitting (0–5), Enter public transport (0–1)

inputs.label: Absence of Deformity
inputs.description: Hip flexion contracture <30°, adduction contracture <10°, internal rotation contracture <10°, limb length discrepancy <3.2 cm

inputs.label: Range of Motion
inputs.description: Flexion, abduction, external rotation, internal rotation. Scored as percentage of normal ROM multiplied by 0.05
inputs.options_text: Flexion: 0–145°, Abduction: 0–45°, External rotation: 0–45°, Internal rotation: 0–45°, Adduction: 0–30°

bands.meaning: Excellent outcome
Good outcome
Fair outcome
Poor outcome
Minimum clinically important difference

citations.text: Harris WH. Traumatic arthritis of the hip after dislocation and acetabular fractures: treatment by mold arthroplasty. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 1969;51(4):737-755. PMID: 5783851

entries.limitations: Ceiling effect — many post-THA patients cluster near 100, making discrimination between good outcomes difficult. Pain component (44 points) heavily weighted, which may mask functional limitations. ROM measurement has poor interobserver reliability. Deformity component rarely differentiates (most patients score 4). Original publication doesn't specify all assessment details. Patient-reported version (HHS-PR) is separate and may differ from clinician-administered version. Doesn't capture patient satisfaction or psychological factors.

entries.name: Oswestry Disability Index
entries.purpose: Gold-standard patient-reported outcome measure for low back pain. Assesses functional disability across 10 domains of daily living affected by back pain.
entries.formula_human:
ODI = (Total score from answered sections / Maximum possible score from answered sections) × 100
If all 10 sections completed: ODI = (Sum / 50) × 100
Score expressed as percentage (0–100%)
If sections missed: divide by (number of answered sections × 5)

inputs.label: Section 1: Pain Intensity
inputs.description: Current pain level and effect on daily activities
inputs.options_text: 0 (no pain) to 5 (worst pain, can't do anything)

inputs.label: Section 2: Personal Care
inputs.options_text: 0 (no extra time) to 5 (need help with everything)

inputs.label: Section 9: Traveling
inputs.options_text: 0 (no extra pain) to 5 (can't travel at all)

inputs.label: Section 10: Employment/Homemaking
inputs.description: Ability to work or manage home

bands.meaning: Minimal disability — can cope with most activities
Moderate disability — pain impacts daily activities, may need treatment adjustment
Severe disability — pain significantly limits function
Crippling disability — bed-bound or exaggerating symptoms likely
Bed-bound or inability to function (rare in practice)
Minimum clinically important difference

citations.text: Fairbank JC, Couper J, Davies JB, O'Brien JP. The Oswestry low back pain disability questionnaire. Physiotherapy. 1980;66(8):271-273. PMID: 6450426; Fairbank JC, Pynsent PB. Spine. 2000;25(22):2940-2952 (ODI 2.1a)

entries.limitations: Self-reported — subject to recall bias and subjective interpretation. May be affected by psychological factors (depression, anxiety, fear-avoidance). Some sections (e.g., employment) may not be relevant to retired or unemployed patients. Sexual function section (Section 8 in some versions) frequently left blank. Ceiling effect in very severe disability. Floor effect in mild/early disease. Different versions exist (ODI 1.0, 2.0, 2.1a) with slight differences. ODI measures disability, not impairment — doesn't capture neurological deficits.
entries.copyright: Mapi Research Trust — permission required for research/commercial use; clinical use generally free

entries.name: Fleischner Society Guidelines for Pulmonary Nodules
entries.purpose: Provides management recommendations for incidentally discovered pulmonary nodules on CT (solid, subsolid, and ground-glass).
entries.formula_human:
Clinical decision algorithm (not a numerical score). Categorizes nodules by size, type, and risk to determine follow-up CT timing and need for PET/CT or biopsy. Consult published Fleischner 2017 guidelines for specific pathways.

Simplified: Solid ≤6mm: no follow-up (low risk) or optional CT at 12 months (high risk). Solid 6–8mm: CT at 6–12 months, then consider 18–24 months. Solid >8mm: CT at 3 months, PET/CT, or tissue sampling. Part-solid ≤6mm: no follow-up or CT at 12 months. Part-solid >6mm: CT at 3–6 months. Ground-glass ≤5mm: no follow-up. Ground-glass >5mm: CT at 12 months.

inputs.label: Risk factors
inputs.description: Patient risk factors for malignancy (smoking history, family history, emphysema, upper lobe location, nodule morphology)

bands.meaning: No routine follow-up necessary.
CT at 6–12 months, then at 18–24 months if unchanged.
CT at 3 months, PET-CT, or tissue sampling depending on clinical context.
CT at 3–6 months. If solid component ≥6mm and persists, consider biopsy.

citations.text: MacMahon H, Naidich DP, Goo JM, et al. Guidelines for management of incidental pulmonary nodules detected on CT images: from the Fleischner Society 2017. Radiology. 2017;284(1):228-243. PMID: 28240562

entries.limitations: Guidelines, not a validated numerical score. Subject to interpretation and clinical judgment. 2017 revision changed recommendations significantly from 2005 version. Does not fully account for ground-glass component growth rate. Different from Lung-RADS (screening context). Patient preference and comorbidity should influence decisions.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published academic guideline

entries.name: Gustilo-Anderson Classification of Open Fractures
entries.purpose: Classification of open (compound) fractures based on wound size, soft tissue injury, contamination, and fracture pattern. Guides antibiotic selection, surgical debridement urgency, and predicts infection risk.
entries.formula_human:
Type I: Wound <1 cm, minimal soft tissue injury, clean, low-energy fracture
Type II: Wound 1–10 cm, moderate soft tissue damage, moderate contamination
Type IIIA: Wound >10 cm, extensive soft tissue damage but adequate bone coverage (may be closed), high-energy mechanism, segmental/comminuted fracture
Type IIIB: Wound >10 cm, extensive soft tissue loss with periosteal stripping, bone exposed, requires flap coverage
Type IIIC: Any open fracture with arterial injury requiring repair

inputs.label: Wound size
inputs.description: Size of the open wound communicating with the fracture

inputs.label: Soft tissue damage
inputs.description: Degree of soft tissue injury, periosteal stripping, and muscle damage

inputs.label: Contamination
inputs.description: Degree of contamination with dirt, debris, foreign bodies

bands.meaning: Infection risk ~2%. Cefazolin (first-gen cephalosporin). Debridement and irrigation, primary closure possible.
Infection risk ~5%. Cefazolin. Debridement, irrigation, delayed primary closure.
Infection risk ~10%. Cefazolin + aminoglycoside. Aggressive debridement, soft tissue coverage within 72 hours.
Infection risk ~20–50%. Cefazolin + aminoglycoside. Aggressive debridement, requires flap coverage (muscle or rotational flap).
Infection risk ~25–50%, amputation risk ~50%. Cefazolin + aminoglycoside + penicillin (or clindamycin for clostridial coverage). Vascular repair required. High amputation rate.

citations.text: Gustilo RB, Anderson JT. Prevention of infection in the treatment of 1,025 open fractures of long bones. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 1976;58(4):453-458. PMID: 773941; Gustilo RB, Mendoza RM, Williams DN. Problems in the management of type III (severe) open fractures. J Trauma. 1984;24(8):742-746. PMID: 64

entries.limitations: Classification typically performed in operating room (final determination during surgery, not in ED). Interobserver reliability moderate (particularly II vs. IIIA, and IIIA vs. IIIB). Does not account for mechanism of injury, contamination time, or patient factors (diabetes, immunosuppression). Wound size alone doesn't capture underlying muscle/soft tissue viability. Retrograde contamination (through muscle) may be underestimated. Mangled Extremity Severity Score (MESS) may be more useful for amputation decisions in IIIC injuries. Does not guide fixation method.

entries.name: BOVA Score for PE
entries.purpose: Risk stratifies normotensive PE patients for early PE-related complications (death, hemodynamic collapse, or recurrent PE within 30 days).
entries.formula_human: BOVA = HR_100-109(1) + HR≥110(2) + SBP_90-100(2) + RV_dysfunction(2) + Troponin_elevated(2)

inputs.label: Heart rate
inputs.options_text: 1 point if HR 100–109; 2 points if HR ≥110

inputs.label: SBP 90–100 mmHg
inputs.description: Systolic BP between 90 and 100 (not true hypotension)

inputs.label: Right ventricular dysfunction
inputs.description: RV dilation/hypokinesis on echocardiography or RV/LV ratio >0.9 on CTPA

bands.meaning: Low risk of 30-day PE complications (~3%). Consider early discharge or outpatient management.
Intermediate risk (~7%). Close monitoring, consider HDU.
High risk (~17%). Monitor in HDU/ICU setting. Consider reperfusion therapy if deterioration.

citations.text: Bova C, Sanchez O, Prandoni P, et al. Identification of intermediate-risk patients with acute symptomatic pulmonary embolism. Eur Respir J. 2014;44(3):694-703. PMID: 24925905

entries.limitations: Requires echo or CTPA (imaging modality-dependent). Does not include renal function, BNP, or biomarkers beyond troponin. Original derivation in patients already enrolled in an RCT (selected population). Stage III patients still need clinical judgment for escalation. Limited external validation in Asian and African populations.

entries.name: European Society of Cardiology Risk Stratification for PE (2019)
entries.purpose: Stepwise algorithm integrating clinical risk (sPESI), cardiac biomarkers (troponin, BNP), and imaging (RV dysfunction) to classify PE into low, intermediate-low, intermediate-high, and high risk.
entries.formula_human:
Stepwise algorithm:
1. Hemodynamically unstable = High risk → reperfusion (systemic thrombolysis/surgery/catheter-directed therapy)
2. Hemodynamically stable: compute sPESI. sPESI = 0 = low risk → consider early discharge/home treatment. sPESI ≥1 = intermediate risk → check biomarkers and imaging.
3. Intermediate risk: Both biomarkers negative = intermediate-low risk → consider early discharge. Biomarker(s) positive = intermediate-high risk → monitor closely in HDU.
4. RV dysfunction + elevated biomarkers = intermediate-high risk.

inputs.label: sPESI score
inputs.description: Simplified Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index (clinical risk)

bands.meaning: Immediate reperfusion therapy. Mortality >25%.
Monitor in HDU. Consider escalation if deterioration. Mortality ~5–10%.

bands.range: Intermediate-low (sPESI ≥1 + normal biomarkers OR negative imaging)
bands.meaning: Hospital ward monitoring. Can consider early discharge if stable.
Outpatient management or early discharge. Mortality <1%.

citations.text: Konstantinides SV, Meyer G, Becattini C, et al. 2019 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism. Eur Heart J. 2020;41(4):543-603. PMID: 31504429

entries.limitations: Algorithm, not a simple numerical score. Requires multiple steps and data points. Biomarker thresholds vary by assay. RV imaging assessment varies by modality and reader. Hemodynamic criteria may be difficult to capture precisely (sustained hypotension vs transient). Not all intermediate-high risk patients need reperfusion — clinical judgment essential.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published academic guideline

entries.name: Kellgren-Lawrence Grading Scale for Osteoarthritis
entries.purpose: Radiographic grading system for osteoarthritis severity on plain radiographs. Most widely used system for classifying knee, hip, and hand OA in research and epidemiological studies.
entries.formula_human:
Grade 0: No radiographic features of OA
Grade 1: Doubtful JSN, possible osteophytic lipping
Grade 2: Definite osteophytes, possible JSN
Grade 3: Moderate osteophytes, definite JSN, some sclerosis, possible bone deformity
Grade 4: Large osteophytes, marked JSN, severe sclerosis, definite bone deformity

inputs.label: Radiographic features
inputs.description: AP weight-bearing radiograph assessment of joint space narrowing, osteophyte formation, subchondral sclerosis, and bone deformity

bands.meaning: No osteoarthritis
Doubtful OA — possible early changes
Mild OA — definite osteophytes, minimal JSN
Moderate OA — definite JSN, osteophytes, sclerosis
Severe OA — near bone-on-bone, large osteophytes, deformity

citations.text: Kellgren JH, Lawrence JS. Radiological assessment of osteo-arthrosis. Ann Rheum Dis. 1957;16(4):494-502. PMID: 13498604

entries.limitations: Interobserver reliability moderate (kappa ~0.5–0.7). Grade 2 (definite osteophytes but 'possible JSN') is particularly problematic — combines patients with osteophytes-only and those with JSN. Does not capture soft tissue, cartilage, or meniscal pathology (MRI needed). Weight-bearing status and positioning affect JSN. Grading scale is ordinal — intervals between grades are not equal. Doesn't correlate well with symptoms (radiographic OA common in asymptomatic patients). Flattening of scale at severe end — all severe OA grouped as Grade 4.

entries.name: Thoracolumbar Injury Classification and Severity Score
entries.purpose: Decision support tool for management of thoracolumbar (T11–L2) spinal injuries. Helps determine operative vs. non-operative treatment based on morphology, neurological status, and posterior ligamentous complex integrity.
entries.formula_human:
TLICS = Morphology (1–4) + Neurological status (0–3) + PLC (0–3)
Total range: 1–10 (minimum possible is 1 because any injury has at least compression morphology)

inputs.label: Neurological status
inputs.description: ASIA grade of spinal cord/conus/cauda equina injury
inputs.options_text: Intact=0, Nerve root=2, Incomplete cord/conus=3, Complete cord/conus=2, Cauda equina=3

inputs.label: Posterior Ligamentous Complex (PLC)
inputs.description: Integrity of supraspinous ligament, interspinous ligament, ligamentum flavum, facet capsules

bands.meaning: Non-operative treatment (bracing, observation)
Non-operative or operative (surgeon discretion, patient factors)
Operative treatment (surgical stabilization ± decompression)

citations.text: Vaccaro AR, Lehman RA Jr, Hurlbert RJ, et al. A new classification of thoracolumbar injuries: the importance of injury morphology, the integrity of the posterior ligamentous complex, and neurologic status. Spine. 2005;30(20):2325-2333. PMID: 16227897

entries.limitations: Validated primarily for T11-L2 injuries — may not apply equally to thoracic (T1-T10) or lumbar (L3-L5) fractures. PLC integrity assessment can be difficult on CT (MRI preferred). Morphology categorization can be ambiguous for burst + distraction combination injuries. Doesn't account for patient age, bone quality (osteoporosis), or mechanism. Translation/rotation and distraction are specific and may be missed on initial imaging. Doesn't guide specific surgical approach (anterior vs. posterior vs. combined). Some authors advocate for sub-classifications not captured by TLICS.
entries.copyright: free for clinical use — published academic tool

entries.name: Hamilton Depression Rating Scale
entries.purpose: Clinician-administered depression severity rating scale. Gold-standard clinician-rated measure for depression severity in clinical trials. Most extensively validated depression rating scale in psychopharmacology research.
entries.formula_human:
HAM-D17 = Sum of Q1–Q17 (maximum 52)
HAM-D21 = Includes 4 additional items (diurnal variation, depersonalization, paranoid symptoms, obsessional symptoms) — maximum 62, but severity usually based on 17-item score
HAM-D6 (6-item version): Q1 + Q2 + Q7 + Q8 + Q10 + Q13 (maximum 22) — recommended for sensitive measurement in trials

inputs.label: Q1: Depressed mood
inputs.options_text: 0=Absent, 1=These feelings only on questioning, 2=Reported spontaneously, 3=Communicated non-verbally (facial expression, posture, voice, tears), 4=Patient reports virtually only these feelings

inputs.label: Q2: Feelings of guilt
inputs.description: Self-blame, guilt, ideas of sin, delusions of guilt

inputs.label: Q8: Psychomotor retardation
inputs.description: Slowness of thought/speech, decreased motor activity

inputs.label: Q13: Somatic symptoms — general
inputs.description: Heaviness in limbs, back, head; diffuse pain

bands.meaning: Normal / Remission
Mild depression
Moderate depression
Severe depression
Very severe depression
≥50% reduction from baseline score
HAM-D17 ≤7

citations.text: Hamilton M. A rating scale for depression. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry. 1960;23:56-62. PMID: 14399272

entries.limitations: Clinician-rated — requires trained assessor, 15–20 minutes to administer. Inter-rater reliability can vary without standardized training. Some items (psychomotor retardation, insight) may be difficult to assess reliably. Somatic items may reflect medical illness rather than depression. Anxiety items mixed with depression items — may conflate anxiety with depression severity. Different versions (17, 21, 6-item) complicate cross-study comparison. Weight loss item may not be relevant in modern populations. Sexual dysfunction item often omitted or scored inconsistently. Newer scales (MADRS, QIDS) may be more sensitive to change.

entries.name: Clinical Global Impression
entries.purpose: Brief clinician-rated global assessment of psychiatric illness severity (CGI-S) and change from baseline (CGI-I). Widely used in psychiatric clinical trials as a reference standard for measuring treatment response.
entries.formula_human:
CGI-S: Single-item clinician rating 1–7
CGI-I: Single-item clinician rating 1–7

Clinical utility index: CGI-S × CGI-I (used in some analyses)
Response commonly defined as CGI-I ≤2 (much or very much improved)

inputs.label: CGI-Severity (CGI-S)
